title: NFL Week 2 odds, picks: Jets continue to stay frisky, while Baker Mayfield torches former Browns team
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 2 schedule, plus five locks against the spread
full_text:
We are off and running in the 2026 regular season and are coming off an opening weekend where we escaped Week 1 with a stellar record on the whole. For the slate, I went 13-3 on straight-up picks and 9-7 ATS. That was good for the best among CBS Sports experts straight up and tied for second against the spread.
The only unfortunate aspect of my weekend was that some of the locks within my five Locks of the Week were faulty. I was 2-3 ATS on my five best bets, with the Jets ' upset win in Nashville and Jacksonville's throttling of the Browns as the lone covers. The Houston Texans nearly swung the day for us as they had the Buffalo Bills on the ropes, but Josh Allen was simply too much to slay, so we'll look to keep the overall momentum rolling in Week 2 while cleaning things up with my locks.
As we turn our attention to the upcoming slate, we're somewhat going back to the well with a couple of teams, attacking the Browns and buying the Jets with the points.
It seems like Cooper Rush is going to get another start for Atlanta, so we'll gladly fade him after a rough debut with the Falcons in Week 1. Out of every starting quarterback that took the field in Week 1, no one has a worse passer rating than Rush (54.9). There was essentially no vertical passing game as Rush averaged just 3.5 air yards per attempt (31st among QBs). Despite that, he still had an off-target rate of 13.6% (22nd). So, while the Panthers ' defense was pantsed by the Bears in Week 1 to the tune of 59 points allowed, they won't face nearly the firepower under center as they did when squaring up against Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams . Meanwhile, lost in the Bears lighting it up, Bryce Young put together a strong effort, with his .29 EPA per dropback ranking sixth-highest among all quarterbacks in Week 1. The Panthers QB also owns a 4-1 SU and ATS record when he starts against Atlanta.
Projected score: Panthers 24, Falcons 20 The pick: Panthers -1
Listen, this might be the last time in our lives that we'll be able to bet against Deshaun Watson , so we HAVE to take this opportunity while it's still there. The Browns QB looked about as you'd expect him to look in the opening loss to Jacksonville. He didn't seem comfortable in the pocket at all, tossed an interception on his opening possession, and nearly had two more turnovers. Dating to before his Achilles injuries, Watson is 0-6 SU and 1-5 ATS over his last six starts. Meanwhile, the Browns are 1-10 ATS in their last 11 road games when they are a dog of 6-plus points.
While Watson won't provide much resistance for the Bucs defense, old friend Baker Mayfield is likely chomping at the bit to square off against his former team. This will be just the second game against Cleveland since he was traded in the summer of 2022. Mayfield lost his first matchup against the Browns while a member of the Panthers, but has since revitalized his career in Tampa and will likely be looking to run it up with his college of skill-position players. The Bucs are 3-0 SU in home openers with Mayfield.
Projected score: Buccaneers 30, Browns 13 The pick: Buccaneers -8.5
It's hard to call a Week 2 matchup a kitchen-sink game or any team, but I sort of feel that way with the Patriots. They completely collapsed in the fourth quarter and lost a winnable game against the Seahawks in the season opener. After this game on Sunday, they'll begin a two-week road trip where they'll head to Jacksonville and Buffalo. The Patriots shouldn't expect to be favored in either of those matchups, so if they drop this home opener to Pittsburgh, they're looking down the barrel of a potential 0-4 start.
While they did lose A.J. Brown (ankle) to injury, I think New England should be able to outpace the Steelers ' offense. Aaron Rodgers was tied for the fourth-worst EPA per dropback in the NFL in Week 1 as the Pittsburgh offense averaged just 4.1 yards per play against Atlanta. The Patriots boast a far better defense than the Falcons, with All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez and a pass rush that was surprisingly disruptive in Week 1.
Remember, the Steelers went into Foxborough in Week 3 last year and pulled out a 21-14 win. In that loss, the Patriots turned the ball over five (!) times. Mike Vrabel will almost certainly remind them of that game and push them to right the wrong here.
Drake Maye is also 6-0 SU and 5-1 ATS as a 3-plus point favorite at home in his career.
Projected score: Patriots 24, Steelers 17 The pick: Patriots -5.5
Can you believe it? We're backing the Jets in back-to-back weeks! Did we slip into the Twilight Zone or something? Unlike last week, however, we're not taking them to pull off the outright win (although I was tempted). Instead, we're looking for them to merely cover as they host the Packers in the home opener. While it was against Tennessee, New York looked far improved from last year's squad. Specifically, they got stable quarterback play from Geno Smith , who was the only quarterback in the entire Week 1 slate to not have an off-target throw. Meanwhile, the defense showed signs of life, specifically with No. 2 overall pick David Bailey tallying a sack in his debut.
As we look at Green Bay, I just don't have a lot of faith in the Packers right now as a road favorite. They collapsed against the Vikings , and Jordan Love did not look good in the process. In stark contrast to Smith, Love's off-target rate was the highest among every quarterback in Week 1 (23.8%). On top of throwing an interception against Minnesota, the Vikings dropped two others, so it was nearly an even more disastrous day for the Packers' quarterback.
They may win because they have a smidge more talent, but it'll be within the number.
Projected score: Packers 24, Jets 21 The pick: Jets +3.5
Maybe it's a trap, but I don't care. I'll fade Cam Ward and the Titans until they give me a reason not to. Ward ranked 26th in the league in Week 1 in EPA per dropback as well as off-target rate in a loss to New York at home. He was sacked three times in the opener, and will now face an Eagles front that will continue to apply pressure. Tennessee scored just 10 points in Week 1, which was the fewest point total in a season opener at home in franchise history. It's hard to imagine this unit suddenly finding success against a superior defense that took it to them on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Breece Hall averaged 4.6 yards per carry while piling up 102 yards and a touchdown on the ground against Robert Saleh's defense in Week 1, and I expect Saquon Barkley to carry the baton with a similar showing in Week 2. This should be a double-digit win by Philadelphia.

title: Cowboys' Caleb Downs explains why historically bad Week 1 defense is 'very fixable'
summary: Dallas produced one of the NFL's worst defensive performances since the start of 2025, but its first-round rookie says the mistakes are correctable
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys entered the 2026 season full of hope for a new era of defense. After firing defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus , Dallas hired 34-year-old, longtime Vic Fangio staffer Christian Parker, and also revamped its roster. Nearly half, 46.2%, per the Dallas Morning News , of the snaps taken on Dallas' defense in 2025 are no longer on the team.
However, the on-field performance was more of the same in a 28-20 road loss to the New York Giants . New York converted 82% of its third downs, with one of those stops being the game-ending knee down. That figure was New York's best third-down conversion rate in a single game since 1978.
Based on defensive expected points added (EPA)/ per drive in TruMedia, the Cowboys delivered the worst effort by any team in Week 1, and it was worse than all of their defensive games last year. Of the 576 defensive performances since the start of the 2025 season, it ranked 574th. Their seven defensive possessions yielded four touchdowns, one takeaway via fumble recovery, a punt and the game ending.
So how did the Cowboys' latest stinker happen after all that change?
"To lose contain on a guy like Jaxson (Dart) that is that athletic, and it was multiple guys at multiple times. ... We have Jayden [Daniels and the Washington Commanders ] this week, and then you guys have maybe heard of Lamar Jackson [and the Baltimore Ravens ] coming in a couple weeks. So we certainly have to get better with our discipline," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "The other thing that I will say, looking at the game, that we need to be better in is our communication on defense. ... Communication is two parts. It's the person that gives [the call], and the person that receives it has to acknowledge it. Some of the things that we did in the red zone late where we didn't have anybody accounting for [running back Devin] Singletary, who is a pretty dynamic player. Those were communication issues. That can't happen because those are self-inflicted wounds that get you beat."
In an otherwise forgettable night, the debut of 11th overall pick Caleb Downs was a positive one. The ex-Ohio State safety racked up seven total tackles, one sack and one forced fumble. Dart targeted Downs once and completed a pass for five yards on the rookie's 29 coverage snaps, per TruMedia. In college, Downs was relied on to help with on-field communication, and he didn't put the blame on Parker, a first-time defensive coordinator, not getting the call in fast enough.
"I think it's just first-game execution honestly," Downs told CBS Sports related to Week 1 communication. "I don't necessarily think it's not getting a call or anything like that. I think it's just making sure we're detailed in our work and doing our jobs at the highest level more so than anything else. Just executing our job is the biggest thing."
While Schottenheimer had plenty to gripe about with his defense after Week 1, Downs wasn't one of them. He's already in love with his ability to harass the quarterback, something he did with a strip sack of Dart with 2:36 left in the first half. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, New York jumped on the football as it did on three of the four fumbles Dallas forced.
"I think Caleb played really, really well," Schottenheimer said. "Jaxson Dart never saw him on the blitz. He gets a free run and the ball goes spiraling through the air, and the 320-pound guard [Jon Runyan Jr.] catches it and rumbles for five yards. That's kind of how the night went for us. I think that's one of the positives of what we did on defense: we attacked the ball. We had four forced fumbles. ... Caleb is a guy that can move around, but we like him down near the line of scrimmage."
Caleb Downs with a HUGE hit on Jaxson Dart 😤 DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6x4h1EbLxb
Early in the game, Downs functioned as a safety in Dallas' base defense and then closer to the line as a nickel corner/hybrid linebacker near the line of scrimmage in sub-packages. That's how former NFL coach Matt Patricia, now Ohio State's defensive coordinator, used him as a chess piece up and down the field.
"Yeah, a lot similar to college, being able to move around," Downs said. "So being able to play, whether it's nickel, being able to play safety and then third down, being able to play dime as well. I think just being able to make plays wherever you're at, that's the biggest thing. So I have confidence in my ability, and that's what I'm going to go out and do."
Dallas' plan at deep safety with Malik Hooker sidelined for what they hope is only a couple of weeks with a forearm fracture is to have seven-year veteran P.J. Locke fill in at that spot so that Downs can be freed up to play more of his hybrid role along the line of scrimmage.
"I think I can play the run game really well. Play the pass game, whatever it is, whether it's man or dropping zones," Downs said. "I'm an extra corner or extra linebacker. Whatever you need."
The Cowboys trust Downs to handle whatever they throw at him because of the way he attacks watching film and preparing himself to play each and every week.
"Man, [I] probably sound like a broken record. The way he prepares, the way he practices is not like, I don't want to say any. It's not like most rookies I've been around. It's different. There's a different mindset," Schottenheimer said entering Week 1. "There's a different competitive fire in this kid. He craves coaching. He cannot get coached enough. And I think at the end of the day, that's why he's such a good player. I think you look at him and just the way he's always played the game, he plays it with instincts. ... He works his butt off at studying the X and the O's part of it. So unique young man, very special talent."
Downs and Parker are the two new faces of the Cowboys' defense, along with four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . They walked off the bus together at MetLife Stadium Sunday night, and Downs sees symmetry in their career trajectories.
"We're going through the same journey at the same time," Downs said. "It's my first season, and it's his first season calling the plays and being the defensive coordinator. So I think there's a lot of similarities there, and we're just trying to succeed at what we do, and that's the biggest thing."
After their deflating primetime defeat, Parker pulled Downs aside immediately after landing back home to talk about what needs to change entering Week 2 against the Washington Commanders.
"When we got off the plane for a couple minutes, just talking about some of the things we needed to correct for this coming week and really just basic defense," Downs said. "How we need to adjust and do certain things. Just talking about this coming week and how we're going to prepare a little bit differently."
Downs' tone when describing that chat oozed with confidence. Why? Because there is a belief that the issue that plagued them in Week 1 can be course-corrected shortly.
"Everything that we made mistakes on is very fixable," Downs said. "Defense is pretty simple. At the end of the day, it's not like we're playing rocket science. It's just we got to do our jobs when we're on the field, and that's the biggest thing."
Schottenheimer had a similarly productive chat both after the game and on Monday back home at The Star, Dallas' team facility. He came away from that conversation feeling convinced he made the right choice to hire Parker.
"He and I were on the same page with that, which is a good thing," Schottenheimer said. "And then this morning he was amazing with the staff and having hard conversations and real conversations. "And this is not just the players, this is us as a staff. That's a leader. That's a leader of men. ... I'm around him every day. ... I have no question Christian Parker is the right guy for this job. He's an outstanding coach. He will learn from this, just like our young players are going to learn from this. We're going to play our young players this…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Ranking the five best 2026 NFL Draft classes after Week 1: Chiefs rookies shine brightest
summary: These five teams' rookies produced the most during Week 1 of the NFL season
full_text:
They say you can't evaluate a draft class until after three seasons. Unfortunately, it's 2026, and no one has that much patience anymore, so how about we do it after one week? As always, the caveat is: this is one game. This is not the end-all, be-all. But with most things, it's better to look good early on than bad.
These are the top-five draft classes after the first week of the season.
Highlight: Peter Woods rare athleticism Lowlight: Mansoor Delane's shoulder injury
There were whispers about Brett Veach having another masterclass draft last April, and they've now turned into roars. Peter Woods was already making special plays as a pass-rusher and in the run game. He also chased down a running back from behind on a flat route. His addition will allow Steve Spagnuolo to be more measured with how many snaps they give to 32-year-old Chris Jones going forward.
Peter Woods with one of the most athletic recoveries vs. a double team you'll ever see from a DT pic.twitter.com/CdMDIiJ7CB
Top-10 corner Mansoor Delane unfortunately left the game after three snaps with a shoulder injury, but the injury occurred on a play where he ran a dig route for Courtland Sutton and picked off a pass.
Mansoor Delane Every Snap in NFL Debut vs Broncos pic.twitter.com/0rrFJYFzhS
Then there was second-round edge rusher R Mason Thomas , who had a crucial sack in a two-minute drill before the half, where he teleported underneath Mike McGlinchey with a spin move.
Rookie R Mason Thomas with the spin move right into a sack 💪 DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mVVJ07s2NB
Oh, and then Day 3 running back Emmett Johnson made as many people miss on two catches Monday night (six) as Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt on 37 combined catches last season. It's hard to swing and hit harder than the Chiefs did with their first three picks, at least in Monday night's win.
Highlight: Austin Barber locking down right guard Lowlight: KC Concepcion's ball security
Lost in the ugliness of the Browns quarterback position was the fact that the Browns look like they've clocked yet another impressive draft haul. The Browns have four starters on offense from the 2026 draft class in Spencer Fano , Austin Barber, KC Concepcion, and Denzel Boston , with Emmanuel McNeil-Warren filling in for 14 snaps defensively. While they weren't as obviously slam dunks as the Chiefs, there were big-time flashes for all of the offensive starters.
Concepcion, in particular, already looks like the Browns' best playmaker. His ability to separate was on full display.
KC Concepcion consistently shows strength & fluidity when running routes. Being able to stem inside, get vertical to the proper depth, and roll into this deep sail route all while a defender on the hip isn’t easy. pic.twitter.com/rdEsYTGOJi
While he didn't have any drops that he was known for in college, Concepcion did have an ugly fumble, which was also a problem for him in school, with four fumbles on 185 career receptions.
The most surprising standout was third-rounder Barber. A career tackle at Florida, Barber kicked inside and flipped to the right side for the Browns. He was incredibly clean for a rookie in his first career start. PFF had him as the highest-graded rookie offensive lineman of the week. While there were more concerns on tape than that grade may suggest, Barber looked like he'll be a long-term starter at the position for Cleveland.
Highlight: Vega Ioane's run game dominance Lowlight: Zion Young's 12 forgettable snaps
The Ravens are the only team on this list that didn't have multiple first-rounders. That didn't stop them from getting a big impact from their rookie class, however. The big reason why is first-rounder Vega Ioane. He was the single best rookie I saw on tape in Week 1. He was dominant in the run game at right guard against the Colts , and while there was a trio of reps he'd want back in pass protection, there were others where he paved the way for Lamar Jackson's scrambles. Considering the state of the Ravens' right guard position a year ago, this draft pick could not have had better early returns.
Vega Ioane was the closest thing I saw to a Pro-Bowler in the rookie class Week 1. A few reps he'd want back in pass pro, but sheer dominance otherwise pic.twitter.com/2cau8PLgNY
The Ravens also got meaningful contributions from third-round receiver Ja'Kobi Lane and fourth-round tight end Matthew Hibner , who played 27 and 23 snaps, respectively. Hibner looked like a very capable TE2, while Lane looked like he'll be a red zone favorite for Lamar Jackson. Lane saw three targets inside the opposing 20-yard line, with one touchdown called back by a penalty.
Highlight: Most rookie starters in the NFL Lowlight: Most rookie starters shouldn't have been starting
No team in the NFL hit reset harder this season than the Miami Dolphins . All told, they had 368 of a possible 1,353 snaps Sunday (27.2%) come from rookies - the most in the NFL. Given that, they have every reason to be elated about what they saw Sunday. Kadyn Proctor was the biggest standout with some truly elite reps in the run game. His power for a 21-year-old is special and translated vs. grown men.
Proctor with a couple pancakes & a knockdown on the 2nd level. Solid debut. Anchor looked pretty strong. Got slipped once across his face against a wide alignment. Another favorable matchup next week against SF's IDL. pic.twitter.com/eF0cvfGBX4
While I think Dolphins' other first-rounder Chris Johnson will be a fine player in time, he had an up-and-down Week 1 with a couple of pass breakups, but a couple of big plays as well. I felt similarly about second-round linebacker Jacob Rodriguez as well. While he struggled to get off the blocks consistently, you saw the play speed flash in space on numerous occasions.
The final rookie worth a mention was third-round receiver Caleb Douglas , who led all rookies with five catches for 94 yards Sunday. In a very underpowered receiving room, Douglas played with a comfort level well beyond that of a rookie.
Dolphins rookie WR Caleb Douglas moved me in week 1. Feed him more targets pic.twitter.com/nm72ms8EJ1
Highlight: Francis Mauigoa's stout pass pro Lowlight: Colton Hood only sees six snaps
Giants fans may see this as a slight, but to me, they check in fifth because I'd expect the only team with two top-10 picks to get an impact out of its rookie class. Arvell Reese was an obvious upgrade for their run defense, while Francis Mauigoa solidified their right guard spot.
There were reps from both, where you saw the high-end talent, but both looked like rookies at times, too.
Wake up with rookie Guard #65 Francis Mauigoa pic.twitter.com/VcNdfBNCCO
The cherry on top of this draft class is third-rounder Malachi Fields , who's already playing a very important role for Matt Nagy's offense. That is doing the dirty work. Fields looks like he'll be a value add in the run game with his ability to dig out box defenders from reduced splits.
Malachi Fields blocking pic.twitter.com/nXtfKRaPFi
author: Mike Renner

title: Predicting the entire NFL playoff bracket after Week 1, including a surprise Super Bowl winner
summary: A wild opening week reshaped our projected playoff bracket, with the Patriots missing out
full_text:
It might sound crazy to try and predict the entire NFL playoff field after just one week of action, but we specialize in crazy.
Week 1 turned the NFL upside down, and you can mostly blame the two teams in Los Angeles for that. The Rams were the Super Bowl favorite going into the season, but right now, it's hard to  envision them even winning their division after they got blasted 27-7 by the 49ers in Australia. And then we have the Chargers . They usually wait until the playoffs to let their fan base down, but this year, they did it in Week 1 with a stunning 26-14 loss to the Cardinals .
As if that's not enough, EVERY team in the NFC South is 0-1, making that possibly the most unpredictable division in the NFL this year. Actually, I take that back; nothing is unpredictable for us here, and that's because we have our resident analytics expert, Stephen Oh, who simulated the rest of the season to see how things will end up playing out. For those of you who are not familiar with Oh's work, let me just say this: If AI was human, it would be Oh.
They say don't overreact to Week 1, but our simulation has run the numbers and reacted accordingly. With that in mind, let's get to the projections.
Before the season started, the Chiefs were kind of a question mark, but that's not the case anymore after their dominant 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday night. Our projection model is now feeling confident that the AFC West will go through Kansas City this year.
If this projection holds up, that means we'll have three new playoff teams in the AFC with the Ravens, Bengals and Chiefs getting in. The biggest surprise here might be that the reigning AFC champion Patriots are projected to miss the postseason.
In the NFC, the computer has three teams in the NFC West making the playoffs. Before the season started, our computer surprisingly projected the Seahawks to win the NFC West over the Rams, which looks like a smart pick right now after the way Week 1 played out. Despite their ugly loss in Week 1, the Rams are still projected to make the playoffs, but just barely. Oh, and did I mention that we have a surprise winner coming out of the NFC South? Because we have a surprise winner coming out of the NFC South.
It's almost impossible to predict who will win the NFC South, but the computer likes Atlanta. The Falcons lost to the Steelers 20-13 in Week 1, but it's a game they certainly could have won if they hadn't been forced to start a third-string QB and didn't miss two field goals.
In the NFC North, the Bears' 59-point outburst wasn't enough to put them at the top of the division. The computer still thinks the Lions are in the driver's seat.
Now that we know who's in the playoffs, let's see who's going to make it to Super Bowl LXI.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
Things are getting interesting. We're down to four teams, and two of them -- the Bills and Lions -- have never won a Super Bowl.
If our projection is correct, we're going to be getting a battle of the birds in the Super Bowl.
NOTE: The Seahawks have said that Sam Darnold's injury isn't serious, so the computer is assuming that Darnold will be out for a short period of time. If it turns into a longer absence, that could certainly change our projections.
author: John Breech

title: Prisco's NFL Week 2 Power Rankings: Rams and Cowboys get a wake-up call, 49ers on the rise
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 2 Power Rankings, including the Bears, Giants and Cardinals moving up
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are done.
The Carolina Panthers ' defense is awful.
The Chicago Bears will break the single-season scoring record.
The Houston Texans ' vaunted defense is now a sieve.
Same for the Denver Broncos .
The Dallas Cowboys are toast.
The Green Bay Packers won't ever hold a lead.
On and on it goes. The Week 1 overreaction bucket is full. Don't be guilty of buying into any of it.
Be more like NFL coaches talking to their teams today: It's just one week. Move on.
Week 1 is full of teases over the years. Remember when the Las Vegas Raiders went to Foxborough and beat the New England Patriots in Week 1 last year. All the Pats did was get to the Super Bowl , while the Raiders were a season-long disaster in 2025.
So don't fall victim to the overreactions.
I took that into account when doing my Week 2 Power Rankings. The Seattle Seahawks stay in the top spot after beating the Patriots to open the season, while the 49ers have moved up after blowing out the Rams. The Rams fall -- but not too far.
That doesn't mean there aren't changes. How can the Los Angeles Chargers not fall after losing at home to the Arizona Cardinals ? The Dallas Cowboys looked terrible on defense Sunday night in losing to the Giants , so they drop a few.
I just want to be cautious that one week won't greatly impact my rankings. One thing that didn't change is Miami in the bottom spot. The Dolphins didn't look good in their loss to the Raiders, but the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans have the look of teams that will challenge Miami all year long for the cellar.
Then again, it's just one week.

summary: The Arizona Cardinals special teams made the play that altered the game more than any other in Sunday’s win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Simi Fehoko blocked a Chargers punt in a 16-14 game early in the fourth quarter. That lead to the Cardinals finally finding paydirt again, and extending their lead to double digits. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Simi Fehoko #80 of the Arizona Cardinals blocks a punt attempt by JK Scott #16 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals special teams made the play that altered the game more than any other in Sunday’s win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Simi Fehoko blocked a Chargers punt in a 16-14 game early in the fourth quarter. SIMI FEHOKO THE MAN YOU ARE 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/ysT2sORxwW — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 13, 2026 That lead to the Cardinals finally finding paydirt again, and extending their lead to double digits. For that, Fehoko was recognized as the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week. This is Fehoko’s first career selection as Special Teams Player of the Week and the first “Special Teams Player of the Week” for the Cardinals since Blake Gillikin in 2024 (Week 9). Fehoko made his mark on special teams in the Cardinals victory last Sunday. He was the first – and only – NFL player to block a punt in Week 1. It was Fehoko’s first career blocked kick, the first blocked punt for the Cardinals since 12/20/20 vs. Philadelphia and the first time the Chargers had a punt blocked since 11/21/21 vs. Pittsburgh. After the Arizona defense forced a three-and-out early in the fourth quarter, the Chargers punted from their own 19-yard line when Fehoko broke through the middle of the L.A. protection to block the kick. The Cardinals took possession at the LAC three-yard line and two plays later, QB Jacoby Brissett hit TE Trey McBride on a three-yard TD pass to give Arizona a 23-14 lead with 11:44 remaining. Fehoko finished Sunday’s game with the blocked punt and two tackles on special teams. Congrats to Fehoko.

title: Falcons’ starting QB for Sunday vs. Panthers still undecided
summary: The Falcons’ quarterback situation seems even murkier after head coach Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media on Wednesday. But Stefanski said he isn’t frustrated. “We want to be able to win and play well regardless of who’s in,” Stefanski said, and saying that the frustration actually comes from losing and falling short on the field. […]
full_text: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Falcons’ quarterback situation seems even murkier after head coach Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media on Wednesday. But Stefanski said he isn’t frustrated. “We want to be able to win and play well regardless of who’s in,” Stefanski said, and saying that the frustration actually comes from losing and falling short on the field. Cooper Rush will practice fully on Wednesday, per Stefanski. I’d expect Rush to remain on the injury report today as he is still getting treatment on his back. “Not many guys are 100% coming out of Week 1,” Stefanski said. Tua Tagovailoa will not practice on Wednesday, but Stefanski said Tua is “getting better.” We didn’t hear anything new from Stefanski on Michael Penix — he’s still progressing and the team and medical staff are happy with the progress, but there is no timetable for him to take over as the starter. And Stefanski declined to rule any quarterback out for Week 2’s home opener against the Carolina Panthers. Yes, that does create the possibility for Jack Strand to see some action on Sunday. Bijan Robinson also spoke to the media before practice, and he shared that it is a little challenging to not know who’s starting at quarterback on Sunday — and the fact that Tua and Penix are both lefties and Rush is right-handed is an additional wrinkle. If they’re designing this game plan around Rush, and they decide Friday that Tua will be the starter, it changes the direction of each play. But it doesn’t matter to Bijan who starts at quarterback — even if it means a LOT of touches like he had against the Steelers in Week 1. “We have so many great playmakers on the offense,” says Bijan. “…for me, it’s whatever I can do to help my team win the game.” And the skill players have to bring the energy and focus to prep this week so they’re prepared for anything, Bijan said. I’m still expecting Rush to start on Sunday against the Panthers, but I’d love to be surprised by Tua, or even better, by Penix.

title: The Falcoholic Reacts Survey: Key players stumble on opening day
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Falcons fans and fans across the country. While the Falcons fought valiantly in dire circumstances against Pittsburgh, the locker room had to be frustrated to fall short in a winnable game. Cooper Rush […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Alex Highsmith #56 of the Pittsburgh Steelers sacks Cooper Rush #13 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of a game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Falcons fans and fans across the country. While the Falcons fought valiantly in dire circumstances against Pittsburgh, the locker room had to be frustrated to fall short in a winnable game. Cooper Rush will attract all the headlines for his abysmal performance. Other subpar showings led to the team’s shortcomings, particularly from two players expected to be cornerstones at their positions. Matthew Bergeron and A.J. Terrell struggled with multiple penalties and were consistently beaten in individual matchups. Bergeron’s play didn’t resemble anything close to a guard making top-tier money. It didn’t matter who Terrell was covering on the outside. He was a step behind often against DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Pittsburgh could have scored a touchdown and produced multiple explosive plays when targeting the veteran cornerback. Questions should be raised about both players following their alarming performances. These are the games where teams with talent limitations need their key players to play at a high level. Losing matchups and being forced to commit desperate penalties won’t lead to wins. Those mistakes cost Maason Smith a sack from a nasty inside move and an impressive effort from Drake London, where he ran through multiple defenders to produce a rare positive passing play. title: Falcons put Da’Shawn Hand on IR, promote TE Nick Muse to active roster
summary: The Atlanta Falcons have made it official, placing Da’Shawn Hand on injured reserve with an ailment that’s expected to knock him out for the rest of the season. The team has promoted tight end Nick Muse to the 53 man roster in a corresponding move and have added defensive end Drake Jackson and running back […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Atlanta Falcons tight end Nick Muse (87) runs after a catch against Indianapolis Colts linebacker Bryce Boettcher (50) during the first half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Falcons have made it official, placing Da’Shawn Hand on injured reserve with an ailment that’s expected to knock him out for the rest of the season. The team has promoted tight end Nick Muse to the 53 man roster in a corresponding move and have added defensive end Drake Jackson and running back Khalil Herbert to the practice squad. The Atlanta Falcons have officially placed DT Da'Shawn Hand on injured reserve. They've signed TE Nick Muse to the active roster to fill Hand's spot. They've also filled out their practice squad by signing DE Drake Jackson and RB Khalil Herbert. https://t.co/rNd9evFFWs — Will McFadden (@willmcfadden) September 16, 2026 We wrote about Hand the other day , but suffice to say his injury is devastating given that the team was set to rely on him as a run-stopping early down force in the middle of this defense. The Falcons will have to replace him by committee but may still sign another player, given that their defensive front is talented but perhaps not as deep as we’d like early in the season. Muse earned the call-up by playing a ton on special teams against Pittsburgh and looking good both in that phase and in his limited looks as a blocker, the same as he has all summer. The Falcons are going to lean heavily on tight ends to help keep either Cooper Rush or Tua Tagovailoa alive in the first weeks of the season, and Muse figures to get some run as part of that mission. Jackson was a former second round pick for the 49ers who had three sacks in each of his first two seasons working as a reserve, but has seen his career spectacularly derailed by injuries that cost him half the 2023 season, the entire 2024 season, and much of the 2025 season. He was released by the Commanders, who picked him up in 2025, with an injury settlement earlier this year. If he’s healthy, he offers some experience and potential upside on the practice squad, as Jackson is still just 25 years old. I mentioned Herbert as a candidate for this roster way back in March , noting that he’s been a pretty productive player when he’s had opportunities, can catch the ball, and has returned kicks. With Tyler Goodson headed to Dallas, Atlanta needed a veteran third back and I think Herbert fits the bill quite well. We’ll see if he’s elevated this week. Join me in giving Muse his props for the elevation, welcoming Herbert and Jackson, and wishing Hand well on his recovery.

title: Falcons Week 1 3 up and 3 down: Defense is up, Offense is down
summary: The Atlanta Falcons couldn’t bring home the win in the season opener, but it wasn’t due to the defensive performances we saw. Unfortunately, the offense and special teams unit let the team down, a story many fans are tired of hearing. Here’s the Week 1, 3 up and 3 down: 3 up Sydney Brown Acquiring […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers is sacked by Za'darius Smith #91 of the Atlanta Falcons during the fourth quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons couldn’t bring home the win in the season opener, but it wasn’t due to the defensive performances we saw. Unfortunately, the offense and special teams unit let the team down, a story many fans are tired of hearing. Here’s the Week 1, 3 up and 3 down: 3 up Sydney Brown Falcons DB Sydney Brown was flying around. Showed that he can be a legit 3rd safety/overhang and make plays for you in the box. Falcons struggled with tackling in the secondary last year and Brown limited YAC opportunities yesterday. pic.twitter.com/ovudZnJ65y — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) September 14, 2026 Acquiring Brown was one of Ian Cunningham’s first moves as GM, and it’s already shaping up to be one of his best. When Brown signed, the initial thought was that he’d be a good special teams contributor and competent depth, but Jeff Ulbrich had bigger plans. Brown was more than depth in the season opener; he was essentially a starter, logging 30 snaps and making every one count. Brown was a force in the box, blowing up runs without fear and getting ball carriers on the ground almost immediately. He also blew up the screen play that led to a fumble recovery. It’s going to be fun to see how his role evolves on this defense, because he’s making it tough to keep him off the field. Za’Darius Smith Expectations were low for Smith entering Week 1; he was ready to call it a career and joined the team late. Smith blew those expectations out of the water. On just 16 snaps , he logged 2 sacks, providing the defense with the finisher they desperately needed after losing both Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr. Smith’s role is expected to grow as the season progresses, but getting production out of him this early on a limited snap count is hopefully a sign of even better things to come for the veteran. Maason Smith Smith was acquired in a player-for-player trade involving Ruke Orhorhoro. The initial take was that this was a lemon swap between two franchises disappointed with their 2nd-round investments. One man’s trash is another man’s treasure. Smith was a force early, splitting double teams and pushing the pocket. If not for a questionable penalty, he would’ve finished the afternoon with a sack. Atlanta has needed a physical presence in the middle of their front, and while it’s too early to say the problem is officially solved, this performance brings the team one step closer to checking that box. Falcons new DT Maason Smith had a nice debut pic.twitter.com/rytlVqKfww — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) September 14, 2026 3 down Matthew Bergeron It was a middling effort for the Falcons offensive line overall, but when you’re the highest-paid member, the spotlight will always be on you. Many questioned the price tag attached to Bergeron’s extension, and those questions still linger after this week’s performance. The left guard committed two holding penalties after getting beat clean off the snap. He also blew an assignment when pulling to the backside of the run, resulting in a negative play. There were flashes of good play but not enough to justify the new deal. Jake Matthews and Chris Lindstrom also had off days, so the hope is this was just the group still adjusting to the new scheme. Nick Folk The most accurate kicker from 2025 doubled his miss count in the 2026 opener. The 54-yard miss is somewhat understandable; at his age, that could be just outside of his range. However, the 45-yard miss was inexcusable. Yes, Pittsburgh is a notoriously difficult place to kick, but when the team signed Folk, it was with the expectation that he would be able to overcome those difficult environments. We aren’t hitting the panic button yet; Folk finished 2/4 on the day, but fans will be feeling a little less confident when he steps on the field for the next few games. Cooper Rush Rush was thrust into the starting role after Tua Tagovailoa was downgraded with an oblique strain. Rush then started experiencing back spasms the day before the game, and looked uncomfortable from the first snap. It was clear that the ball wasn’t getting aired out in this matchup, and even completing simple screens became a monumental task. It was interesting to see he had success on the few play-action concepts run Sunday, and if he’s starting again in Week 2, Rees needs to lean into those concepts more if he wants to salvage the passing game. The #Falcons ran 3 Playaction plays all from under center against the Steelers imo not just Cooper but the entire offense looked comfortable. Cooper had a 26.1% successfull play rate/ -1.07 epa on plays with no PA vs a 100% success rate/ +2.00 epa pic.twitter.com/EUH5xqLoMY — Juke🔴⚫️⚪️ (@Jukejuke99) September 15, 2026 While the Falcons didn’t get the win, all hope isn’t lost. This defense has legitimate pieces that will keep the Falcons in games all season. If the offense and special teams can pull their weight, this team can win games this year. The team will host the Carolina Panthers in Week 2, who’ve had the Falcons number lately.

title: Buffalo Bills records to watch against the Detroit Lions
summary: A new season means new chances to rewrite the record books, and it didn’t take long for us to have to start scribbling in ours.   The Buffalo Bills opened the season with a 36-31 win over the Houston Texans, and several of the numbers we were watching last week moved — including a couple that earned permanent ink.  Now […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: Khalil Shakir #10 of the Buffalo Bills warms up prior to an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images A new season means new chances to rewrite the record books, and it didn’t take long for us to have to start scribbling in ours. The Buffalo Bills opened the season with a 36-31 win over the Houston Texans, and several of the numbers we were watching last week moved — including a couple that earned permanent ink. Now the Bills come home. Not just home, but to a brand-new house as they host the Detroit Lions Thursday night in the first regular-season game ever played at the new Highmark Stadium. So, sharpen the pencils again. We have more numbers to watch. Each week, we’ll open the Buffalo Record Book to four chapters: Sure Things, A Good Bet, Not Impossible, and Superhuman. Some weeks, we will have an entry in every chapter. Other weeks, we may be more selective. This is one of those weeks. _____________________________________________________________________________ WEEK 2 — September 17, 2026 ____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1: Sure Things Nothing. Yes, Josh Allen will extend his consecutive-start streak when he takes the field Thursday night. And, yes, there will be all sorts of firsts recorded simply because this is the first regular-season game played inside the Bills’ new home. But we aren’t going to fill space just because we have a chapter to fill. Moving on. ____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2: A Good Bet • Khalil Shakir receptions: Last week, Shakir needed eight catches to move past Robert Woods and Jay Riemersma on Buffalo’s all-time receptions list. He got halfway there. Shakir caught four passes against Houston, bringing his career total to 201. Four more Thursday night gets him to 205 and moves the human pinball into 17th place in franchise history. Four catches? After doing exactly that in the first one? Yeah. We’ll call that a good bet. • Dawson Knox receptions: Knox also made progress Sunday, although it was just one catch for seven yards. That gives the Bills tight end 230 career receptions. Two more would move him past Cole Beasley and into 15th place on Buffalo’s all-time receptions list. Two catches feels considerably less dangerous to predict than three did a week ago. Although I am not saying enter this in your parlay – don’t forget Knox is sharing the field with a host of legitimate targets for Allen this year. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3: Not Impossible • Josh Allen keeps chasing running backs: Well, this one escalated quickly. Allen needed two rushing touchdowns against Houston to tie Frank Gore and Ottis Anderson for 20th on the NFL’s all-time rushing-touchdown list. So, naturally, he scored two. Allen enters Thursday with 81 career rushing touchdowns. One more would give him 82 and tie Corey Dillon for 19th all-time. Two? That gets Allen to 83 and another running back — Jim Taylor — at No. 18. Again, completely normal quarterback stuff. • Dawson Knox touchdown catches: This one didn’t move last week, so we’re trying it again. Knox remains at 27 career touchdown receptions. One Thursday would tie Stevie Johnson with 28 touchdown catches. A second would give Knox 29 and tie Jerry Butler for seventh on the Bills’ all-time list. Apparently, Allen was too busy throwing touchdowns to DJ Moore and Josh Palmer in Houston to help us with this one. We’ll give him another chance this week. • James Cook rushing yards : Look who escaped the Superhuman chapter this week! Cook entered Week 1 needing 187 yards to pass Joe Cribbs and move into fifth place on Buffalo’s all-time rushing list. His 57 yards against Houston didn’t get him particularly close Sunday, but they still count. Cook now has 4,316 career rushing yards, leaving him 130 yards away from passing Cribbs’ 4,445. One hundred thirty yards isn’t easy. But James Cook won the NFL rushing title last season. We’re certainly not calling it superhuman anymore. • Bradley Chubb’s road to 50: Chubb’s first regular-season game in a Bills uniform didn’t get him any closer to this one. The veteran still sits at 48 career sacks, meaning two against Jared Goff Thursday night would get him to 50. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4: Superhuman We’re leaving this one blank, too. No need to manufacture something ridiculous just so we can ask Josh Allen to throw for 600 yards or James Cook to run from Orchard Park to Detroit. ____________________________________________________________________________ There will already be history made Thursday night simply by playing a football game in the new Highmark Stadium. Let’s see who adds their name to the other pages while they’re there.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Buffalo Bills heroes and head-scratchers ahead of Week 2’s game vs Detroit Lions
summary: The Bills survived Houston. They got 96 hours to fix everything that almost got them beat before Josh Allen and company make their first official appearance at the new Highmark Stadium against a Lions team that just needed overtime to put away the Saints. Buffalo’s 36-31 win over the Texans was one of the most […]
full_text: The Bills survived Houston. They got 96 hours to fix everything that almost got them beat before Josh Allen and company make their first official appearance at the new Highmark Stadium against a Lions team that just needed overtime to put away the Saints. Buffalo’s 36-31 win over the Texans was one of the most entertaining openers in recent memory, but despite the win, there are some real issues that Detroit can take advantage of on a short week. Here are three Bills on fire, three that can do better, and how each of them fits into Thursday night. Heroes: Josh Allen, QB Allen was the engine of this offense in Week 1, and he’ll need to be again against a Lions team capable of turning this into a track meet. He finished 20-of-29 for 334 yards and two touchdowns, adding 23 rushing yards and two more scores on the ground — 357 total yards and four total touchdowns against a Texans defense that led the NFL in EPA per play, success rate, and yards per play a year ago. According to PFF, Allen posted a 69.7 passing grade with an 8.8% big-time-throw rate and a completion percentage 14.3 points above expectation, ranking fourth among all quarterbacks in EPA per play for the week. A big-time performance against a big-time opponent. The Lions needed overtime to beat New Orleans, with Jared Goff throwing for 206 yards and two scores and Jahmyr Gibbs running for 156 yards and two touchdowns on his own. If this turns into the shootout it has the potential to be, Buffalo’s margin for error shrinks to whatever Allen can create. He’s proven he can carry a game by himself. He might need to again. Dalton Kincaid, TE Kincaid was the biggest beneficiary of Allen’s big game, and if he stays healthy, Joe Brady certainly plans to make him one of the most dangerous mismatches in the league. He caught five of six targets for a career-high 130 yards, tying Khalil Shakir for second on the team in targets behind only DJ Moore. PFF gave him a 91.2 overall grade and a 91.6 receiving grade, both first among all tight ends in Week 1, to go with 5.91 yards per route run and two broken tackles after the catch. His 38-yard grab from his own end zone had just a 9.4% completion probability, per Next Gen Stats — officially the most improbable catch of the entire weekend. Brady has already shown he can increase Kincaid’s snaps by using him as a big receiver sometimes, in the role we used to see Tyrell Shavers last year, rather than a traditional in-line tight end, which lets him stay on the field without sacrificing what Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes bring as blockers. Detroit’s front seven is strong, but its safety group is banged up without starters Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, and this offense is going to test the over-the-middle area of the field regardless of who’s healthy. Kincaid can be up for another big game. Deone Walker, DT The second-year defensive tackle looks like he’s about to establish himself as one of the more disruptive young interior players in the league, and Thursday is about as good an opportunity as he’ll get all season. He generated two total pressures (one sack, one hurry) with three solo tackles, and PFF credited him with an 85.3 pass-rush grade that ranked third among 106 qualified interior linemen in Week 1 — on the heels of a rookie season in which PFF graded his pass-rush at 78.3 with 20 pressures on 283 snaps, naming him a breakout candidate for 2026. His most important play might have been the least statistical one: a red zone sack of C.J. Stroud with 16 seconds left that forced Houston’s final timeout and helped set up Greg Rousseau’s game-sealing strip sack. Detroit’s own injury report has them down two starting offensive linemen for Thursday — right tackle Blake Miller (knee) and left guard Christian Mahogany (hip) are both out, with center Cade Mays already on injured reserve. That’s Larry Borom and Ben Bartch filling in around a banged-up Juice Scruggs. Walker should live in that backfield, both collapsing running lanes for Jahmyr Gibbs and putting Jared Goff on the move before he wants to be. Head-Scratchers: Ed Oliver, DT Oliver wasn’t bad. He finished with five tackles and a fumble recovery on Houston’s opening drive, and everyone in that building knows what it takes for him to even be out there after the personal tragedy he’s gone through this offseason. None of that changes what the defense needs from its most established interior presence going forward — more than flashes. PFF graded him at a 54.9 overall, with a 61.2 pass-rush grade and a 48.8 run-defense grade, generating just two total pressures (one QB hit, one hurry, zero sacks) — modest numbers for the player who’s supposed to anchor this interior. That’s exactly what makes Thursday a real opportunity. Facing a patchwork interior with backups settling in next to a hobbled Scruggs, this is the week for Oliver to live in Detroit’s backfield and make Goff’s life uncomfortable before he can get the ball out to his playmakers. Damar Hamlin, S With Cole Bishop officially questionable (knee/groin) for Thursday, Hamlin’s role in Jim Leonhard’s defense could grow, and that’s a real concern. He played a notable number of snaps in that dime package against Houston, and PFF’s numbers back up the eye test: a 41.1 overall grade, a 49.5 coverage grade, and a 60.0 run-defense grade, all bottom-tier among qualified safeties. He allowed a 100.0 passer rating on his lone target in coverage. He’s shown, again, that he’s slow-footed and a liability in man coverage. That’s a brutal profile to bring into a game against this specific group. Amon-Ra St. Brown posted a 99th-percentile ESPN OPEN score and a 98th-percentile PFF route grade last season, and according to FantasyPros’ Week 1 usage report, he opened 2026 with a team-high 14 targets, a game-high 95% route participation rate, and two touchdowns in the win over New Orleans. Jameson Williams led the NFL in plays of 20-plus mph with the ball in his hands back in 2024, per NFL Next Gen Stats, and he’s continued to show documented in-game speeds north of 21 mph since. Sam LaPorta adds size and red zone gravity underneath. If Hamlin is on the field in a significant role, Leonhard needs to be smart about how he uses him, because this Lions offense will find the weak link. Dee Alford, CB Alford ended the game fine, with a couple of coverage plays down the stretch that mattered. That doesn’t erase one of the rougher debuts of the week for a Bills defender (51.8 PFF overall grade, 52.4 in coverage, 54.6 against the run). He and Maxwell Hairston got their signals crossed on a blown coverage that nearly cost Buffalo the game outright, and he was beaten for a 20-yard third-down conversion to Xavier Hutchinson in the fourth quarter. It wasn’t an isolated moment — he looked lost for stretches in his first game as a Bill after signing a three-year, $21 million free-agent deal this offseason to be one of the veteran leaders of this defensive backfield. Detroit runs arguably the best slot receiver in football in Amon-Ra St. Brown, who lines up in exactly the space Alford is responsible for. The former Falcon needs to be at the top of his game Thursday, because this secondary will need to survive a very tough matchup so the offense can lead the way again. Honorable Mentions Trending Up: Greg Rousseau (OLB) — Two sacks, two forced fumbles, five quarterback hits, and a game-sealing strip sack of Stroud with 16 seconds left. PFF’s 84.5 grade was the second-highest on the entire Bills roster. DJ Moore (WR) — Five catches for 100 yards and a 43-yard touchdown in his first game in a Bills uniform, good for a 79.0 PFF grade, third-best on the team. Trending Down: Christian Benford (CB) — Beaten routinely by Nico Collins throughout the afternoon, finishing with eight catches allowed on 85 yards and a 38.7 PFF grade, third-worst on the roster . James Cook (RB) — Just 13 carries for 57 yards and three catches for 12 yards, with Allen doing most of the offensive heavy lifting. Per…

title: Buffalo Bills K Tyler Bass’ nearly flawless start needed vs. Detroit Lions
summary: It’s a short week so expect short content, but there were a few things from this game that stood out and I couldn’t pass up on my thoughts about Buffalo Bills kicker Tyler Bass. As this was originally written too early for the All-22 to be out, I’ll ask you to endure this just being […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - AUGUST 22: Buffalo Bills place kicker Tyler Bass (16) leaves the field following the National Football League preseason game between the Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns on August 22, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s a short week so expect short content, but there were a few things from this game that stood out and I couldn’t pass up on my thoughts about Buffalo Bills kicker Tyler Bass. As this was originally written too early for the All-22 to be out, I’ll ask you to endure this just being narrative based. If you’ve been following along with the Bills in recent years, you know that Bass missed the entire 2025 NFL season due to injury, and that he carried a reputation for having a bit of the yips prior to that. Buffalo felt a healthy Bass was the right call and one week into the 2026 season, holy moly was he ever. Let’s take a glance back at Bass’ return to see what might be in store for Week 2 against the Detroit Lions. Kickin’ Bass The Bills won by five points in a bit of a nail-biter over the Houston Texans. Any kind of miss by Tyler Bass would have loomed large, so let’s start off with the idea of him scoring points. Bass was asked to kick three extra points and, in my opinion, one of those was as close to a blemish as it gets for this kind of kicking. Squeaking inside the right upright, one of the extra points wasn’t picture perfect. That said, it still went in. In the field goal game, Bass was called on three times as well. Bass’ first try was from 46, not a gimme but well within his range. His other two tries were from 34 and 33 yards. These should be chip shots for Bass. He made all three and none of them looked questionable from what I recall. That’s 12 points off of Bass’ foot. The reason for this article though wasn’t the field goals and extra points. The NFL has been tinkering with the kickoff rules quite a bit in the last few years and the current mold rewards kickers who kick it just short of the end zone. Kicks can’t be downed unless they go into the end zone, so the closer to the razor’s edge of the end line, the better. How did Tyler bass do in this regard. Here’s where his kickoffs landed in Week 1: Houston one-yard line Three-yard line The Houston ZERO. This is quite literally a perfect kick. It HAS to be returned from here Houston three Houston three Houston three Houston seven Houston three The closest thing to a blemish was the second-to-last kick landing at the seven. Let’s see how Fairbairn did: Buffalo eight Buffalo one Touchback Buffalo five Buffalo five Buffalo one NFL fans know Fairbairn’s name too, consistently being one of the best in the business. He had some amazing kicks himself Sunday (including another very long field goal against Buffalo), but Bass’ consistency was out of this world good. For at least this fan, I’m hoping it’s not a fluke. I’ve always liked Tyler Bass’ swagger and we should all remember that he still holds the Bills’ single-season points record after unseating Steve Christie in his rookie year. Bass’ record is 141 points, one more than Christie’s. Fan club membership aside, Bass being great only helps the Bills. Fingers crossed we see inside-the-five kicks Thursday evening, and all season.

title: Buffalo Bills should continue to lean into early-down passing
summary: While the NFL analytics community has long pushed passing on first down, it’s certainly not a new methodology birthed out of an algorithm, and if Week 1 is any indication of what’s to come for the Buffalo Bills, they may be returning to those early-down passing roots. Bill Walsh famously championed this counterculture in the […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 13: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills looks to pass against the Houston Texans in the first quarter of a game at NRG Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the NFL analytics community has long pushed passing on first down, it’s certainly not a new methodology birthed out of an algorithm, and if Week 1 is any indication of what’s to come for the Buffalo Bills, they may be returning to those early-down passing roots. Bill Walsh famously championed this counterculture in the 1980s, regularly stating openly his teams prioritized passing the football on first (and second down), with the hopes of actually not needing to get to third down at all. As a gigantic advocate of this passing framework — particularly with Josh Allen at quarterback — it was glorious to see the Bills go pass-happy on early downs in the season-opening win over the Texans. Here’s the NFL’s early-down (first and second down) pass frequency through Week 1 in “neutral” situations, which in this case, is based on win probability not being lopsided toward one team (ie. the game is reasonably close in score): The Bills in sixth place is, in my opinion, a tremendous start for this Joe Brady offense. For as much as I’m inclined to want the Bills to literally lead the league in early-down passing, I do understand the presence of one James Cook, the league’s reigning rushing champion. Of course — sample size — but check the difference in placement for the Bills in the below graphic that shows every team’s early-down pass frequency in neutral situations from the start of 2024 through 2025. The Bills finished in 20th in this advanced metric, with a pass rate in those circumstances just under 50%. They were over 60% in Week 1 against the Texans. There was also this, from Rich Hribar on Twitter: On the road in Houston, the Bills averaged 9.6 yards per play on 1st downs yesterday, their most in a game since 2023. Josh Allen threw for a league-high 186 yards on 1st downs. 8 of 12 passing, 7 1st downs. — Rich Hribar (@LordReebs) September 14, 2026 At this point, you might be asking yourself, “do we know passing on early downs is actually better for an offense than running?” For The Athletic in 2019, Ben Baldwin wrote “ The 10 commandments of numbers-based football analysis ” highlighted by the reality that 1st and 10 runs regularly result in modest gains, thereby leaving the offense in 2nd-and-long situations. No bueno. Instead choosing to pass on first down increases the likelihood of getting into a 2nd-and-manageable (or short) scenario or even moving the chains entirely. A decade earlier, the real seminal piece on this front came from Brian Burke — before he was at ESPN — wrote a tremendous historical run-pass balance article explaining his findings from 1970 to 2009, and (paraphrasing here, of course) proved that because passing performance steadily increased, therefore yielding a higher yards-play-play average than a run, offenses were actually relinquishing efficiency by running the ball at close to a 50-50 split on early downs. Among all teams in Week 1, the Bills generated the sixth-most Expected Points Added per play and EPA per drop back on first and second down. And that very well could have been due to how frequently they decided to drop back to pass on those early downs against the Texans. We’ll see if this trend continues for this new-look offense in Week 2 against the Lions and throughout Buffalo’s 2026 season.

author: Matt Byham

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. the Detroit Lions
summary: Fresh off a thrilling 36-31 victory over the Houston Texans, the Buffalo Bills have little time to prepare for their 2026 home opener against the Detroit Lions. A Thursday night kickoff means that the Bills have but three off days before taking the field to begin play in Week Two. Fortunately, the Bills escaped Houston […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 13: Offensive tackle Dion Dawkins #73 of the Buffalo Bills readies to block during the NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Buffalo Bills on September 13, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX.(Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Fresh off a thrilling 36-31 victory over the Houston Texans, the Buffalo Bills have little time to prepare for their 2026 home opener against the Detroit Lions. A Thursday night kickoff means that the Bills have but three off days before taking the field to begin play in Week Two. Fortunately, the Bills escaped Houston relatively healthy, which means that they’ll have nearly their full array of players available for what should be a great game. The Bills were outstanding on offense last week, putting up 36 points on a Houston defense widely regarded as one of the best units in the league. Buffalo’s own stop unit, however, left plenty of room for improvement, and while they performed better as the game progressed, they still allowed nearly 400 yards of total offense, 26 first downs, and 36 minutes of possession. With that in mind, we have a slight slant towards the defensive side of the ball for this week’s five players to watch. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB James Cook III Buffalo’s lead running back was the NFL’s leading rusher last year, and while he was efficient against a tough Texans run defense (13 carries, 57 yards), I’m looking for more out of him this week. Cook was active in the pass game, as he saw four targets to slot in behind DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid, and Khalil Shakir in the pecking order. He caught three of those passes for just twelve yards. Cook dropped a pass late in the game when he heard the footsteps of linebacker Aziz Al’Shaiir coming. He also narrowly averted disaster when he fumbled on the opening play of what would become Buffalo’s game-winning touchdown drive. Cook had a career-high six fumbles last year in the regular season, and the fumble he lost in Buffalo’s playoff loss to the Denver Broncos swung early momentum away from the Bills and back towards the home team while Buffalo was driving. Cook doesn’t have to put up superstar numbers every week, but watching him keep hold of the ball while scoring would be a nice way to kick off Week Two and his first game at the new Highmark Stadium. LT Dion Dawkins I’ll preface this with the positive: Buffalo’s offense line did a great job against the Texans last week, as they kept Josh Allen upright and gave him time to make multiple big plays down the field. The assignment isn’t any easier this week, though, as someone is going to have to deal with Aiden Hutchinson, Detroit’s Pro Bowl pass rusher who was named Second-Team All Pro last year. If Pro Football Focus grades are your thing, Dawkins graded out as one of the five worst offensive players for the Bills last week, earning a 53.1 grade from the analytics site. Given that most of us have had high praise for Buffalo’s offensive line last week, it is a red flag for me that three of the team’s five lowest graded players on offense were linemen, as O’Cyrus Torrence (45.4) and Alec Anderson (52.4) were also in that bottom group. Dawkins had some bad reps—a whiff on corner Kamari Lassiter on Buffalo’s failed fourth-down try during the first offensive possession of the game comes to mind—but the good reps outweighed the bad. He’ll need to put together another strong performance this week against a Lions pass rush unit that sacked New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough five times last week. OLB Bradley Chubb Chubb played a ton of snaps last week, logging 63 of the team’s 79 defensive snaps. He totaled four tackles and two quarterback hits on the afternoon, which isn’t a terrible showing, but it’s not quite what we’d like to see from the veteran pass rusher. Given how disruptive Greg Rousseau was on Sunday, I assume that the Lions will look to slide protection his way. That should leave Chubb in some one-on-one situations, and it he can beat his man to pressure Jared Goff, then the Bills will be in great shape. The problem is that the Lions have an all-world left tackle in Penei Sewell. so if that’s the one v. one matchup, it’s definitely advantage Lions whether Chubb or Rousseau is across from him. Using some games and stunts up front to free up rushers is going to be the move, and new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard did a nice job generating pressure using that method with just his front four on Sunday. Look for Chubb to move around the formation a bit more this week rather than anchoring an OLB spot like he did on Sunday. CB Christian Benford Buffalo’s top corner had a tough matchup on Sunday against Nico Collins, and it was not his finest hour as a result. Collins caught seven passes for 75 yards and a score on ten targets, most of which came when matched up against Benford. Quarterback C.J. Stroud targeted Benford a whopping 11 times in the game, completing seven of those passes for a total of 75 yards and a touchdown. Benford started slowly last season, too, before turning it on late, but his matchup isn’t going to be any easier this week. Given that he traveled with Collins against the Texans, it wouldn’t surprise me to see him travel with Detroit’s top wideout, Amon-Ra St. Brown. Granted, St. Brown does more work in the slot than Collins does, so that might pose a problem or change the calculus a bit, but the Bills believe—rightly—that Benford is their best cover guy. He’s going to have to step up and try to bottle another big-play receiver this week. CB Dee Alford Two corners make the list this week, as the defensive secondary was not an area I was impressed with on Sunday. Alford, in particular, left a lot to be desired, as he seemed to miscommunicate on multiple assignments. He didn’t look great in run support, either, often coming in a step late or a step wide to expose running lanes for David Montgomery and Woody Marks. Alford has big shoes to fill given the hard-nosed example of what a nickel corner can do that Taron Johnson set over the last eight seasons, and for the first week, he did not fill them well. Detroit has a bevy of receiving options that can line up all over the formation, so Alford could see work against Amon-Ra St. Brown, tight end Sam LaPorta, or anyone in between. He’ll need to step up this week.
author: Sean Murphy

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Detroit Lions: Series history, Josh Allen record
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions have both been around for a long time. A really long time. Yet, somehow, Thursday night will be just the 14th regular-season meeting between the two franchises.  And, because apparently 13 games spread across more than five decades isn’t weird enough, there’s this: The Bills have scored 274 points in those games. The Lions have scored 273. One point […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 15: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball while being chased by Jamal Adams #25 of the Detroit Lions in the third quarter at Ford Field on December 15, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions have both been around for a long time. A really long time. Yet, somehow, Thursday night will be just the 14th regular-season meeting between the two franchises. And, because apparently 13 games spread across more than five decades isn’t weird enough, there’s this: The Bills have scored 274 points in those games. The Lions have scored 273. One point separates two teams that have been playing football for over a combined hundred years. This week’s Time Capsule takes us through a series that hasn’t given us a lot of games but has certainly given us a few worth remembering. _____________________________________________________________________________ The last time: Dec. 15, 2024 This one was supposed to be a potential Super Bowl preview. The Lions entered the afternoon 12-1 and riding an 11-game winning streak. The Bills were 10-3 and coming off a 44-42 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Apparently, Buffalo decided 42 points wasn’t enough. The Bills walked into Ford Field and scored 48. Josh Allen threw for 362 yards and two touchdowns while adding another 68 yards and two scores on the ground. James Cook rushed for 105 yards and two touchdowns as Buffalo piled up 559 yards of offense. And they needed almost all of it. Buffalo jumped out to a 14-0 lead and stretched that advantage to 35-14 in the third quarter, but Jared Goff and the Lions weren’t going quietly. Goff threw for 494 yards and five touchdowns. Detroit scored 21 points in the fourth quarter, and a game Buffalo had seemingly put away turned into one where nobody could really relax until the clock finally hit zero. Bills 48. Lions 42. Potential Super Bowl preview? Well, we know how that part turned out. But Buffalo did leave Detroit with one of its biggest wins of the regular season, and Allen left with another addition to the increasingly ridiculous collection of games on his MVP résumé. _____________________________________________________________________________ Before that: Thanksgiving in Detroit Two years earlier, Allen and the Bills were also in Detroit. Actually, they were there for the second time in five days. A massive snowstorm in Western New York had forced Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Cleveland Browns to Ford Field. The Bills won that one, flew home, and then turned around and went right back to Detroit for Thanksgiving. Because why make anything easy? This time, the Lions made sure Buffalo had to work until the very end. Detroit tied the game at 25 with just 23 seconds left. Allen hit Stefon Diggs for 36 yards on the first play of the ensuing drive, Buffalo moved into field-goal range, and Tyler Bass connected from 45 yards with two seconds left to give the Bills a 28-25 win. Allen finished with 253 passing yards and two touchdowns while adding 78 yards and another score on the ground. It wasn’t quite the offensive explosion we would see two years later, but the result was the same. _____________________________________________________________________________ The first one: Rookie Josh To find Allen’s first game against Detroit, we have to go all the way back to 2018. Buffalo was 4-9. Detroit was 5-8. Allen was a rookie, and the Bills were still trying to figure out exactly what they had in their first-round quarterback. There were clues. Allen threw for 204 yards and a touchdown and rushed for another score as Buffalo beat Detroit 14-13. It wasn’t 48-42, and it wasn’t a last-second Thanksgiving win, but it started a streak. Allen is now 3-0 against Detroit. Thursday night gives him a chance to make it four. _____________________________________________________________________________ How far back do we have to go? Want to find the last time the Lions beat the Bills? We need to open a slightly older Time Capsule. Oct. 15, 2006. Dick Jauron was Buffalo’s head coach. J.P. Losman was the quarterback. Willis McGahee was carrying the football. For Detroit, it was Jon Kitna at quarterback, Kevin Jones at running back, and Roy Williams catching passes. The Lions won 20-17, and they haven’t beaten Buffalo since. The Bills have won five straight meetings — in 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022, and 2024. Of course, there’s a pretty important qualifier here. Buffalo and Detroit only see each other once every four years under the NFL’s normal scheduling rotation, so a 20-year drought doesn’t exactly mean the Bills have spent two decades tormenting the Lions. But 20 years is 20 years. _____________________________________________________________________________ One stadium closes, another one opens There’s one more piece of history that makes this week’s matchup a little different. Allen’s first game against Detroit, that 14-13 win in 2018, was the last time the Lions played a regular-season game in Orchard Park. It was also their last game in the old Highmark Stadium. Now they’re back, and this time they’re part of something much bigger than the series history. Thursday night’s game will be the first regular-season game played in the new Highmark Stadium. The Bills and Lions have met only 13 times. Buffalo holds an 8-4-1 advantage. One point separates them on the all-time scoreboard. Detroit hasn’t beaten Buffalo since 2006, and Josh Allen has never lost to the Lions. But none of that history happened here. The new stadium doesn’t have a Bills-Lions story yet. Thursday night gets to write the first one.
