title: Chargers bringing sense of urgency in Week 2 vs. Raiders
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers have a lot of work to do after their season-opening loss against the Arizona Cardinals. The Cardinals came into the season with low expectations and the Chargers were viewed as a massive favorite going into the game, but that wasn’t reflected in the 26-14 loss. With a chance to start 0-2 […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on in the fourth quarter of a game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers have a lot of work to do after their season-opening loss against the Arizona Cardinals. The Cardinals came into the season with low expectations and the Chargers were viewed as a massive favorite going into the game, but that wasn’t reflected in the 26-14 loss. With a chance to start 0-2 at home against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, the Chargers are attacking this week with more urgency than before. “Just as I would have expected,” Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said in his press conference. “Everybody really looking at their position, their group, and trying to find out exactly what they can do better to help the cause, just as you would expect a group of competitors to be about.” The Chargers have been in the postseason in each of the last two seasons under Harbaugh, but they have yet to win a playoff game. They know this year can provide that next step forward, but not if they continue to play how they did on Sunday. There was a lethargic energy on both ends of the field, which the Cardinals were easily able to take advantage of. The Cardinals went into the game with nothing to lose, and they played just like that. The Chargers need to zap some of that energy from the Cardinals and apply it to themselves because losing back-to-back games at home at the start of the season to two teams that finished in the top three of the NFL Draft will only set Los Angeles up for failure moving forward. BFTB community, how do you feel about the progress going into this week against the Raiders? Let us know in the comments section below.

title: The personnel grouping that makes Rams dangerous can’t save a deficit
summary: The rest of the NFL was quick to emulate the Los Angeles Rams’ frequent deployment of 13 personnel (one RB, three TE’s) over the offseason. But LA was forced off their spot as soon as Week 1. The San Francisco 49ers took away the Rams’ most effective personnel grouping and cornered them into running 11 […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Terrance Ferguson #18 of the Los Angeles Rams attempts to catch a pass in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images The rest of the NFL was quick to emulate the Los Angeles Rams’ frequent deployment of 13 personnel (one RB, three TE’s) over the offseason. But LA was forced off their spot as soon as Week 1. The San Francisco 49ers took away the Rams’ most effective personnel grouping and cornered them into running 11 personnel (one RB, one TE) at a 56% clip . The problem being that the Rams’ offensive production fell off a cliff when they transitioned away from 13 personnel, which underscores an offseason-long issue . LA passed on upgrading over Jordan Whittington and Konata Mumpfield at third receiver through free agency and the draft. It’s completely unsurprising that neither player is able to carve into the target share of Puka Nacua or Davante Adams. This is not something that can be fixed in the short-term, and the Rams have already spent plenty of draft capital on acquiring Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett. You can try to go back to the well. It might be dry. Of course, 11 personnel being less effective than 13 personnel is a problem. The bigger, ongoing concern is the fact that the 49ers were easily able to get the Rams out of their comfort zone. How did they do it? Well, they built an early lead. If you are hoping to cut into a deficit, you aren’t going to lean into 13 personnel. Teams need more firepower through the air, and usually it helps to have as many receivers on the field as possible. Heavier personnel also requires the threat of a commitment to the run game. Passing in 13 is a changeup off the running game. It’s difficult to live in a traditional drop back world with mostly marginal athletes on the field. These limitations were perfectly acceptable if the Rams were the world beaters we were told they would be. Through one week that has not been the case, and now LA’s best defensive player—Myles Garrett—will sit out for at least the next four games. The Rams may still be a good or even great team. Their chance of building a lead early and then milking it with heavier personnel packages may at least be mitigated in the short term. Sean McVay is one of the best offensive play callers in the NFL. His decision making is still subject to situational football and the overall game script. The Rams may not be who McVay wants them to be this year simply because the score might force them to change.

title: Not all 0-1 NFC teams should be hitting the panic button
summary: The Los Angeles Rams got off to the worst start imaginable in Week 1, but several other playoff-hopeful NFC teams did too. Playoff teams from last season, including the Rams, Packers and Panthers, lost their season openers, each in a spectacularly depressing fashion. In fact, Los Angeles and Green Bay are the only winless teams […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled after making a pass in the first quarter of the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams got off to the worst start imaginable in Week 1, but several other playoff-hopeful NFC teams did too. Playoff teams from last season, including the Rams, Packers and Panthers, lost their season openers, each in a spectacularly depressing fashion. In fact, Los Angeles and Green Bay are the only winless teams in their respective divisions, while Carolina is fortunate(?) to play in the NFC South, where no teams won in Week 1. That’s pretty on-brand for that division. Not every team should be panicking after losing the first game, but some teams should be more concerned than others. Here is the panic meter for five 0-1 playoff-hopeful NFC teams ahead of Week 2. Los Angeles Rams Week 1 Result: Lost 27-7 to the 49ers The Rams are currently the worst team in their division and were the only team not to score double-digit points in Week 1. That’s the bad news, and I didn’t even mention how Myles Garrett is out for the next four games. The good news, however, is that LA has had plenty of time to assess what they did against the 49ers. Los Angeles has about a week and a half to prepare for the Giants. They should be well-rested and come out with more energy after probably being crazy tired from the late arrival in Australia. The Rams will be fine, even if they have some ground to make up. On the plus side, they have no more international games coming up, so no worries about any more bone-headed travel plans. Panic Meter: Low, even if the upcoming schedule featuring road trips to Philadelphia and Denver is daunting. Carolina Panthers Week 1 Result: Lost 59-37 to the Bears The Panthers were on the wrong end of the highest-scoring season opener in NFL history. However, there were some positive takeaways from the game. The defense wasn’t one of them, as Carolina gave up 552 yards of offense, with nearly 300 of those coming on the ground. They also made Caleb Williams look like an accurate quarterback for an afternoon. Holy cow, that’s bad! Oh right, the positives! The Panthers seem to have a solid offense. Yes, Chicago was missing several key defenders, but either way, they moved the ball well for much of the game. This despite being limited to 13 points in the second half. Bryce Young also seemed to pick up where he left off after a career year. Bryce Young did what in Week 1?! https://t.co/z5nD6tObLi — Corbin (@corbin_young21) September 14, 2026 Like the Rams, the Panthers will be fine. Though they are nowhere near LA’s talent level if things pan out as expected. Panic Meter: Fairly low. Every team has a chance in their crappy excuse for a division. Green Bay Packers Week 1 Result: Lost 39-22 to the Vikings It’s not that the Packers lost; it’s how. Green Bay cannot hold a lead to save their lives, and that’s a problem. It’s not a recent occurrence, either. This has been a significant issue dating back to early last season. In the last year, the #Packers had a 99% chance of winning vs. the #Browns and #Bears (regular season), a 96% chance vs. the #Bears (playoffs) and a 90% chance today vs. the #Vikings late in those contests. The odds of going 0-4 were 1-in-2.5 million, yet GB did it. — Rob Reischel (@robreischel) September 14, 2026 The Packers gave up 22 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, turning a 12-point lead into a 16-point loss. Their defense even allowed Carson Wentz to become the first quarterback off the bench to throw three touchdowns and no interceptions in a season-opening win since Minnesota legend Fran Tarkenton in 1961. Aside from that, the offensive line play is atrocious, forcing Jordan Love to run for his life on every play. GB has a six-game losing streak dating back to last season. If they struggle in their next two games against the Jets and Falcons, their season’s essentially over before a Week 4 rematch against the Bears at Lambeau Field. It’s reasonable to say Matt LaFleur is coaching for his job this season, and will likely be out if the collapses continue. Panic Meter: Be afraid, be very, very afraid cheeseheads. You’re in for a long season. Dallas Cowboys Week 1 Result: Lost 28-20 to the Giants The Cowboys weren’t facing the same old Giants on Sunday night, yet Dallas was back to its usual ways defensively. That’s, um, not great, considering all the investments they made on defense this offseason. Things were so bad against New York that everybody’s favorite color commentator Cris Collinsworth was ripping them on the broadcast. Once Collinsworth dunks on you, just know it’s over. Cris Collinsworth: "I thought I saw some bad defense out of the Cowboys last year. That sequence was as bad as it gets… I don't know who's blowing these coverages…" 🏈🎙️ pic.twitter.com/JkuvCX8bPS — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 14, 2026 It wasn’t just the defense that had a rough night. Dak Prescott was held to under 200 yards passing, and no Cowboys wideout had more than 50 receiving yards. Personally, I pegged this team as a potential dark-horse NFC Championship team , and thought they might do something with above-average defensive play. Sunday was the same old Cowboys, and I apologize for maybe becoming as delusional as their fanbase for that dark-horse pick. Fool me once! Panic Meter: Relatively high. This was a game they couldn’t afford to lose. Their new-look defense will be tested in upcoming games against the Ravens, Packers and Eagles. Washington Commanders Week 1 Result: Lost 24-22 to the Eagles Washington looked decent against the Eagles, but that wasn’t good enough to win. They did look much improved compared to last season, yet they’re a far cry from the team that made an NFC Championship run two seasons ago. Jayden Daniels played fine for a guy coming off an injury-plagued campaign. The defense was also okay, limiting Philly, which was breaking in a new offensive coordinator, to 318 total yards. There isn’t much to say about the Commanders, as they came into 2026 with not as much hype as they did a year ago. Only playing good enough won’t do the trick in a relatively strong NFC. Panic Meter: High. They could very well start 0-3 with games against the Cowboys and Seahawks coming up.

title: Rams’ decision not to draft a linebacker could cost them
summary: When the Los Angeles Rams opted to trade their first-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons in 2025, they also bypassed the opportunity to draft back-to-back Defensive Rookie of the Year players. The Rams traded pick 26 to the Falcons and shortly thereafter the Cleveland Browns drafted linebacker Carson Schwesinger at 33, a rookie who ended […]
full_text: When the Los Angeles Rams opted to trade their first-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons in 2025, they also bypassed the opportunity to draft back-to-back Defensive Rookie of the Year players. The Rams traded pick 26 to the Falcons and shortly thereafter the Cleveland Browns drafted linebacker Carson Schwesinger at 33, a rookie who ended up being ranked in the top-100 by his peers after only one season. But Schwesinger would not be the last example of an opportunity the Rams had to draft a linebacker that they may end up regretting, as rookie second-round picks Josaiah Trotter, Anthony Hill, and Jacob Rodriguez all had outstanding Week 1 performances for their respective teams. They also all had better games than Nate Landman, Shaun Dolac, and Omar Speights. No. 93 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Browns LB Carson Schwesinger! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/mam7nlaoz2 — NFL (@NFL) June 25, 2026 When will the Rams’ value linebackers? Landman, who is in the first season of a three-year, $22.5 million contract signed in the middle of 2025, has not been the linebacker expected to be when he was extended. In Week 1, Landman had a PFF grade of 50.3 (for what it’s worth), as he’s been a frequent target in the passing game and is considered to be someone struggling against the run . He was blamed for a missed tackle in Week 1 as well. The 49ers were able to run against L.A.’s defense at will, and while plenty of blame will fall on Chris Shula, coaching is a hell of a lot easier when the team has great players. The Rams do not have great linebackers and that’s something fans have known for years. They certainly knew it when the Rams opted to trade down in 2025 and Schwesinger was on the board. Speights was better against the run than Landman, but much worse in coverage. He’s merely a replacement level player (at his absolute best), with or without the “hip pointer” injury that he’s currently dealing with. Sean McVay said that ILB Omar Speights has some swelling in his hip after getting a hip pointer Friday. “We’ll kind of manage him throughout the week, but he's feeling better than what we had anticipated. He's as tough as it gets, and so he's making positive gains right now.” — Benjamin Royer (@thebenroyer) September 14, 2026 Dolac had the best PFF grade of the three, but it still wasn’t considered a good day for him either. We expected the Rams to have a weakness at linebacker … and they do. Didn’t draft Schwesinger Although Carson Schwesinger had a bad Week 1 game against the Jaguars — no worse than Landman had against the 49ers — he’s far more likely to become a perennial star than most defensive players in the NFL under 25. At any position. He’d be a breath of fresh air on the Rams. Les Snead decided that instead of drafting Schwesinger, he’d trade that pick to Atlanta and eventually select tight end Terrance Ferguson. Okay. No targets for Terrance Ferguson, but he had a 73% route share in the first half. Ran more routes than any other Rams tight end. — JJ Zachariason (@LateRoundQB) September 11, 2026 Through one season and one game, Ferguson has yet to have the impact on the passing game that Sean McVay hoped he would have by now. He did clock the second-most snaps among LA’s tight ends in Week 1 behind Colby Parkinson and maybe his targets will increase, but then there’s also a future in which he must co-exist with Max Klare anyway. In any case, just know that’s the score: Didn’t draft a LB (or someone else) Did draft Ferguson + get a 2026 first-round pick The Rams received Atlanta’s first-round pick in 2026, which of course they used on Ty Simpson. Between those two picks, the Rams had a player who was inactive in Week 1 and another who had zero catches on one target. The long-term outcome could play out great in L.A.’s favor if Simpson becomes a starting quarterback and Ferguson is an above-average tight end. Even without Ferguson, any future with Simpson as a good starting QB is a win for Snead. Okay, that’s established. However, in the meantime, as the Rams look to rebound from an 0-1 start with an increasingly difficult schedule ahead, this potentially detrimental weakness in the middle of their defense could cost L.A. amid an “all-in” season. The 2026 draft standouts By drafting Ty Simpson, trading their own first-round pick for Trent McDuffie, and using a second-round pick on Klare, plus a third-round pick on Keagan Trost, the Rams did end up avoiding the opportunity to take one of these linebackers. All of whom weren’t just as good or slightly better than Landman in Week 1, but extraordinarily better: 2.43 LB Jacob Rodriguez, Dolphins Drafting Rodriguez, one of the most coveted defensive players in the draft, would have necessitated not drafting Simpson (and trading down from pick 13, if they could find a good partner), not trading for McDuffie, or trading up from pick 2.61. These are obviously all difficult moves to pull off based on what the Rams actually did, but I’m not going to just let it go that Rodriguez—as obvious an NFL star as Schwesinger—came out swinging in Week 1. He had a PFF grade of 90.3. Jacob Rodriguez did not look like a rookie for Miami on Sunday 5 SOLO, 9 AST He was flying around all game vs. Las Vegas. https://t.co/ma4aR4UFim pic.twitter.com/0tmhLK36eK — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 14, 2026 He had 14 tackles in his debut. 2.46 – LB Josaiah Trotter, Buccaneers Trotter had 11 tackles in his NFL debut with Tampa Bay, plus he had a grade of 72.8. Trotter’s debut was the splashiest of all these players—and all rookies probably—notching a pick-six and a sack against Joe Burrow. Just 21 years old, Trotter could have a future as bright as his father’s career with the Eagles. Josiah Trotter is having a DEBUT FOR THE AGES Pick Six Sack 7 Tackles Bucs look like they found one outta @MizzouFootball pic.twitter.com/jdNiX3KT9A — PFF (@PFF) September 13, 2026 Again, the Rams would have had to maneuver to get him, but let’s talk about that: In 2025, the Seahawks traded picks 52 and 82 for pick 34 and then they drafted Nick Emmanwori. Do they regret it? Emmanwori helped Seattle win the Super Bowl by having one of the best rookie seasons by a defensive back in recent memory. And the Seahawks were able to do it by trading a second and a third for a higher second round pick: The Rams had picks 61 and 93 but were content with waiting to draft players who they KNEW would not contribute this season, which ended up being Klare and Trost. Snead just had to pick up the phone. He could have traded those picks and drafted Rodriguez or Trotter. But it would have taken even less to get the next linebacker. 2.60 – LB Anthony Hill, Titans Taken just one pick ahead of Klare, who was inactive in Week 1 and is likely to continue to be a healthy scratch for many weeks to come, Hill had 16 tackles in his NFL debut, four stops, two pass breakups, and a PFF grade of 78.7. Anthony Hill Jr. snaps in his NFL debut 14 total tackles, 4 stop tackles, 2 pass breakups… he looked like the best player on the Titans defense 👀 pic.twitter.com/Mvd6PEkQdF — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) September 14, 2026 Like Trotter, he’s also only 21. (Rodriguez is 24.) Anthony Hill is basically a “Ready, set, linebacker” who comes into the NFL as a plug and play option in the middle of any defense. He would have been an upgrade in run defense and pass defense over Landman, Speights, and Dolac. Pick your poison. While trading up for the other two would have necessitated both day two picks (still should have done that though), trading up for Hill would have cost nothing. It would be the inclusion of a seventh round pick, or a sixth-round pick in 2028 maybe. Nothing. If Snead thought that Hill would fall to him, that’s a miscalculation. But more likely than not, the Rams never planned to draft Anthony Hill anyway. That’s a mistake. What now? The only option moving forward this season is to continue to start their own players and hope they get better, as a trade for a…

title: Aaron Donald has ‘realistic’ chance to play vs. Giants
summary: There is a “very, very realistic chance” that Aaron Donald could play for the Los Angeles Rams against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football, according to the NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Given the injury to Myles Garrett that will keep the Rams’ star pass rusher out for at least a month, Donald’s return […]
full_text: There is a “very, very realistic chance” that Aaron Donald could play for the Los Angeles Rams against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football, according to the NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Given the injury to Myles Garrett that will keep the Rams’ star pass rusher out for at least a month , Donald’s return to the field in Week 2 couldn’t come at a better time. Donald’s return has been THE storyline this offseason, starting with weeks of “Will he?” followed lately by ”When will he?“. With Garrett injured and L.A. looking for a rebound from their ugly Week 1 loss to the 49ers, the “when” can’t come soon enough for the Rams. Donald not expected to be limited Despite not playing in two years, Rapoport expects Donald to push for a full-time workload rather than a strict snap count once he’s on the field. “Part of me wants to say ‘expect Aaron Donald to come in and be a part-time player.’ I know the player too well. And I know human nature too well. We can talk about how he can come in and play 10 to 15 plays a game and sure, that’s a possibility,” Rapoport explained. “But with the game on the line, even in the trenches during the third and fourth quarter, he’s going to want to play.” Rapoport also said that, based on conversations he’s had with “people who know,” Donald is targeting Monday night. He goes on to say that“the goal would be to be out there against the Giants with the entire country watching.” That sounds like Hollywood doesn’t it?
author: John Newman

title: Rams vs. Giants: Sean McVay still gives L.A. an advantage
summary: The Los Angeles Rams return home for a Monday Night Football showdown against the New York Giants after disappointing in their season opener. The Rams were defeated 27-7 by the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia; struggling offensively while allowing Brock Purdy and the 49ers to control the game. Matthew Stafford finished with 155 passing […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams return home for a Monday Night Football showdown against the New York Giants after disappointing in their season opener. The Rams were defeated 27-7 by the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia; struggling offensively while allowing Brock Purdy and the 49ers to control the game. Matthew Stafford finished with 155 passing yards, while the Rams managed just 290 total yards. Meanwhile, the New York Giants enter Week 2 with momentum after a 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football . John Harbaugh secured a big divisional win in his first year as Head Coach of the Giants. Jaxson Dart threw three touchdown passes and New York’s rushing attack helped the Giants control possession and dictate the pace. Now, the Rams look to rebound at SoFi Stadium on Monday, September 21 at 8:15 p.m. ET. Here is a look at the primetime matchup. OFFENSE: RAMS Make no mistake, the Rams offense was lackluster in the season opener. However, there were glimpses in which the offense was able to move the ball with the rushing attack. The Cowboys never really tested the Giants defensive front. The Rams are fully capable of kickstarting the offense by committing to their tandem of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. That will open up the passing game for Matthew Stafford. The Giants offense is not to be taken for granted. Greg Roman has dual threats in Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo. There is a similar scheme to the 49ers and the Rams will have to slow that down and force Dart to win the game through the air. DEFENSE: GIANTS On paper, the Rams have the better defense. But execution has been lacking so far and dating back to the end of last season. It’s not just a matter of having the pieces… the pieces must be execute and be used correctly. The Rams will be without Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald’s status for Monday Night remains undetermined. The Giants meanwhile have a strong pass rush featuring Brian Burns, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Arvell Reese, and Abdul Carter. DJ Reader is also a strong presence in the interior for the Giants. The Giants defense is strong and slowed down the Cowboys offense that finished #2 last year. SPECIAL TEAMS: GIANTS John Harbaugh has a special teams pedigree. The Rams meanwhile are still trying to find stability in their special teams. COACHING: RAMS Sean McVay is a more complete coach than John Harbaugh which gives him an edge. But the area to watch here is the assistants. The Rams will want to see a bounce back performance from coaches like Kliff Kingsbury (Assistant Coach), Nate Scheelhaase (OC), and most importantly Chris Shula. Shula in particular is under a microscope. The Giants looked renewed with their new offensive identity and game plan. Dart in particular has grown in Year 2 so credit to the new regime.

title: The Giants showed they can be ‘dangerous’, will the Rams?
summary: Matthew Stafford referred to the New York Giants as a “dangerous” football team, and he further explained that every team in the NFL has a chance to be dangerous. The logic that any team can be dangerous makes sense as every team is made up of the best talent in the world. So, by extension, […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Isaiah Likely #9, Jaxson Dart #6 and Malik Nabers #1 of the New York Giants pose for a photo after the game against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matthew Stafford referred to the New York Giant s as a “dangerous” football team, and he further explained that every team in the NFL has a chance to be dangerous. The logic that any team can be dangerous makes sense as every team is made up of the best talent in the world. So, by extension, the Los Angeles Rams can be dangerous too, right? One would think, but it’s hard not to be a little concerned or maybe more than a little concerned given how disappointing they were in Week 1. Now, Myles Garrett is out too. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . For the Giants, we just saw them be very dangerous over a touted Dallas Cowboys team on Sunday Night Football. The Giants showed they had the goods in Week 1. They’ll look to do it again in Week 2. It’s not all doom and gloom, it’s one week. But the Rams haven’t shown, so far, that they have the goods to be a dangerous team for four quarters in 2026. Will they find that gear on Monday night? Tune in, find out. Matthew Stafford shares early thoughts on ‘dangerous’ Giants (ramswire) “Obviously, the young quarterback, Jaxson Dart, I thought played really well, played within himself, made some plays with his feet,” he added. “They’re a dangerous team. I think every team in the NFL, it’s what people out there forget, year in and year out going through training camps and watching preseason, think they can pick who’s gonna win every game. And that’s why we play them. You put the ball down, you go play the games. And I thought the Giants did a heck of a job the other night. I thought it was cool on the weekend of September 11th, 25 years later, for the Giants in New York City to get a win, felt right and felt great to have the NFL have something like that happen and those guys play well.” View Link NFL power rankings Week 2: There’s a new No. 1 after Rams tumble (usatoday) “ Seattle Seahawks (2): Should’ve known they’d demand and command the respect of a reigning champion that deserves the No. 1 slot until proven otherwise. Did the ‘Hawks look spectacular while winning their Super Bowl rematch with the Patriots, despite losing QB Sam Darnold five plays in to a hip injury? Nope. Did they show their typical grit and dominant defense while again vanquishing a quality opponent? Yep. And plenty of upward mobility, as they’ll tell you. “We’ll improve our operation,” said coach Mike Macdonald after the win. “(W)e can get so much better very quickly.” Good bet they will.” How did former Rams OLB Jared Verse play in his Browns debut? (ramswire) “Similar to Garrett’s first game with the Rams, Verse’s debut with the Browns was disappointing. He finished the game with four tackles, one of which went for a loss, but zero sacks or quarterback hits. According to Pro Football Focus, Verse didn’t record a single pressure and also missed one tackle.” Why Richard Sherman is concerned about Rams’ defense, and it has nothing to do with Myles Garrett injury (clutchpoints) “The corners you got are great corners, but they have played in (Steve Spagnuolo’s) system their whole career, and you don’t run to Spags’ defense…You don’t use a Corvette to Uber. You get in a Corvette, you’re racing…you pay them their money, let him do what he was doing,” he said, per Kevin Clark on X, formerly Twitter. Sherman wasn’t the only one to question how the Rams utilized new cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in their season opener, as Brock Purdy and the 49ers’ offense seemed to have no issues moving the ball down the field throughout the evening.“ Matthew Stafford downplays Rams’ big injury as ‘little bump in the road’ before four-game gauntlet (nypost) ““This is just a blip in the radar, a little bump in the road,” Stafford said on the “Let’s Go!” podcast, predicting Garrett would work diligently to return quickly. Stafford understands the expectations attached to a blockbuster acquisition, having arrived under similar pressure in 2021. He also emphasized that Garrett is “a human being, too” and said the entire team must compensate for his absence.“ Another baby girl is joining the Rams ‘Ramily’ after star player’s heartwarming Instagram announcement (nypost) “ Terrance Ferguson’s second NFL season may have started quietly, but away from the football field, the Los Angeles Rams tight end just received much bigger news. Ferguson and his wife, Sophia, announced Tuesday that they are expecting their first child, a baby girl, in early 2027. The couple shared the news on Instagram with a photograph featuring a pink Nike baby outfit, tiny pink Air Jordans, a pregnancy test, an ultrasound photo and a sign reading, “Baby Ferguson coming 2027.” Their two dogs completed the family portrait wearing matching pink bandanas declaring, “It’s a girl.” NFL Power Rankings, Week 2: Seahawks leapfrog Broncos and Rams into No. 1 spot; Chiefs hit top 10 (nfl.com) “Week 1 is complete, and as is always the case with the opening weekend of a new season, surprises appeared all over the place. The Cardinals rolled into SoFi Stadium, punched the Chargers in the mouth , stole their lunch money and ran back to the desert cackling with satisfaction. title: Las Vegas Raiders playmakers introduced themselves in win
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders 2026 season got off to a hot start with a 27-13 victory over the Miami Dolphins. Rookie head coach Klint Kubiak got his first victory. Starting quarterback Kirk Cousins threw his 299th, 300th and 301st career touchdown passes. Additionally, he also threw his first and second interceptions of the season as […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders 2026 season got off to a hot start with a 27-13 victory over the Miami Dolphins. Rookie head coach Klint Kubiak got his first victory. Starting quarterback Kirk Cousins threw his 299th, 300th and 301st career touchdown passes. Additionally, he also threw his first and second interceptions of the season as well. Cousins was marvelous in the game management role, but displayed a disturbing lack of arm strength. The ballers Ashton Jeanty ran 23 times for 102 yards and led the team in receiving. Catching six passes for 67 yards, including two touchdown passes. One was a beautifully run option route that faked out the middle linebacker and angled into the end zone. The other was a play-action pass where Cousins threw a touch pass that he caught up to and beat Jordyn Brooks to the end zone. Mike Washington Jr. made his debut in a backup role and rushed seven times for 41 yards, with the longest run of the day at 18 yards. Jack Bech caught the first touchdown pass of the year from Kirk Cousins. Michael Mayer, the recently extended $45million dollar man, caught six passes for 32 yards and was a constant force as an inline blocker as well. The hit squad Free agent edge acquisition Kwity Paye had himself a silver-and-black party and invited all of Raider Nation to attend. Not only was he the first to sack the quarterback, but he would do so multiple times and be credited with a team-leading two sacks. Maxx Crosby had the highest pass rush win rate of the entire league, winning on 33% of his rushes and finishing with 1.5 sacks in the game. If you can read body language, Crosby was happy, feeling like he finally had the help around him he so desperately had been craving. Crosby would finish the game with 1.5 sacks and was on a “play count.” Second-round draft pick free safety Treydan Stukes’s interception was the first turnover of the season. Stukes was all over the field, narrowly missing a second interception just off his fingertips later in the game. An extremely rangy safety with length and speed, Stukes displayed ball-hawking abilities that have been missing from the free safety position for years. Strong safety Jeremy Chinn forced the first fumble of the year with a clean peanut punch. Letting it be known, if the ball gets too close to him, he’s still that dude. Pairing him with Stukes, who has the traditional free safety role, allows Chinn to focus and apply himself to what he does best. Defending the box, and locking up backs and tight ends.

summary: While the team still has hope, the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice week began Wednesday without starting tight end Brock Bowers and conerback Darien Porter working on the practice field. full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the team still has hope, the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice week began Wednesday without starting tight end Brock Bowers and conerback Darien Porter working on the practice field. Before practice began, Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak said neither Bowers nor Porter will practice. However, he said he is hopeful they could practice this week before Sunday’s game at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. Like he said Monday, Kubiak said both Bowers and Porter are “day-to-day.” Bowers missed a Week 1 victory over the Miami Dolphins because of a knee surgery he had last Tuesday. Porter left the Miami game late in the fourth quarter with a foot injury. Michael Mayer started for Bowers and rookie Zeke Masses played the final 10 plays of the game for Porter. Earlier Wednesday, ESPN reported the Raiders don’t considers Bowers’ injury overly serious and he could play this week, but the team won’t allow him back until he’s completely ready. The reported estimated Bowers will miss a total of three games at maximum, thus he would surely be back for Week 4’s home game against the Chiefs. Meanwhile, Chargers’ receiver Ladd McConkey isn’t practicing Wednesday because of a ribs issue that could keep him out of Sunday’s game.

summary: It didn’t take Kwity Paye long to make an impact with the Las Vegas Raiders. full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kwity Paye #95 of the Las Vegas Raiders sacks Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images It didn’t take Kwity Paye long to make an impact with the Las Vegas Raiders. In his first game as a Raider, after signing a three-year, $48 million deal in free agency, Paye provided a major pass-rush burst. Paye had two of the Raiders’ five sacks also had six total tackles. He had a team high four quarterback hits. He and superstar Maxx Corsby showed the makings of a dynamic pass-rush tandem. Paye made his huge impact in a fairly limited role. He played in 57 percent of the snaps. So, he made a great impact base don how much he was on the field. So, he is off to a really strong start to his Raiders’ career.

title: Ashton Jeanty starts 2nd season in a big way
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and what to look for Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 73 percent of the snaps in Week 1. He averaged […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and what to look for Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 73 percent of the snaps in Week 1. He averaged 77 percent play time as a rookie. He made a big impact. He had 29 touches on 68 offensive plays and accounted for 147 of the Raiders’ 290 scrimmage yards. He is a focal point of the offense. Jack Bech: The second-round pick logged the third most snap totals of the Raiders’ receivers. He played 39 percent of the snaps in Week 1. He played more than seven times last season. Bech had three cathces for 23 yards and a touchdown against Miami. Like all of the Raiders’ receivers, Bech needs to find a way to produce more. Darien Porter: After beating rookies Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses for the starting job, the third-round pick played every snap in Week 1 until he left with an injured foot. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick didn’t play on offense after losing a camp battle to Jackson Powers-Johnson at right guard. Rogers did play six plays on special teams. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, also only played six snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, will be on the injured reserve for, at least, three more weeks. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 57 percent of the defensive snaps, the most of any defensive tackle and he played 12 snaps on special teams. He had four tackles (three assisted) against the Dolphins. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was inactive in Week 1, a healthy scratch. He was active in nine of 17 games as a rookie. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick was also a healthy scratch in Week 1. It was a bit of a surprise. He was active every games and was a core special teamer as a rookie.

The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost their opening contest this past Sunday against the Raiders in Las Vegas. Adding injury to insult, their top pass rusher — third-year player Chop Robinson — suffered a concussion in that game and now finds himself in concussion protocol as the team prepares to face the San Francisco 49ers on the road in Week Two. On Wednesday, the Dolphins released their first practice report of the week, and Robinson was listed as “limited” with his concussion. He was not known to have been suffering from symptoms at any point during Sunday’s game, so he may have reported symptoms following the conclusion of the clash — or he may have suffered the concussion during Wednesday’s practice. We should find out more tomorrow. Also on the injury report was quarterback Malik Willis — although he practiced in full with an apparent toe injury. Safety Dante Trader also practiced in full with a hamstring ailment. Longsnapper Tucker Addington (shoulder) and rookie tight end Seydou Traore (thumb/achilles) both joined Robinson in practicing in a limited fashion. Linebacker Ronnie Harrison was the only member of the active roster to miss practice while he deals with a hamstring issue. title: Vikings-Bears First Injury Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at Soldier Field. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Chicago Bears Injury Report Terms and Glossary Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at Soldier Field. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason RB Thumb DNP IR-OUT Blake Cashman* LB Wrist LP Jauan Jennings WR NIR DNP Kyler Murray* QB Concussion LP Andrew Van Ginkel* OLB Chest LP Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP Chicago Bears Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Coby Bryant* S Knee DNP IR-OUT Neville Gallimore DT Illness DNP Grady Jarrett* DT NIR-Rest DNP Darnell Wright* RT Knee DNP Kyle Monangai RB Hamstring LP Malik Mohammad* DB Ankle LP Dayo Odeyingbo* DE Shoulder LP D’Andre Swift* RB Ankle/Knee LP Ozzy Trapilo* LT Knee LP Xavier Woods DB Groin LP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Bears, starting right tackle Darnell Wright did not practice due to a knee injury, which appears to be a new injury after the Panthers game in which he played every snap. No details on the severity, but Wright not being able to go on Sunday would be a significant loss for the Bears as he is arguably their best offensive lineman. Ozzy Trapilo is working his way back from a torn patellar tendon injury and is likely to start at left tackle when he is ready. Unclear if he’ll be ready to return this week, however. Both Bears running backs were limited in Wednesday’s practice. I don’t think at this point either will not play on Sunday, but depending on the severity of their injuries, they could be less than 100% on the field. Hamstring injuries can be tricky injuries that can sometimes require rest even if they don’t seem severe to prevent a worsening condition. There is no reason to believe the other players on the list for the Bears will be unable to go on Sunday, but Thursday and Friday’s reports were provide more clarity. For the Vikings, the news of the day is Jordan Mason going on short-term IR for a broken thumb, which will sideline him for four games. That is a significant loss. Deejay Dallas is being promoted to the active roster in a corresponding move. He appears to be ahead of Demond Claiborne at this point on the depth chart. The other news is Kyler Murray being limited after suffering a concussion early in the Packers game. Reports from coaches are that he hasn’t been suffering any lingering symptoms so there is a chance he could play against the Bears on Sunday. There is a protocol that needs to be followed, but it seems his chances of playing on Sunday look more promising than they did earlier in the week. There is no reason to believe that any of the other injuries listed are significant enough to keep players out on Sunday, but once again the next two injury reports this week will provide more clarity. Stay tuned. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Vikings Place Jordan Mason on Injured Reserve
summary: The Minnesota Vikings, who already have some issues offensively, will now have to go through the early part of their season without their lead running back. The Vikings announced on Wednesday that they have placed running back Jordan Mason on injured reserve with a fractured thumb. The move means that Mason will miss the next […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jordan Mason #27 of the Minnesota Vikings runs the ball against the Green Bay Packers in the fourth quarter of a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings, who already have some issues offensively, will now have to go through the early part of their season without their lead running back. The Vikings announced on Wednesday that they have placed running back Jordan Mason on injured reserve with a fractured thumb. The move means that Mason will miss the next four games, essentially giving him five weeks to recover as the Vikings will take their bye in Week 6, making him eligible to return for the team’s Week 7 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mason led the Vikings in rushing in their 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, including a long of 28. The lead back responsibilities will now fall to Aaron Jones, who had 40 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries against his former team in Week 1. To fill Mason’s spot on the active roster, the Vikings signed DeeJay Dallas from the practice squad the active roster. Dallas, who did not have a carry against the Packers but did have one catch for one yard, could now serve as Jones’ primary backup given the fact that rookie Demond Claiborne was inactive against Green Bay. He has been primarily a special teamer over the past few seasons for a few different teams. Dallas’ spot on the practice squad has been filled by veteran Jerome Ford, who was among a group of backs the Vikings worked out earlier in the week. Ford has appeared in 57 games over the past four seasons for the Cleveland Browns but has seen his usage steadily decline over that time. He got just 24 carries for Cleveland last season, but carried the ball 204 times for 813 yards for the Browns back in 2023 and 565 yards on 104 carries in 2024. He had signed a 1-year deal with the Washington Commanders back in March but was waived with an injury settlement in mid-August. The Vikings also added a member of the league’s International Player Pathway Program to their practice squad, adding safety Maceo Beard-Aigret. Beard-Aigret, a native of Paris, France, spent time in the UFL with the DC Defenders and has also spent time in the Nordic Football League, where he was named their Defensive Player of the Year. See. . .he’s practically a Viking already! Because Beard-Aigret is a member of the IPPP, the Vikings get an exemption for him, giving them a seventeenth player on the practice squad. That should get everyone caught up on all the roster moves the Vikings have made on this Wednesday. If any other news hits the wire, we’ll have it here for you as soon as it comes down.

Ben Johnson holds a 5-1 record going up against Brian Flores which includes his years with Detroit as OC. Last year they split the games. Flores blitzed Caleb Williams 40% and masked his coverage shells in the second half of the first game enabling the Vikings to get a 27-24 comeback win. In the second game, Ben Johnson deployed the most condensed offense in the NFL that season, squeezing his formations to an average width of just 17.7 yards. These hyper-tight sets neutralized Flores’ wider blitz angles. It forced the Vikings’ cornerbacks into heavy run-defense roles and opened up quick out-breaking routes into massive voids of empty turf. Flores anticipated the adaptation and flipped his own script, abandoning his signature man-coverage blitz looks to drop into heavy-personnel zone coverage. The Bears leaned on the running game a lot more that second game. The Vikings took the lead with 50 seconds remaining but special teams gave up a 56 yard kickoff return to put the Bears in field goal position enabling them to grab a 17-16 win. Obviously, you’d like to think that both teams are a little better this year. The Bears offensive line is top 5 or 6 in the NFL and it is going to be a true test for the Vikings defensive line. They did a good job against the Panthers but the game was 31-31 in the third quarter before the Panthers fell apart. I think the sledding will be much tougher for the Bears this week. I am always going to pick the Vikings but the QB situation is concerning. I cannot say I am confident in Wentz. It seems every drop back is a hitch hitch worm ball. Then, he will make a good throw. Confounding actually. I have not seen enough of K1 to draw any conclusion. It seems the team is going to put him back in as the starter once he is good to go. The Panthers had no answer for Caleb Williams and D’Andre Swift. … Since Flores arrived in Minnesota, he has struggled against Johnson perhaps more than any other offensive coach. title: Mack Hollins’ chemistry with Drake Maye set for bigger test
summary: As Mack Hollins takes his seat in the Patriots team meeting room, it’s typically in the front row next to quarterback Drake Maye. The veteran wide receiver isn’t ready to credit his seat selection into his on-field chemistry with his quarterback, but it’s apparent Hollins has earned Maye’s trust. “I think that the quarterback knows […]
full_text: As Mack Hollins takes his seat in the Patriots team meeting room, it’s typically in the front row next to quarterback Drake Maye. The veteran wide receiver isn’t ready to credit his seat selection into his on-field chemistry with his quarterback, but it’s apparent Hollins has earned Maye’s trust. “I think that the quarterback knows he’s going to be in the right spot when he’s supposed to be there,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. Last season, Maye completed 70 percent of his passes in Hollins’ direction — the 19th-best mark for any wide receiver in football. Much of that production came in the intermediate area of the field, where the 6-foot-4 receiver was again one of the most efficient receivers in the NFL, with his size working to his advantage. “He’s obviously big in the run game, but I think Coach [McDaniels] rewards him with play-action off it. So he always says, ‘Just throw it to me on the in-cuts.’ He loves [that],” Maye said. Despite ending last season on injured reserve, Hollins put together one of the best seasons of his career posting 46 catches for 550 yards. The chemistry the two former UNC Tar Heels developed will be needed for the Patriots in the upcoming weeks after star wide receiver A.J. Brown landed on injured reserve with to a high-ankle sprain, knocking him out for at least the team’s next four games. After leading the team in receiving during the season opener, Hollins is projected to see the biggest uptick in snaps in Brown’s absence. “It’s the National Football League. They’re going to play 11 guys out there on offense, no matter who’s up, who’s down,” Hollins said. “Obviously, A.J. is a great player, and we would love to have him, but he’s not there, so there’s nothing you can do but dress 11 and get ready to work. “We’re all ballplayers. It’s not like we can’t do anything without A.J. Like I said, we’d love to have A.J. out there, but ships keep sailing.” The expanded workload is one Hollins is ready for. “Kind of a ‘I told you so’ to myself. Like the work eventually pays off,” Hollins said. “You don’t know when it is. It might not be exact at the time you wanted it to be, but if you put in the work, eventually it’ll pay off.”

title: Kevin Byard hopes to add Aaron Rodgers to his interception collection
summary: Kevin Byard has made a habit out of intercepting opposing quarterbacks. Since entering the NFL as a third-round draft pick in 2016, he has picked off 37 passes and twice led the league in interceptions. A total of 28 different QBs fell victim to his ball-hawking skills, including some of the best in the league […]
full_text: Kevin Byard has made a habit out of intercepting opposing quarterbacks. Since entering the NFL as a third-round draft pick in 2016, he has picked off 37 passes and twice led the league in interceptions. A total of 28 different QBs fell victim to his ball-hawking skills, including some of the best in the league today. One prominent name, however, is missing: Aaron Rodgers. On Sunday, Byard will have a chance to add the current Pittsburgh Steelers passer to the list. He is very much looking forward to doing so. “Definitely looking to get my first interception against Aaron Rodgers this week,” the 33-year-old explained at his locker on Wednesday. “But, no, I think it’s going to be fun, and really I just want to win. I don’t care if I don’t get an interception. If we just get some turnovers on defense, I’ll be more than happy. But it’s definitely something that’s on my mind.” Despite Byard and Rodgers being among the most experienced players in the NFL right now, they only have crossed paths three times so far. All of those meetings came when the former was with the Titans and the latter with the Packers, and none of it included Byard getting his hands on a pass. If this changes this week, Rodgers would be joining a list filled with prominent names. “Got [Patrick] Mahomes. Got Josh Allen a couple of times. Dak Prescott a few times,” Byard recalled. “It’s countless, honestly. It’s almost too much to count at this point. But I would say those are probably the top two, Josh Allen and Mahomes. I think I got Lamar [Jackson] too, so I got a lot of guys.” Byard added that he has each of the footballs he picked off lying around in his attic, even though he does not plan to change their whereabouts until after his retirement. Turning them into a leather chair was mentioned as one possible way to repurpose the balls. How big that theoretical chair will end up being remains to be seen, and also if it will ultimately end up having that long-awaited connection to Aaron Rodgers.

title: Reworked Mack Hollins contract increases Patriots cap space, makes incentives harder to earn
summary: The New England Patriots and wide receiver Mack Hollins have reached an agreement on a reworked contract that reclassified his contract incentives. The 33-year-old entered 2026 with three incentive escalators. He could earn an extra $300,000 each by catching 30 and 40 passes, respectively, and add $400,000 more if hauling in 50 passes during the […]
full_text: The New England Patriots and wide receiver Mack Hollins have reached an agreement on a reworked contract that reclassified his contract incentives. The 33-year-old entered 2026 with three incentive escalators. He could earn an extra $300,000 each by catching 30 and 40 passes, respectively, and add $400,000 more if hauling in 50 passes during the regular season. As a result of Hollins finishing his 2025 campaign with 46 catches, the first two of those levels were classified as likely to be earned and therefore counted against New England’s salary cap this year. That is no longer the case. As first reported by Joseph Pasteris, the Patriots moved the goal posts for all three of those escalators and made them fall entirely into the not likely to be earned category. According to Michael Ginnitti of Spotrac, the new incentive structure looks as follows: WR Mack Hollins: Contract incentives Maximum incentives: $1,000,000 2026: Up to $1,000,000 $300,000: 47 receptions $300,000: 50 receptions $400,000: 55 receptions Increasing all three levels — 30 to 47, 40 to 50, 50 to 55 — still keeps them within Hollins’ theoretical reach; his career-high in catches stands at 57, accomplished during his lone season with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2022. That said, reaching even the first level is now significantly more challenging considering that he finished his first year as a Patriot with the aforementioned 46 catches. It is worth noting that the renegotiation took place before the Patriots’ season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. Hollins caught four passes in that game, all while seeing teammate A.J. Brown suffer a high-ankle sprain that is reportedly expected to keep him out for six weeks . With Brown sidelined, Hollins is expected to increase his role and target share. The renegotiation is not the first time the Patriots decided to alter Hollins’ previously agreed-upon incentive structure. Back in February, they added a $400,000 signing bonus to his deal after he missed out an incentive of that value by only four catches. This latest agreement means that the Patriots created $600,000 in cap space for 2026. Hollins was originally counted against New England’s books with $5.56 million, a number that has decreased to $4.96 million.

title: Patriots vs. Steelers preview for NFL Week 2
summary: With a disappointing 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFL opener last Wednesday, the New England Patriots got their 2026 season off on the wrong foot. The goal now is to avoid an 0-2 start against a Pittsburgh Steelers team that started its own season with a victory. What can be expected from […]
full_text: With a disappointing 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFL opener last Wednesday, the New England Patriots got their 2026 season off on the wrong foot. The goal now is to avoid an 0-2 start against a Pittsburgh Steelers team that started its own season with a victory. What can be expected from the Steelers, though? Let’s take a closer look at them ahead of Sunday’s matchup. Steelers key stats The Steelers opened the 2026 season with a victory but in a competitive AFC North are currently still only ranked third. Obviously, a lot will change over the coming weeks both with this and other rankings. Record: 1-0 (3rd AFC North/8th AFC) Scoring differential: +7 (11th) Turnover differential: +1 (t-8th) Offense: 20.0 points/game (t-22nd), 264.0 yards/game (25th), 1 giveaway (t-8th), -0.251 EPA/play (30th), -0.251 EPA/dropback (27th), -0.252 EPA/run (27th) Defense: 13.0 points/game (t-6th), 238.0 yards/game (3rd), 2 takeaways (t-5th), -0.358 EPA/play (2nd), -0.638 EPA/dropback (1st), -0.113 EPA/run (13th) What the Steelers’ season opener against the Falcons shows us, though, is that the defense was ready to play. The unit dominated an Atlanta team starting its third-string quarterback and scored the decisive points when T.J. Watt returned an interception 35 yards for a fourth-quarter touchdown. Pittsburgh’s own offense, on the other hand, had a rough go itself despite ultimately doing enough to secure a W. Steelers 2026 season Even though it was not a particular display of power, the Steelers opened their first season under head coach Mike McCarthy with a win. However, it remains to be seen just how representative that performance against the Falcons actually was. Week 1: 20-13 win vs. Atlanta Falcons (1-0) The Patriots, despite their own issues in Week 1, project to be a much tougher opponent for Pittsburgh. Steelers active roster Roster up-to-date as of Sept. 16, 8 a.m. ET | *denotes nominal starter Quarterback (4): Aaron Rodgers (8), Mason Rudolph (2), Will Howard (18), Drew Allar (16) Running back (3): Jaylen Warren (30), Rico Dowdle (13), Eli Heidenreich (29 | KR) Fullback (1): Riley Nowakowski (37) Wide receiver (6): DK Metcalf (4), Michael Pittman Jr. (11), Roman Wilson (14), Germie Bernard (17), Ben Skowronek (15), Kaden Wetjen (10 | PR) Tight end (3): Pat Freiermuth (88), Darnell Washington (80), Robert Tonyan (85) Offensive tackle (3): Troy Fautanu (76 | LT), Dylan Cook (60 | RT), Max Iheanachor (71) Interior offensive line (6): Mason McCormick (66 | LG), Zach Frazier (544 | C), Spencer Anderson (74 | RG), Ryan McCollum (62), Brock Hoffman (67), Gennings Dunker (73) Interior defensive line (7): Keeanu Benton* (95), Cameron Heyward* (97), Derrick Harmon (99), Yahya Black (94), Sebastian Joseph-Day (69), Gabriel Rubio (96), Kevin Jobity Jr. (92) Defensive edge (4): T.J. Watt* (90), Alex Highsmith* (56), Nick Herbig* (51), Jack Sawyer (33) Linebacker (4): Patrick Queen* (6), Payton Wilson* (41), Cole Holcomb (55), Carson Bruener (44) Cornerback (5): Joey Porter Jr. (24), Jamel Dean* (35), Asante Samuel Jr.* (22), Daylen Everette (23), Brandin Echols (26) Safety (4): Jalen Ramsey* (5), Jaquan Brisker* (3), Rayshawn Jenkins (20), Robert Spears-Jennings (28) Specialists (3): Chris Boswell (9 | K), Cameron Johnston (19 | P/H), Christian Kuntz (46 | LS) If the game against Atlanta is any indication, the Steelers offense once again revolves around Aaron Rodgers. The future Hall of Famer dropped back to pass 42 times in the season opener and went 40-for-24 with 221 yards, a touchdown and two sacks. He did distribute the ball well, but his 5.5 yards per attempt shows that he found most of his success in the short and intermediate areas; he went 0-for-6 on passes of more than 20 yards. This, in turn, was bad news for No. 1 wide receiver DK Metcalf. Averaging a depth of target of 19.0 yards, he caught only four of nine targets for 40 total yards. The success might have been inconsistent, but the target share itself shows that Metcalf remains Rodgers’ favorite target — a group that also includes Roman Wilson, tight end Pat Freiermuth and running back Jaylen Warren. The three were targets 17 times between them. Overall, Pittsburgh’s passing game had its ups and downs last week —something that was also true for the rushing attack. The Steelers offense was okay but not particularly impressive either, even though it did enough to secure a win against a struggling Falcons team. The Patrick Graham-led defense, on the other hand, performed at a high level. The standout performer was, once again, the aforementioned T.J. Watt. Not only did he register the aforementioned pick-six, he also had a pair of sacks and an additional tackle for loss. Fellow edge A.J. Highsmith notched two sacks as well, while Nick Herbig had a pair of quarterback pressures without taking down Atlanta QB Cooper Rush. The team’s secondary held up well, even without Joey Porter Jr: the fourth-year cornerback sat out the season opener, officially due to a back injury. However, his ongoing contract dispute with the Steelers and the trade rumors surrounding him are impossible to be ignored either. His status will be one of the big stories to watch over the coming days leading up to the game. In Porter’s place, Asante Samuel Jr. got the start at outside cornerback. With Pittsburgh playing predominately zone defense versus Atlanta, he and the rest of the starting secondary — a group typically also including Jamel Dean, Jalen Ramsey and Jaquan Brisker — limited the Falcons to 143 passing yards; Brisker also caught an interception. In the kicking game, the Steelers showed some weakness: Atlanta averaged 11.0 yards on its three punt returns, and 30.8 yards on four kickoff runbacks. Kicker Chris Boswell also went just 2-of-3 on his field goal tries, even though his miss came from 56 yards out. Steelers reserves Practice squad (17): RB Travis Homer (21), RB Lew Nichols III (31), WR Max Hurleman (84), WR Brandon Johnson (89), WR Brandon Smith (89), TE Lake McRee (81), OL Steven Jones (79), OL Doug Nester (72), DT Kyler Baugh (65), DT Esezi Otomewo (93), ED Bradyn Swinson (57), LB Julius Welschof (45 | exempt), LB Jacoby Windmon (53), CB Sebastian Castro (49), CB Doneiko Slaughter (40), CB Car’lin Vigers (42), S Bishop Fitzgerald (38) IR (3): OT Jack Driscoll (68), DT Logan Lee (91), S DeShon Elliott (25) PUP (1): CB Donte Kent (34) The Steelers’ reserve lists features a familiar name: ex-Patriots fifth-round draft pick Bradyn Swinson joined the club’s practice squad after getting cut by the Patriots. Also worth pointing out here is nominal starting safety DeShon Elliott, who is starting the year on injured reserve because of a hamstring issue. Steelers coaching staff Head coach: Mike McCarthy Coordinators: Brian Angelichio (OC), Patrick Graham (DC), Danny Crossman (ST) After 19 seasons with the Steelers, former head coach Mike Tomlin announced his resignation in January. Eleven days later, Mike McCarthy was announced as his successor — reuniting him with his former Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The change up top also led to a major shakeup further down the ranks. Brian Angelichio, Patrick Graham and Danny Crossman were all hired as coordinators, replacing Arthur Smith, Teryl Austin and Danny Smith, respectively. Also part of the group is Robert Kugler, the former Patriots assistant offensive line coach who was hired by McCarthy as Pittsburgh’s new tight ends coach this offseason.

title: Drake Maye ready to bounce back against the Steelers in Week 2
summary: Drake Maye had a forgettable regular season opener, tossing three interceptions in his final three possessions to seal a 13-10 New England Patriots loss to the Seattle Seahawks. However, there is no time to dwell on those mistakes: Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers awaits. And for Maye, it will be an opportunity to bounce […]
full_text: Drake Maye had a forgettable regular season opener, tossing three interceptions in his final three possessions to seal a 13-10 New England Patriots loss to the Seattle Seahawks. However, there is no time to dwell on those mistakes: Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers awaits. And for Maye, it will be an opportunity to bounce back against a team that qualified for the playoffs in 2025. So, how is he planning on doing that? By bringing the proper mindset to the preparation. “We’re on to Pittsburgh. We have another week and another chance in this league. That’s dealing with the ups and downs in this league. That’s part of playing in the National Football League,” Maye said during an appearance on WEEI earlier this week. “It’s just part of being an athlete at a professional level. My brothers and my dad played sports in college and have done things, and you have teammates — that’s what we have teammates for and coaches. They’ve experienced it. And at this capacity it’s just different when you’re playing this position at quarterback. Your mistakes and what you do with the football is at a more drastic level because your decisions change the outcomes of games. Just realizing that and also realizing that you got to go back out there and and have a next-play mentality.” Maye started the Patriots’ season opener fairly well, executing the take-what-the-opponent-gives-you game plan and helping his team head into the fourth quarter up 10-3. However, things fell apart from that point on. By his own admission, the third-year quarterback “lost patience” and ended up costing his game a possible victory and 1-0 start to the season. Against Pittsburgh, a similar outcome would put the reigning AFC champions under quite a bit of pressure already at this early stage in the season. Maye, however, is not letting that outlook impact his work leading up to Week 2. “He’s a guy who has a lot of confidence,” said left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, who himself had a challenging first game . “We pat him on the back. We got him. We’re always riding for him, but he’s the type of guy who doesn’t really need that. He’s able to fix things on his own and come ready to work the next week.” “He’s been great,” added tight end Hunter Henry. “He sometimes takes too much of the burden. I think we all can be better. We all have to look at ourselves in the mirror. Obviously, we can’t turn the ball over, and he knows that. But, maybe if we finish a little longer, we run better routes, we block a little better, protect a little better, some of those things don’t come into play. We all have to be better. It’s not on just one guy. This is a complete team sport and that’s the beauty of football. Excited to go out there and compete with him again this weekend.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Steelers ahead of Week 2
summary: Some former New England Patriots and former Pittsburgh Steelers will meet again at Gillette Stadium. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold this September have been members of both clubs during their NFL careers. With stays ranging from days to years, here’s a glance through those ties ahead […]
full_text: Sep 21, 2025; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots linebacker Robert Spillane (14) returns an interception during the third quarter at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brian Fluharty-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Some former New England Patriots and former Pittsburgh Steelers will meet again at Gillette Stadium. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold this September have been members of both clubs during their NFL careers. With stays ranging from days to years, here’s a glance through those ties ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET home opener. PITTSBURGH Brandon Smith, wide receiver — The Patriots signed Smith to the practice squad last December. The 27-year-old wide receiver’s stay ended with his release ahead of the AFC divisional round in January. A futures contract with the Steelers arrived 48 hours later, and he was retained on Pittsburgh’s practice squad at its formation following the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline in August. Undrafted out of Iowa in 2021, Smith made previous stops with the Dallas Cowboys, DC Defenders, Arizona Cardinals and New York Jets. He has made three appearances as a standard elevation. Bradyn Swinson, outside linebacker — As the NFL’s cutdown deadline closed in, the Patriots waived a member of the 2025 draft class. Swinson subsequently went through the wire unclaimed en route to joining the Steelers’ initial practice squad. Taken in the fifth round at No. 146 overall last year, the 24-year-old former transfer from Oregon to LSU began his rookie campaign on the practice squad. He earned a promotion to the 53-man roster in November and went on to appear in four matchups, including the AFC Championship Game, handling 27 snaps on defense, 31 snaps on special teams and one solo tackle. Christian Kuntz, long snapper — Once a linebacker prospect by way of Duquesne, Kuntz entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2017 and became an August addition in Foxborough. He was waived following that year’s preseason finale as the roster reduced from 90. Kuntz proceeded to log stints with Denver Broncos, Jacksonville Jaguars and Dallas Renegades on the way to converting to long snapper. The 32-year-old has since had a hand in Pittsburgh’s operation for 86 games dating back to his 2021 debut. Kuntz has made 11 tackles on special teams during his AFC North tenure. NEW ENGLAND Robert Spillane, linebacker — Now a back-to-back Patriots captain, Spillane has appeared in 100 games, including 64 starts, since breaking into the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2018. Originally signed by the Tennessee Titans after serving as a rookie minicamp tryout, the Western Michigan product went on to spend four years in Pittsburgh while cutting his teeth on special teams and as a sub-package linebacker. He moved on to the Las Vegas Raiders in 2023 and Foxborough in 2025. Spillane’s run has spanned 602 tackles and 9.5 sacks, plus two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, eight interceptions and one touchdown return. A pick and a team-high 15 tackles were in the cards last September when the Steelers visited Gillette Stadium.

title: State of the NFC South: Week 1 recap
summary: This was an interesting week for the NFC South. Every team lost, but aside from the Falcons, the scoring was really good in this division. Tampa Bay Buccaneers For the first loss of the division, the Buccaneers had an up-and-down game. The Bengals’ defense did really well against Tampa Bay, forcing four fumbles, getting three […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 13: Head Coach Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints coaches from the sidelines during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on September 13, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images This was an interesting week for the NFC South. Every team lost, but aside from the Falcons, the scoring was really good in this division. Tampa Bay Buccaneers For the first loss of the division, the Buccaneers had an up-and-down game. The Bengals’ defense did really well against Tampa Bay, forcing four fumbles, getting three from Baker Mayfield, and completely stopping the Buccaneers’ running game. Mayfield also looked jumpy throughout the game and was sacked 4 times. Although the Buccaneers’ defense was able to completely shut down Ja’Marr Chase, Joe Burrow really controlled the game. This loss wasn’t horrible, but it also didn’t calm the calls for Todd Bowles job. Next week, the Bucs should win their game against the Cleveland Browns. Carolina Panthers The best offensive performance in the NFC South came from the Carolina Panthers, but it came with the Chicago Bears scoring a whopping 59 points. For the most part, this game was close, but the Bears just looked like the better team, and once the Panthers slowed down, the game was virtually over. Bryce Young finished with 361 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, and 1 interception. Overall, Young looked like a complete QB who could make really great throws, which was a great start to an important year for the young player. Defensively, giving up 59 points is unacceptable, even if the Bears offense is great. The Bears completely ran over this Panthers defense, and next week against the Bijan Robinson-led Falcons, good luck. Atlanta Falcons Speaking of the Falcons, they had the worst week out of the NFC South teams. After Michael Penix couldn’t play and Tua Tagovailoa was ruled out with his own injury, the Falcons had to rely on Cooper Rush, and as you could have guessed, it wasn’t great. He threw two interceptions, one being an incredible pick-six by T.J. Watt, and was sacked 4 times. Robinson carried this team in both the run and pass game, but it just wasn’t enough, even if the defense kept this team in the game. In the Panthers game, Atlanta needs to rely on the run again, but the defense will have arguably a bigger task than what they faced in Pittsburgh. New Orleans Saints Then we have the Saints. Arguably the most exciting game of the Week, New Orleans was able to back a nearly incredible comeback to win the game, but just fell short after a failed two-point conversion in overtime. I’ll revisit that two-point conversion, but for now, let’s talk about the game. The offense was horrible to start, but looked incredible in the second half (well, after the second interception). Kellen Moore must do better at adjusting because one main reason for the slow start was that the Lions were using unscouted looks against the Saints. New Orleans couldn’t adjust for most of the game, but once they did, it was over for the Lions’ defense. On defense, the Saints played really well. It’s always difficult to stop Jahmyr Gibbs, but overall, Detroit’s passing offense wasn’t good until their last drive in overtime. Now, let’s talk about the two-point conversion. You can have your criticisms about the play call, or maybe Shough’s decision (although both, I think, were perfectly fine and the Lions played it really well), but the one argument that does not make sense is that the Saints should have kicked the extra point. First, one of Kellen Moore’s main criticisms is being conservative on offense. If he had gone for the tie, it would have looked horrible. Then, even if the Saints had tied the game, the Lions still had three timeouts and around a minute and thirty seconds to get a field goal. That was also just after the extremely tired Saints defense got picked apart downfield. Don’t even get me started on the “incomplete pass” that should have been a fumble. Next week, the Saints will face another dangerous offense: the Baltimore Ravens. Hopefully they can keep the game from getting out of hand. NFC South standings: Atlanta Falcons (0-1) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1) New Orleans Saints (0-1) Carolina Panthers (0-1)
author: Caleb Yaccarino
