summary: The Philadelphia Eagles created some cap space in 2026 and 2027 by converting portions of Nolan Smith’s salaries over the next two years into bonuses, according to Spotrac. Gasp! What does it mean? Are the Eagles about to sign Zach Ertz or make another big move?! Maybe! But maybe not. It’s hardly uncommon for NFL […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 8: Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman walks the field prior to the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on December 8, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles created some cap space in 2026 and 2027 by converting portions of Nolan Smith’s salaries over the next two years into bonuses, according to Spotrac. The #Eagles converted $1.24M of OLB Nolan Smith's salary into signing bonus, creating $992k of cap space. They also converted $12.5M of his 2027 5th-year option salary into an option bonus, opening up $10M of 2027 cap space. — Spotrac (@spotrac) September 16, 2026 Gasp! What does it mean? Are the Eagles about to sign Zach Ertz or make another big move?! Maybe! But maybe not. It’s hardly uncommon for NFL teams — the Eagles included — to create cap space for flexibility purposes … and not necessarily because they immediately make a big move with the newly freed up funds. As a reminder, any cap space that the Eagles free up in the short-term will be rolled over into the future if it goes unused. So, we’ll see if Howie Roseman truly has something up his sleeve or not. Prior to this move, the Eagles were listed at $12,371,633 in 2026 cap space from Over The Cap . For context, that ranked 13th-most in the league. They had $33,104,750 in 2027 cap space, which ranked 14th-most.

title: T.J. Watt already buying into playing fewer snaps
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers kicked off the 2026 season with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons, marking their third consecutive Week 1 win, and their sixth opening win over the last seven seasons. The Steelers largely won off the strength of a vintage performance from T.J. Watt. The star edge rusher looked like his old […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: T.J. Watt #90 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers kicked off the 2026 season with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons, marking their third consecutive Week 1 win, and their sixth opening win over the last seven seasons. The Steelers largely won off the strength of a vintage performance from T.J. Watt. The star edge rusher looked like his old self, racking up two sacks, three tackles for loss, and his first career pick-six that iced the win for Pittsburgh. One of the more noteworthy developments from the game, though, was the intentional lower snap count for Watt and all three of the top edge rushers for Pittsburgh. Watt played just 38 snaps, which accounted for 63 percent of defensive snaps. For reference, he hasn’t played in lower than 82 percent of the snaps in games he’s played since 2021. Appearing on Cam Heyward’s Not Just Football podcast, Watt says he feels great and credited a lower snap count for it, “My body feels significantly better,” Watt said. “I feel way better. And you know how it is, you want to be out there every play. You feel like any play you’re not out there is a missed opportunity to make a play. Especially guys that can make splash [plays] like you can.” Watt credits linebackers coach C.J. Ah You for managing the reps of the edge rushers. “I think that’s something I didn’t really recognize was in C.J.‘s repertoire was managing reps like that,” Watt said. “I think that’s a skill, honestly, to be able to rotate us. Especially, as you know, with me, Herb, Jack, and Alex, sometimes there’s three of us out there on the field at the same time… I think that’s a skill that C.J. put on display on Sunday.” Watt and the Steelers will head to New England in Week 2 to take on the Patriots – a game they won a season ago 21-14. full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are preparing to do something they haven’t done in 318 days: play a snap of football with Tory Horton on the field. That’s after the second-year wideout was a full participant in the Seahawks’ Wednesday practice ahead of their game against NFC West rival Arizona Cardinals. Horton hasn’t played for Seattle since Week 9 of last season, when he went down with a tibia fracture and missed the team’s 2026 opener with a hamstring injury he suffered in training camp. The Colorado State grad should add more speed to the Seahawks offense, which will be run by backup quarterback Drew Lock. Starting quarterback Sam Darnold’s recovery from his mysterious glute injury continues, but he did not participate in practice on Wednesday. The other notable tidbit in the release was news about Seahawks star Nick Emmanwori. The safety was again limited in practice on Wednesday with an ankle and a new hip injury. Emmanwori missed the team’s preseason and opener after having surgery on his ankle in July , but was questionable to play last week. The team could use their Swiss-army-knife back, as it appears they’ll continue to be without safety Ty Okada as well, after he did not participate in Wednesday’s practice. Mike Macdonald did say Okada had a chance to return on Sunday, but we’ll see about his hamstring on Thursday. The Seahawks’ second wideout Cooper Kupp was limited in practice as well with a back injury, that will be one to keep an eye on. Here in the full report: With two days left before the team needs to make an official game status, the health of Emmanwori may be critical against a Cardinals team fresh off an upset victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1. Kickoff for the Seahawks game is set for this Sunday at 1:25 p.m. PDT.

full_text: Fredd Young #42, Left Inside Linebacker for the Seattle Seahawks in motion running the football during the American Football Conference West Division game against the Los Angeles Raiders on 25th October 1987 at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, California, United States. The Seattle Seahawks won the game 35 - 13. (Photo by Rick Stewart/Allsport/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have announced the passing of former linebacker, four-time Pro Bowl selection, and special teams standout Fredd Young. Drafted in the third round out of New Mexico State by the Seahawks in 1984, Young was a Pro Bowler in each of his first four seasons, as well as being named an All-Pro twice—first for his special teams as a rookie, then in 1987 as a middle linebacker. While being a special teams ace in his first season, Chuck Knox named him a starter at linebacker in his second year. Per the Seahawks site : “Young led the Seahawks in tackles in three of his four seasons in Seattle, recording at least 100 tackles in a season from 1985-1987. His best season in the NFL came in 1987 when he recorded nine sacks despite only playing in 13 games. He received Defensive Player of the Year votes to go along with a Pro Bowl and All-Pro nomination.” He was named a Seahawks Legend in 2025, the 50th anniversary of the team. Young was traded to the Indianapolis Colts for two first-round picks, which turned into Andy Heck and (through a trade up) Cortez Kennedy. Injuries led to him retiring from the NFL in 1990 after seven seasons. Fredd is survived by his wife, Michelle, as well as their children, Jessica, Freddy Jr. Matthew, Monroe, Fenix, Jeremiah and Amirah. He is also survived by his grandchildren Jaysha, Jarah, Jianika, Titus, Cassius, Justus, and Sunday. A standout linebacker who impacted the game in multiple ways, we remember the life and legacy of Fredd Young. pic.twitter.com/b5tqWldHLH — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 16, 2026 Rest in peace, Fredd Young.

title: The Seahawks have turned the turnover battle around during 11-game win streak
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks won Super Bowl 60, they became only the 10th team to end the regular season with a negative turnover differential but still hoist the Lombardi Trophy. According to Stathead, no team has ever won more games in a season despite a minus in the turnover column than the 2025 Seahawks. But […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Nehemiah Pritchett #28 of the Seattle Seahawks intercepts a pass during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Seattle Seahawks won Super Bowl 60, they became only the 10th team to end the regular season with a negative turnover differential but still hoist the Lombardi Trophy. According to Stathead , no team has ever won more games in a season despite a minus in the turnover column than the 2025 Seahawks. But that’s only part of the story when it comes to Seattle’s tale of two halves. Including last season’s playoffs, the Seahawks have won 11 straight games, tying a franchise record. Outside of their thrilling regular season win over the Los Angeles Rams, they have dominated in the turnover department. Compare that to the preceding 11 games, in which they were still 8-3, and it’s easy to see how the Seahawks have tilted close games in their favor and turned competitive games into blowouts. Seattle Seahawks turnover splits Seattle’s last 22 games Giveaways Takeaways Turnover differential Points off turnovers differential First 11 games of 2025 season 20 13 -7 -28 Current 11-game winning streak 8 22 +14 +86 That’s right. The Seahawks have kept the turnovers down, driven the takeaways up, and they’re scoring off of those takeaways at a very high clip. When they have turned it over during their win streak, they’ve allowed only 10 points off those eight giveaways. The only touchdown off a Seahawks turnover was in the second Rams game, and that was literally a 1-yard drive after a Sam Darnold interception. Of the Seahawks’ 22 takeaways on defense and special teams, 16 have resulted in at least a field goal, including 12 touchdowns. During Seattle’s 8-3 start last season, the losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Los Angeles Rams were more or less a story of untimely and costly turnovers. The Buccaneers recovered a Jalen Milroe fumble and scored a touchdown on the ensuing drive, and picked off Sam Darnold late for the winning field goal. Seattle didn’t come remotely close to forcing a turnover. Against the Rams, Darnold threw four interceptions, two of which led to touchdowns, while Seattle’s takeaway off of a Puka Nacua fumble only led to a field goal. That’s -21 points in the points off turnover column in games lost by a combined five points. Even the eight-point win over the Houston Texans could’ve been a blowout if not for a -3 turnover differential, including Darnold losing a fumble in the end zone for a touchdown. In the somewhat sputtering portion of their current 11-game winning streak, the Seahawks have repeatedly come up with turnovers to generate points. Against the Minnesota Vikings, 17 of their 26 points were off Vikings giveaways (mostly off poor Max Brosmer). After a lackluster first half versus the Atlanta Falcons, the Seahawks turned the screws and turned a 6-6 halftime score into a 37-9 blowout in large part to a trio of turnovers, which led to 17 points. Likewise versus the Carolina Panthers, they quickly turned a 3-3 third quarter score into 17-3 thanks to short fields set up by a pair of Carolina turnovers. In the nail-biter of an NFC Championship Game versus the Rams, Xavier Smith’s muffed punt gifted Seattle a short field and a Jake Bobo touchdown, which gave the Seahawks an 11-point lead and essentially provided enough cushion for the Seahawks to hang on for the win. Fast foward to the opening night win over the Patriots, the Jaxon Smith-Njigba tying touchdown is likely not possible without the Nehemiah Pritchett tip-drill interception. Julian Love’s pick off of Drake Maye gave Seattle a short field to kick the (ultimately) game-winning field goal. The final interception by Josh Jobe didn’t need anything other than a subsequent victory formation kneel. JOSH JOBE TOE TAP INT NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MrmQx0a3fo — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 And, of course, sometimes the defense does the scoring to seal a Super Bowl victory. PUNCHED OUT BY SPOON. CHENNA TO THE HOUSE. 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/32dYC8vWqN — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) February 9, 2026 After being a significant net negative in turnovers through the first 28 games under Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald, Seattle has found a way to take better care of the ball, while the league’s best defense has turned the screws to “see ball, get ball,” and keep the good times rolling.

title: Seahawks Week 2 power rankings: Seahawks stay on top, Rams slip from national glory
summary: Entering the 2026 season, the national media has been very high on the Seattle Seahawks. This is not surprising as the team just won the Super Bowl, and in a dominant way. Across the NFL landscape, the consensus top two teams appeared to be the Seahawks and their division rival, Los Angeles Rams. However, will […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks runs the ball to score a 45 yard touchdown against Kevin Byard #31 of the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering the 2026 season, the national media has been very high on the Seattle Seahawks. This is not surprising as the team just won the Super Bowl, and in a dominant way. Across the NFL landscape, the consensus top two teams appeared to be the Seahawks and their division rival, Los Angeles Rams. However, will the national media keep the Seahawks in a top position with their win over the New England Patriots? Or will the loss of Sam Darnold to a glute injury show them slip in the rankings? Let’s take a look at five national media sites power rankings ( NFL.com , CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (B/R), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. Starting with the bad news … if you can call it bad. ESPN ranks the Seahawks at number two in the NFL , keeping the same ranking they had entering the season. In this ranking ESPN notes that rookie running back Jadarian Price had a solid debut, while also giving a shoutout to safety, Rodney Thomas II who played for an injured Ty Okada. The only team ranked above Seattle was the Buffalo Bills. Entering the season, both CBS Sports and PFT had the Seahawks ranked as the number one team in the league. Their win over the Patriots did not change this. In their ranking, CBS Sports shows optimism that Seattle can keep winning with backup quarterback, Drew Lock at the helm. On the opposite end of the spectrum, despite keeping the Seahawks ranked at number one, PFT does question how long the team can keep winning with Drew Lock at the helm . Neither NFL.com nor B/R had the Seahawks ranked number one entering the 2026 season. However, after the week one victory over the Patriots, both have moved Seattle into the top spot. The biggest jump was with NFL.com , who originally had the Seahawks ranked number three entering the season. In this week’s ranking, NFL.com moved them up to number one on the list, and highlighted the team’s big second half comeback, led by three fourth-quarter takeaways, and a signature Jaxon Smith-Njigba touchdown . B/R on the other hand moved the Seahawks up from second to first . In this ranking, B/R notes that this team’s victory with Drew Lock at quarterback shows just how dominant of a team they are. An added note that B/R made was that the “Seahawks should’ve been No.1 to start out power rankings.” The team that Seattle took the top spot away from? The Los Angeles Rams – who have now fallen to sixth in BR’s rankings. I know this is a Seahawks power rankings roundup. However, it is sweet to see the Rams fall from national grace. It isn’t just BR who dropped the Rams down a lot in their rankings. ESPN also had the Rams falling from first entering the season to being ranked fourth. NFL.com dropped the Rams from first to seventh. CBS Sports dropped the Rams from second to fifth. And lastly, PFT had the Rams drop all the way from second to 11th. Overall, the Seahawks have to be feeling good after pulling off that come from behind victory with a backup quarterback, first time play-caller, and with it all being week one of the season (and banner night of all nights). The national media feels good about the team as well. Entering the season the average power ranking between the five polled sites was 1.8. This week the average power ranking between the five sites is 1.2. Although it is small, this still shows an upward trend. Despite going into next week with backup, Drew Lock, the Seahawks are still likely going to be favorites against the Arizona Cardinals. However, this is the NFL, and if Seattle is caught slipping, they may very well see a similar fall in rankings as the Rams did this past week.

(Photo by Amanda Loman/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s been a lot of talk in the news lately about AI. According to the experts on the topic, one of the existential risks is that AI becomes so smart that it reaches “superintelligence”. By that point, AI would be as much smarter than humans as humans are smarter than a chicken or a bug or a Raiders fan. That must be what Kyle Shanahan feels like when he talks football with mere mortals like us. Trent Williams spoke on an interview the other day about Kyle Shanahan’s football smarts. He said that he “came here a 10-year vet. I learned more just in that 30-minute team meeting we had with Kyle breaking down the next opponent, I learned more football in that time than I did the previous 10 years. The way he breaks it down is literally like something you’ve never seen. Down to the quarterback, where his weight is.” If a Hall-of-Fame left tackle feels like that, imagine how vast the gap is between him and non-NFL players or coaches like us? I’ve been enjoying all the tape breakdowns of the Rams game this past week. Analysts much smarter than me are pointing to all these motions and shifts and dashes and banana and it’s enough to make my head swirl. Kyle is far from a perfect coach, but we’re pretty damn lucky to have him. If only our luck with injuries could match that too…. 49ers’ De’Zhaun Stribling has surgery, to miss about 10 weeks “He sought multiple opinions to potentially rest the ankle and come back to play but ultimately decided on surgery.” 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan shares injury updates ahead of Dolphins game “Defenses play different calls based off of whether you’re in shotgun or gun. Sometimes you only do drop-back plays in shotgun and never under center and that changes entirely what a defense does. So, you just try to balance things out so you can have a threat of every type of play call and any type of look so the defense can’t eliminate certain things. And sometimes it helps with the quarterback’s rhythm a little bit more to get a smooth seven-step drop instead of a short one from shotgun.” 49ers rookie De’Zhaun Stribling to miss 10 weeks; Jake Tonges out for season “Tonges could not make it off the field under his own power. Afterward, Shanahan said Tonges’ injury was to his medial collateral ligament, along with some other “issues.” 49ers Notebook: Fred Warner reflects on ‘dream’ reunion, Jaden Dugger’s debut; Christian McCaffrey misses party “I was so excited for the flight, and then I passed out for like 13 hours,” McCaffrey shared. “So, when I woke up, there was like an hour and a half left, and I was like, ‘Damn, I think I missed the fun part.’ But it was good.” Bosa was also among the players who fell asleep pretty quickly after takeoff. But before boarding, he and his teammates had time to reflect on the win. “We all were talking a big game that we were going to hang out and enjoy it for a few hours,” Bosa said. “But we had to wait for the Rams to board [their plane], so we hung out at the airport. Some guys had some beers, maybe. And then we dozed off pretty quick. I slept the majority of it, so it was nice.” The 5 biggest surprises from the 49ers in Week 1 “Morris leaned into coverage in this game, blitzing Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford only 10.3% of the time. The 49ers were middle-of-the-pack in both 1-high and 2-high coverages. They only ran man coverage 18% of the time. Re-watching the game, it felt like Stafford had a hard time distinguishing the coverage, thanks to the safeties rotating post-snap. The 49ers rotated their safeties nearly 45% of the time last Thursday, which was the fourth-highest in Week 1…I’d argue Bosa was the 49ers’ best defensive tackle in Week 1. A couple of Bosa’s run stops came when he reduced down to a tackle in Morris’s different fronts. That allowed a guard to block him, and Bosa isn’t going to lose that battle.”

full_text: San Francisco 49ers' wide receivers #5 Mike Evans and #7 De'Zhaun Stribling talk to a member of the coaching staff during a training session at AAMI Park in Melbourne on September 7, 2026. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / -- IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE -- | AFP via Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided injury updates ahead of Wednesday’s practice. The following players won’t practice today: K Eddy Pineiro (sick) WR De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) Nick Bosa (rest) Dre Greenlaw (rest) Christian McCaffrey (rest) These players will be limited: Kyle Juszczyk (finger) George Kittle (Achilles) Khalid Kareem (shoulder) Keion White (back) Shanahan said the team will place Stribling on the Injured Reserve list later this week after he needed ankle surgery. Stribling is expected to miss about 10 weeks. Shanahan wasn’t “exactly sure” about the timetable but said it’d be “close to 10 weeks.” Here’s an excerpt from Ian Rapoport: “With new information early this week, the 49ers and De’Zhaun Stribling made the smart decision and opted to repair his deltoid rupture. Surgery will allow a complete recovery, and Stribling should be back in late November or Early December.” Shanahan was asked if Stribling exacerbated his injury when he went back onto the field. Here’s how the 49ers head coach responded: “No, it just didn’t check out as an Achilles. It didn’t check out as a certain ankle, the stuff that they did. They went through the normal protocols. He was past them, but when he ran a certain route, it really showed. The one you guys saw on TV that he collapsed on. It was going to happen regardless.” Shanahan said he believes the 49ers have as much depth at wide receiver as any team in the league, so the team doesn’t need to make any moves in the interim. Shanahan didn’t share the same optimism for tight end Jake Tonges, who will miss the remainder of the season with an MCL injury. There may be some concerns about the 49ers’ recovery process after their trip from Australia. Shanahan said he did not modify the upcoming week of practice: “No, we didn’t have to modify it, just because we got those off days. We had a bonus practice on Monday, which really wasn’t one. The coaches didn’t even go out. We met and did all the film with the guys, like a normal Monday. Dustin, the strength staff, just worked those guys out. And then it was normal today, so we’re back to a truly normal Wednesday. It actually is out normal schedule now because our times were a little bit different in Australia with the travel to the practice field and stuff. So, it’s real normal now. Shanahan said he “felt like crap all weekend.” He said it took a couple of days, but he was good by Monday. There wasn’t a consensus among the players. It took some a couple of days, while others felt fine right away. According to Shanahan, “we’re definitely good by now.”

title: 49ers fact or fiction: Is the offensive line a top-10 unit?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers spent their offseason wondering who would start at left guard after Ben Bartch and Spencer Burford departed in free agency. Truthfully, since Aaron Banks departed for Green Bay, the left guard position has been a revolving door. Last season, as a rookie, Connor Colby got some run, but earned a mixed […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers spent their offseason wondering who would start at left guard after Ben Bartch and Spencer Burford departed in free agency. Truthfully, since Aaron Banks departed for Green Bay, the left guard position has been a revolving door. Last season, as a rookie, Connor Colby got some run, but earned a mixed bag of results. The 49ers drafted Carver Willis and signed Robert Jones to add to the competition, but Colby got the nod in Australia, and his play was very solid. Overreacting to one week of football isn’t wise, but the 49ers have been ranked as a top-ten offensive line group this offseason nearly everywhere, and a great showing against the Rams only supports that thinking. Pro Football Focus ranks the 49ers seventh after Week 1. The 49ers’ offensive line had a strong showing in the win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne. Connor Colby got the start at left guard and was the only player in the group to produce a PFF Pass Block Win Rate below 90.0%, while no member of the unit allowed more than two pressures. The 49ers were solid as run-blockers, too. Colby had the highest negatively graded play rate in the group at 35.7%, but he also had the highest positively graded play rate as a run-blocker at 21.4%. Much has been made about PFF and its grading system, but SIS Data Hub believes the 49ers offensive line was excellent. Jake Brendel, Dominick Puni, and Colby all have a zero percent blown-block rate, with Colton McKivitz and Trent Williams drawing two blown blocks each, one pass block and one run block. The trio of Brendel, Puni, and Colby is also in the top 12 for total points earned. Now, the Rams were neutralized, and Myles Garrett was injured, but the 49ers should expect performances like this when the game plan is to get the ball out quickly and establish the running game. The bump in run blocking is a welcome sight and comes in addition to the new “dash” or “banana” motion, whichever you prefer, helping to create new window dressing and angles. It remains to be seen if this will continue for the 49ers offensive line, but they are a top-ten unit. The hope is that continuity will build and cohesion will come at the right time, especially against the NFL’s top defensive units.

title: The 5 biggest surprises from the 49ers in Week 1
summary: We asked San Francisco 49ers fans what they thought were the biggest surprises from the Week 1 mashing of the Rams. There was no shortage of answers, because there was no shortage of ways the Niners stood out, both individually and as a team. Today, we’ll highlight the biggest surprises from the Niners Week 1 […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images We asked San Francisco 49ers fans what they thought were the biggest surprises from the Week 1 mashing of the Rams. There was no shortage of answers, because there was no shortage of ways the Niners stood out, both individually and as a team. Today, we’ll highlight the biggest surprises from the Niners Week 1 win, based on your responses. We narrowed them down from 50. The 49ers offensive line shines OL play. I can’t remember the last time I saw them absolutely bully a defensive line, much less one supposedly as amazing as this year’s Rams, in the way they did. — SoCal delenda est🏜🌉 (@The530Bro) September 15, 2026 Trent Williams played like a Hall of Famer. That’s where he set the bar. But overall, each player consistently won their individual matchups. As a unit, they kept the quarterback upright in pass protection and excelled on the ground. The running backs weren’t touched, on average, until 2.79 yards downfield. That was the best mark of any team in the NFL in Week 1. The offense averaged 3.17 yards needed to gain on third downs. And they only had 12 of those. Those numbers show an offensive line dominating. Raheem Morris’s coverage schemes Not so much surprised but impressed by Raheem coverage schemes. Matt looked lost — DS (@DSLION904) September 15, 2026 Morris leaned into coverage in this game, blitzing Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford only 10.3% of the time. The 49ers were middle-of-the-pack in both 1-high and 2-high coverages. They only ran man coverage 18% of the time. Re-watching the game, it felt like Stafford had a hard time distinguishing the coverage, thanks to the safeties rotating post-snap. The 49ers rotated their safeties nearly 45% of the time last Thursday, which was the fourth-highest in Week 1. Here’s a breakdown of the coverage usage, with two plays unknown: Cover 3 : 9 plays, 66.7% success rate (6 of 9) Cover 6 : 9 plays, 77.8% success rate (7 of 9) Cover 1 : 5 plays, 80.0% success rate (4 of 5) Cover 4 : 4 plays, 25.0% success rate (1 of 4) Stafford was forced to check the ball down time and time again. He had three completions on ten attempts over 10 yards, with one interception. That tells me Stafford wasn’t seeing the field well and didn’t have anywhere to throw the ball. Kaelon Black in the game early Honestly, that Coach didn't overuse CMC — Chuck Beretz (@ChuckBeretz) September 15, 2026 Arguably the biggest surprise of the game came when Kyle Shanahan used his rookie running back on the first drive of the game. Black had a carry and a reception on the first drive. And he came onto the field for the second drive. Nobody in their right minds would have predicted that Black would have more carries than Christian McCaffrey in Week 1. McCaffrey ran 18 routes compared to Black’s 10. The game script set up perfectly for Black to get snaps in the fourth quarter. You don’t need McCaffrey taking any unnecessary hits. It’s one week, but that’s the kind of rotation that’ll keep McCaffrey on the field all season. Deebo Samuel’s impact Why we haven't been using Deebo in kick returns since he was a rookie. — JayJayLockerius (@JayLockeriusII) September 14, 2026 Deebo looking svelte, in shape, and doing his thing….no drop off — Chili Dog (@HighOnLiberty) September 14, 2026 Deebo looked like Deebo, with 62.5% of his receiving yards coming after the catch. He was involved on quick throws, he lined up in the backfield, and he made himself available to Brock Purdy on a scramble drill that led to a touchdown. I thought Deebo changed the game with his kickoff return to open the third quarter. It was a chance for the Rams to take control of the game, but once the Niners got the ball around midfield, that was all she wrote. Deebo was built to return kickoffs under the new rules. My bold prediction is that he’ll finish in the top five in average among all kickoff returners this season, which is great news for the offense. Nick Bosa didn’t miss a beat For me it was how well Nick Bosa played from the first snap! I thought he might be done but he shut my mouth. He played ferocious and fast. The OLine was surprising as well. That and how fast that whole Defense looked. IMO — Madlock (@kevinlmatlock) September 15, 2026 Nick Bosa has only been practicing for a maximum of two weeks. So for him to be a dominant force in under 60% of the snaps is something that feels like it’s being taken for granted. Now, it helps that the Niners didn’t get into a shootout where they’d be on the field for 70+ snaps. Bosa played 33 snaps, but recorded four run stops that were all impact plays, and made Stafford pay the price on the first play of the game. I’d argue Bosa was the 49ers’ best defensive tackle in Week 1. A couple of Bosa’s run stops came when he reduced down to a tackle in Morris’s different fronts. That allowed a guard to block him, and Bosa isn’t going to lose that battle. Surprise, surprise, it helps to have a Defensive Player of the Year candidate back on the field.

title: 49ers in review: We’re buying stock in the secondary
summary: As we get ready to turn the page to the Miami Dolphins, let’s take one last look at the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 1 undressing of the Los Angeles Rams. What are some things that happened in Australia that could be things to watch for as the 49ers return stateside? What players stood out? Which […]
full_text: (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we get ready to turn the page to the Miami Dolphins, let’s take one last look at the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 1 undressing of the Los Angeles Rams. What are some things that happened in Australia that could be things to watch for as the 49ers return stateside? What players stood out? Which play was the most impressive? Let’s officially close the book on Week 1 with our first game in review of 2026: Nick Bosa: run stopper? The returns of Fred Warner and Nick Bosa were the two biggest headlines for the defense heading into Week 1. Warner lived up to his standard, exiting Week 1 as the most impressive 49er in Australia. Bosa, however, left a bit to be desired. While the 49ers pass rush created 14 pressures on 28 Rams pass attempts, there was little impact felt from the front four. Bosa was no exception, collecting just one pressure and one quarterback hit on 20 pass-rush snaps. But surprisingly, it wasn’t Bosa’s pass rush ability that was the story; it was his play against the run. While the 49ers defense as a whole struggled against the run, allowing 122 yards on 29 carries, Bosa’s performance especially stood out. Bosa led the 49ers with four run stops on 16 run-play snaps, responsible for a third of the 49ers’ run stops on his own. Bosa’s pass rush ability will come around at some point as he’s returning from the season-ending injury suffered in 2025, but if Week 1 run-stopper Bosa can show up consistently, it would only add depth to the already uber-talented defensive end. A two-player running back room Maybe what happened on Thursday night was a blip and Kaelon Black will never out-carry Christian McCaffrey again. But the fact that it’s something that happened in Week 1 makes it significant. Here’s a list of games where a 49ers running back not named Christian McCaffrey has 14 or more carries in a game where McCaffrey played: Elijah Mitchell, 18 carries – Week 10 2022 Elijah Mitchell 17 carries – Week 17 2023 Kaelon Black 14 carries – Week 1 2026 And Black was deserving of those carries. The rookie gained 65 yards on his 14 attempts, looking explosive with the ball in his hands, with his longest run of the night a 14-yard carry on the 99-yard touchdown-scoring drive. While Black impressed in his debut, McCaffrey showed why he’s still the top back in the offense. On four fewer carries, McCaffrey gained more yards than Black, with a 10-carry, 68-yard performance in the season opener. McCaffrey also added five receptions for 20 yards while Black finished with one for five yards. This is likely the most interesting thing to watch over the next few weeks. Was it a coincidence that Black out-carried McCaffrey, or was it intentional? Position Group of the Week Several position groups could have earned this spot. We just discussed the running back room. The receiving corps was just as solid. And Fred Warner’s performance alone could have given it to the linebackers. But I am going to go with the cornerback group as the inaugural position group of the week. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are as fearsome of a duo the league has to offer, and the 49ers cornerbacks held them quiet. Deommodore Lenoir was targeted four times against Nacua, allowing 28 yards on three receptions, with the biggest blemish being a 23-yard reception allowed. Other than that, Lenoir was solid against the Rams’ top receiver. On the other side, Renardo Green handled his business. When in coverage against Adams or Nacua, Green was targeted three times, allowing two receptions to Adams for 23 yards. But the lone time Matthew Stafford targeted Nacua with Green in coverage, Green hauled in the first interception of his career. Jack Jones and Upton Stout contributed as well, with the duo targeted seven times against Nacua and Adams, allowing just two receptions for eight yards, with Jones having two near-interceptions but settling with a pair of pass breakups. Because of the corners, Stafford completed just 60 percent of his passes, which is a pretty significant percentage for the quarterback from 2025. In the four games Stafford completed 60 percent or less of his passes in 2025, the Rams went 1-3. The 49ers’ cornerback play against Stafford and his top-two targets was just as important as anything else that led to the 49ers’ 20-point win. Touchdown of the Week There are three very good choices for this category, with Brock Purdy having a trio of highlight throws going for scores. The first a beautiful deep throw to Demarcus Robinson for a 39-yard touchdown followed by a connection with Mike Evans taking advantage of a one-on-one in a goal line situation. But this week’s touchdown of the week goes to Purdy’s third and final touchdown pass: Slimebo's back in business 😤 📺 Netflix pic.twitter.com/D8bs7y89AJ — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 11, 2026 For multiple reasons, it earns the nod, so let’s start with Purdy. He starts with an excellent slide to the right outside of the pocket the second he feels pressure. But then there’s the throw. As he’s rolling to his right, he puts the ball perfectly over a pair of Rams defenders, perfectly leading Deebo Samuel into the open spot of the end zone for the score. And that’s the other reason this particular score earns touchdown of the week: it’s not any Deebo Samuel, but it’s No. 19, Deebo Samuel. Nostalgia is what the Robinson and Evans scores are lacking. It was the perfect exclamation point for Samuel’s return to San Francisco, closing a six-catch, 48-yard day with his first touchdown as a 49er since December 30, 2024. Oh, and it was also the dagger in a rout of the Rams.

title: 49ers considered favorites to win NFC West after Week 1
summary: Through one week, the NFC West is 3-1, with the lone loss being the Los Angeles Rams, who fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. While the spread was 3.5-points, not many had faith in the 49ers, myself included, after the Rams added a ton of star talent in the offseason, making them the […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through one week, the NFC West is 3-1, with the lone loss being the Los Angeles Rams, who fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. While the spread was 3.5-points, not many had faith in the 49ers, myself included, after the Rams added a ton of star talent in the offseason, making them the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl. With the Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks still around with their nucleus of players, they were also considered above the 49ers for both the NFC West and the Super Bowl. But things have quickly shifted after Week 1, when the 49ers beat the Rams 27-7 and showed the potential of what their team can do when healthy. According to ESPN, the 49ers have jumped from third to first in NFC West odds, climbing up to +160 odds to win the division. The Seahawks are shortly behind at +175, and the Rams, who were hovering around +100 to begin the season, are now third at +205 odds. However, that hasn’t changed the big-picture outlook as much. ESPN still has the Rams as the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl at +650, while the 49ers are tied for the fifth-best odds with the Kansas City Chiefs at +1400. Ahead of them are the Baltimore Ravens (+900), Buffalo Bills (+950), and Seattle Seahawks (+1100). It’s interesting that oddsmakers don’t see the Rams as the NFC West division winner, but they do still have them as the favorite to win the Super Bowl. The 49ers, however, do have better odds to win the NFC than the Seahawks. Los Angeles is seen as the favorite to make the Super Bowl out of the NFC at +455, while the 49ers jump up to second with +550 odds. The Seahawks are shortly behind at +580, while the Philadelphia Eagles (+710) and Chicago Bears (+800) round out the top five. There have been some early injuries shifting the tune in the NFC West. Los Angeles will be without star pass rusher Myles Garrett for at least the next month after placing him on Injured Reserve. Of course, Aaron Donald has yet to play as well. Sam Darnold is dealing with a hip injury and will also be out, making Drew Lock the starter for the upcoming weeks. The 49ers have dealt with their mass of injuries already, with players like Ricky Pearsall and Alfred Collins set to miss the season, but their core group of stars was all healthy for Week 1. San Francisco will first face the Seahawks on the road in Week 5 after three straight home games against the Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, and Denver Broncos. That could be the next major game that shifts the division odds one way or another, and could also be around when Sam Darnold returns.

title: 49ers News: Welcome to the Bay, McKinnley Jackson!
summary: The Miami Dolphins are begging to be overlooked. A trap game this early sounds insane, I know, but after coming back from such a long flight and an emotional win… going against an opponent that doesn’t seem like much… let’s not forget that the Dolphins are still an NFL team. The 49ers are going against […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX-DECEMBER 9: McKinnley Jackson #93 of the Cincinnati Bengals looks on during the game at AT&T Stadium on December 9, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are begging to be overlooked. A trap game this early sounds insane, I know, but after coming back from such a long flight and an emotional win… going against an opponent that doesn’t seem like much… let’s not forget that the Dolphins are still an NFL team. The 49ers are going against a young, hungry, mobile QB-led team with nothing to lose and everything to gain from embarrassing the 49ers. They started rallying on the Raiders before the Raiders put them away. WR Caleb Douglas seems like the real deal, so the 49ers secondary can’t be coasting just because they shut down Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Everybody better lock in at practice today. 49ers Week 1 Tape Takeaways: Motion commotion (paywall) “The 49ers looked coordinated in the run game. They went back to their zone-heavy roots, and I wonder if leaning on Dash helped simplify things. It made things easier for the offensive line and made every run look the same (sometimes they were). San Francisco consistently attacked the Rams’ weak linebacker corps. The coordination on help blocks and second-level climbs was outstanding. Colby looked weak at times, and allowed a team-high six run stops (my measure), but he also had great moments. This is, at this moment, a legitimately good offensive line. A healthy Trent Williams and Dom Puni make a massive difference…The 49ers didn’t really go to dime looks until the fourth quarter, once the Rams had all but abandoned their run game and 13 personnel looks. I love it. Raheem Morris used the 49ers’ best DBs, letting Deommodore Lenoir thrive in that Star/Jackal/Apex/positionless position that’s really just a second nickel. We’ll see how much they lean on dime going forward, but I’d be stunned if this was a one-off experiment. It was too effective….Also, I enjoyed how effective the 49ers were at running stunts. They were far cleaner than in the past. It created a lot of effective disruption, and helped limit some of the wear and tear Nick Bosa would face with head-up rushes….Lastly, George Kittle. He doesn’t look near where he was last year before his injury and I wouldn’t expect him to. I say that while also noting that he had some nice blocks on the move. But he can’t really power off his surgically-repaired right leg.” 49ers mailbag: What’s next after De’Zhaun Stribling’s and Alfred Collins’ injuries? (Paywall) “But I still think the bigger need is at defensive end. Though Mykel Williams is technically a defensive end, he’ll be able to play a lot of defensive tackle snaps — especially on obvious passing downs — when he’s back after Week 4. The same goes for Keion White. There are also a lot more quality defensive ends available, a list that includes Haason Reddick, Leonard Floyd and Joey Bosa. Here’s how I’d classify them: If the team wants another Romello Height-like player or is worried it’s not getting enough out of Height, Reddick would be a good solution. He’s a lighter-bodied edge player who’s played in systems similar to the one defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is running this year. If the team wants a dependable, every-down defensive end, Floyd is the answer. He’s familiar to both the 49ers’ brass and Morris. Yes, Floyd turned 34 last week and had only 3.5 sacks last year for Morris’ Falcons. But the 49ers aren’t in a position to look down their noses at 3.5 sacks. Their sack leader last year had four. If the 49ers want a second-half-of-the-season boost, how about Bosa? The team might be worried about how Nick Bosa’s oft-injured older brother might hold up over a 17-game season. But an eight-game season seems reasonable. Joey had five sacks and 54 quarterback pressures for the Bills last year. That’s not elite, but it’s better than what the 49ers have opposite Nick at the moment. Another interesting option is Yetur Gross-Matos, whose recent stint with the 49ers was marred by a knee issue. Gross-Matos didn’t play or practice much, but when he was on the field, he made an impact. His 16.3 percent pass-rush win rate last season was second best on the team behind Bosa’s 20 percent rate. Gross-Matos is currently rehabilitating from that knee injury and isn’t ready to play. That could change by midseason.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Will 49ers’ De’Zhaun Stribling need an ankle procedure? Surgeons explain factors at play (paywall) “To be clear, most deltoid ligament sprains heal on their own. And that could be the case with Stribling. But the nature of the injury is why athletes are sidelined for at least a month — with some recoveries requiring up to six weeks — if surgery isn’t required. Jung and Dr. Nicholas Strasser, a foot and ankle surgeon who is consultant to the Tennessee Titans and Vanderbilt University, explained that the deltoid ligament is a stronger ligament than the two on the outside of the ankle that are associated with low and high ankle sprains. As a result, it requires more force to damage the deltoid. And more force means more trauma to the ankle. …Jung said Stribling would have already had a procedure if he had “gross instability,” but it’s likely premature to say whether rest and rehabilitation will restore whatever instability Stribling is experiencing. Stribling’s stability will be determined by how the fibers in his torn ankle heal. “If they heal a little bit stretched out, or in a way that it just doesn’t have enough support to it, that could lead to surgery,” said Strasser, an assistant professor of orthopedics at Vanderbilt. “Especially because it’s on the inside part of the ankle and you’re often cutting and pushing off that a little bit more. The stress in that area is a little bit more extreme.” If Stribling needs surgery, his recovery would last three to four months, which would sideline him for most or all of the regular season.” 49ers overreactions: Will 2026 NFL season be a touchdown frenzy for Brock Purdy? “Mike Evans and George Kittle are the most-likely players to have 10 or more touchdown catches. Christian McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel are candidates to team up with Purdy for a lot of scoring receptions, too.” 49ers find needed balance in run game with McCaffrey, Black “From midfield, Brendel turned toward coach Kyle Shanahan on the sideline and waved his arms to suggest he wanted to run the ball, run it again and keep running it until the Rams showed they could at least slow it down. “After a few of those good chunk run plays hit, I’m looking right at Kyle, ‘Let’s go,'” Brendel said. “Let’s just keep going. Let’s keep dialing them up.” Shanahan apparently agreed with Brendel’s assessment. The success of those plays only yielded more runs, and by the end of San Francisco’s 27-7 win, it had 30 attempts for a robust 5.8 yards per rush….San Francisco also took advantage of a schematic curveball from the Rams. According to Brendel, the Niners spent the week preparing for plenty of five-man fronts — similar to what Los Angeles threw at them in recent matchups. Brendel was surprised when the Rams not only played four down linemen more frequently but were also often in nickel packages (five defensive backs). “The way that they chose to play us on defense schematically we weren’t really expecting,” Brendel said. “Most teams are a little bit more scared of our wide zone and our run game.” 49ers’ Renardo Green credits experience for his big interception vs. Rams “I knew the way I played it, I knew he (Stafford) didn’t see me, and even if he did, he didn’t think I could get to it,” Green told NBC Sports Bay Area. “He underestimated my abilities and what I could do, and he paid for it. title: Are you willing to be patient with the Titans?
summary: The Tennessee Titans had the worst opening day imaginable. There weren’t many fans who had hope after a rough preseason, but the ones who did lost it after the 23-10 loss. It wasn’t just that they lost; it was the fact that they looked completely overmatched in every phase of the game. Robert Saleh and […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans looks on prior to the game against the New York Jets of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans had the worst opening day imaginable. There weren’t many fans who had hope after a rough preseason, but the ones who did lost it after the 23-10 loss. It wasn’t just that they lost; it was the fact that they looked completely overmatched in every phase of the game. Robert Saleh and his staff are preaching patience. That’s easy for him to say. He has only been here for about nine months. It was just one week for him, but for those of us who have suffered through the last three seasons of Titans football, it just felt like a continuation of those dreadful years. Things don’t get any easier for Saleh and his team on Sunday. The Philadelphia Eagles are coming to Nashville on a day when the forecasted high is 98 degrees. There will probably be about 40,000 people there, and I’d wager at least 25,000 of them will be Eagles fans. The Titans will most likely be 0-2, and Saleh will be saying that it is only two weeks. How long are you willing to give them? For me, I just need to see some progress. I need to see Cam Ward look like he has the potential to develop into a franchise quarterback. I need to see the offensive line take a step forward. I need to see Saleh’s defense play with “all gas and no brakes.” Seeing at least one of those things will give me some hope that things are actually building toward success. Progress is required for patience. How patient are you willing to be?

title: Titans must start Cedric Gray, Anthony Hill at LB in Week 2
summary: The only positive takeaway from the Tennessee Titans’ Week 1 blunder was the performance of rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. The 60th overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft recorded a team-high 16 tackles. The Titans need to start Hill and Cedric Gray at linebacker versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. Hill started in […]
full_text: Aug 4, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans linebacker Anthony Hill (53) talks with the media during training camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The only positive takeaway from the Tennessee Titans’ Week 1 blunder was the performance of rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. The 60th overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft recorded a team-high 16 tackles. The Titans need to start Hill and Cedric Gray at linebacker versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. Hill started in place of Gray, who failed to clear concussion protocol in time for Week 1 after suffering an off-field leisure accident . That put Hill in the starting lineup next to veteran Cody Barton. The rookie took full advantage of the opportunity. Head coach Robert Saleh confirmed that Gray has already cleared protocol during his Monday press conference. That opens up the possibility for the Titans to start Gray and Hill in Week 2. They must be bold enough to send Barton to the bench, especially versus an athletic Eagles offense. Hill didn’t just register 16 tackles. He appeared to have forced and recovered a fumble in Jets territory when he punched the ball loose from sophomore tight end Mason Taylor. The refs called an incomplete pass on the field, and surprisingly upheld that call once Saleh challenged it. Even with his takeaway confusingly stolen from him, Hill still made impact plays. The former Texas standout had a really nice pass breakup on a peanut-punch, breaking up a pass for a Jets running back on a wheel route. Hill also shoved Geno Smith out of bounds short of the sticks on a third-and-short, forcing a fourth down. The rebuilding Titans are still stacking young talent. They aggressively traded up for Hill, nabbing him with a second-round pick they initially didn’t have. That decision paid immediate dividends in Week 1. The Titans were terrible, but Hill was excellent. Hopefully he starts opposite Gray versus the Eagles in Week 2.

title: Commanders film session: Scott Turner breaks down Washington offensive issues
summary: Washington Commanders starting center Nick Allegretti has taken plenty of criticism on social media following the team’s 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. But a closer look at Washington’s offensive performance reveals that their problems went far beyond Allegretti. Former Washington offensive coordinator Scott Turner joined the latest Trap or Dive Podcast for a live […]
full_text: Washington Commanders starting center Nick Allegretti has taken plenty of criticism on social media following the team’s 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles . But a closer look at Washington’s offensive performance reveals that their problems went far beyond Allegretti. Former Washington offensive coordinator Scott Turner joined the latest Trap or Dive Podcast for a live film session, breaking down Washington’s offensive performance against Philadelphia and identifying what went right, but more importantly, where things went wrong. Washington struggled to generate explosive plays, but the opportunities were there. On one play, the Eagles failed to account for receiver Terry McLaurin, creating a potential touchdown opportunity. However, immediate pressure from Jordan Davis disrupted the play before Washington could capitalize. Turner and the Trap or Dive guys break it all down right here, and several other key plays below: Breaking down how Nick Allegretti could have defended Jordan Davis better with @ScottTurner https://t.co/PBRMvjErpN pic.twitter.com/k3Y1rQyPBJ — Jamual (@LetMualTellit) September 16, 2026 The receivers also contributed to the offense’s early struggles, and may have had difficulty processing Philadelphia’s coverages. In turn, receiver Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo took poor releases that effectively killed a play before it ever had a chance. One of the issues Washington’s offense had Sunday came down to receivers taking more efficient releases. Scott Turner broke down how one play failed because of that, and what Stefon Diggs and Chigg Okonkwo could have done better. @TraporDive | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/yjDiehzDlI — Jamual (@LetMualTellit) September 16, 2026 Quarterback Jayden Daniels also had moments where he could have helped create more opportunities. Daniels undoubtedly faced a lot of pressure. In fact, it came on 50% of his dropbacks . Still, there were plays where staying in the pocket for another second, even at the risk of taking a hit, could have allowed him to connect with his receivers for potentially explosive gains. These moments became a major focus of the film session with Turner, as we dissected where Daniels could have trusted the pocket, helped his receivers and given the offense a better chance to make plays. The good news for Washington is that many of these mistakes can be corrected through film study, communication and mental reps. The bigger question is whether Washington can correct them quickly enough. One thing is certain: Washington cannot afford another slow start offensively against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. Dallas has a high-powered offense capable of putting points on the board, making execution from the start critical if Washington wants to keep pace. full_text: The Commanders emerged from training camp in solid shape. While they put a few key players on injured reserve, all 53 members of the active roster were available for the regular season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles. They won’t enter Week 2 that way. A few key Commanders got banged up in that 24-22 loss to Philly , putting their status in some doubt. Tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) didn’t practice on Wednesday, the first full workout leading up to Sunday’s road test against the Dallas Cowboys. full_text: The Washington Commanders are back at practice, and it’s Dallas Cowboys week. Both teams are coming off disappointing division losses and will be looking to climb out of the NFC East basement. Washington announced several roster moves before today’s practice, including placing LB Jordan Magee (hamstring) on injured reserve , and signing veteran iOL Lucas Patrick . Dan Quinn said Tyler Owens will practice today after injuring his ankle during a return on Sunday. LB Frankie Luvu ( groin ) and TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) were also injured on Sunday, and won’t practice today. Quinn said there’s some uncertainty on their availability vs the Cowboys, and they would know more later in the week. Quinn said Mike Sainristil’s play was unacceptable after multiple mental mistakes led to Eagles’ scores. He focused on fixing those mistakes today, and said he still has a lot of confidence in the third-year corner, and said he’ll be leveling up. Fans waiting for Trey Amos to return from injured reserve to replace Sainristil in the lineup might have to wait longer than they want. Amos broke his fibula last November, and then suffered an ankle injury to the same leg after he returned during training camp. Quinn said that even after the four-game minimum games missed for going on IR he would still need to practice and ramp up for a return to the field. title: Commanders roster moves: Backup linebacker moved to injured reserve
summary: Jalen Hurts’ 22-yard scramble on a key 3rd-and-18 was impactful in Philadelphia’s 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders. It was longer lasting for Washington than just one game. Linebacker Jordan Magee got hurt on that play, suffering a hamstring strain that will keep him out for some time. The Commanders placed him on injured reserve […]
full_text: Jalen Hurts’ 22-yard scramble on a key 3rd-and-18 was impactful in Philadelphia’s 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders. It was longer lasting for Washington than just one game. Linebacker Jordan Magee got hurt on that play, suffering a hamstring strain that will keep him out for some time. The Commanders placed him on injured reserve on Wednesday afternoon, meaning he’ll miss at least four games while recovering from the ailment. Perhaps the play of the game. 3rd & 18 and Jalen Hurts converts for 22 yds. Cannot happen. pic.twitter.com/OuxYeiVaTT — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) September 14, 2026 The previously reported Lucas Patrick signing was the corresponding move. While Magee is the fourth linebacker in Washington’s deep position group, his loss remains a blow on defense and special teams. This loss is magnified by Frankie Luvu’s own hamstring issue. His injury will keep him out of Wednesday’s practice and his status for Week 2 at Dallas is up in the air. Sonny Styles and Leo Chenal are the top healthy linebackers, with Kain Medrano as a reserve on the active roster. The Commanders also have Ale Kaho and Austin Keys on the practice squad . Washington could elevate one of those two without having to alter the 53-man roster for the Cowboys game.

title: Commanders mailbag: Discussing Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels, Mike Sainristil
summary: The Commanders showed well in Philadelphia but not well enough to beat the Eagles. That Week 1 affair proves that every snap counts, with but a few explosives allowed and offensive opportunities missed separating a win from a loss.   Washington’s intriguing to be sure, with plenty left to learn about this group as we […]
full_text: The Commanders showed well in Philadelphia but not well enough to beat the Eagles. That Week 1 affair proves that every snap counts, with but a few explosives allowed and offensive opportunities missed separating a win from a loss. Washington’s intriguing to be sure, with plenty left to learn about this group as we move forward. There are plenty of questions about the state of the franchise and what must be better heading into Week 2 in this Wednesday mailbag. Thanks to everyone who suggested a discussion topic. Let’s get right to them, right now: “Let’s say the Commanders have a respectable season, but miss out on a Wildcard spot. Does DQ stay? Where is the line for Peters? I’m not asking this question to be inflammatory, and in general I’m in favor of keeping continuity and ideally keeping AP and DQ in that scenario. To me, even if our team was extremely good, it would be an uphill battle given our division and general NFC playoff picture. But the clock keeps ticking. Would love to hear the HH writers’ thoughts on this.” — “Evgeny Last Words?” I pondered this question a bit just before the season and it generally follows Evgeny’s logic. I think the Commanders want Dan Quinn and Adam Peters sticking together. They’re also on different timelines. I don’t think Adam Peters’ seat is even warm. He’ll be around another cycle at least, even if things go really bad in 2026 (which they won’t). It’s Quinn who might be in trouble . Anything close to a 2025 repeat and I think we’re covering a coaching search next year. If the Commanders reach eight wins with this schedule – that’s a three-victory improvement – and DQ still has buy-in, he sticks. Six, or possibly seven, and things get murky. I believe continuity is the goal here. Quinn’s the culture builder. If his coordinator hires develop and his game management is good, you stick with what you’ve got. If not, you’ll likely start all over with a new head coach and another new play caller for Daniels. “May be too early but does the FO plan to extend JD after this season or drag the process out through year 4 and into the option year (year 5). Personally, I think if they do it after this season, they will probably save money in the long run; ie the most lucrative contract in NFL history this year will be less than the most lucrative contract in NFL history next year.” — DGOLD510 One thing the NFL’s quarterback cost won’t do is go down. There’s only inflation on the horizon here, and the amount someone gets paid is far less about their ranking among the NFL’s best and far more about who’s next. While there is some merit-based pay involved here, there’s no way Jayden Daniels gets cheaper the farther we go from his next extension. The smart play here is to extend him when he’s first eligible , following this season. The team should have some leverage for that first season – even Daniels doesn’t want to play two more seasons without generational guarantees – but it makes sense to lock something down then. The Patriots, Bears and (possibly) Broncos will be thinking the same thing next offseason, so those salaries should be bunched together. If you’re Washington, you want Daniels done before Caleb Williams and maybe even Drake Maye, so those contracts don’t elevate costs. One situation where you may want to put the contract off a year: If Daniels has a 2025 repeat, where he can’t stay healthy. That might create some doubt in a long-term deal. If Daniels is healthy, he’ll play well and deserve the money given. I think it’s part of the front office plan to get it done next offseason. They’ve budgeted for it. I think they’re prepared to lock Daniels down. And as for a more game-oriented question, how has Caleb Downs looked so far and do they think he will be a major factor in this week’s game? — B&G Beatdown Caleb Downs looked pretty, pretty good in Week 1, to the tune of eight tackles, a sack and a forced fumble. The Dallas defense overall was putrid, but Downs can play. He’s a do-everything safety that must be accounted for and game-planned against. The Dallas defense, overall, looks exploitable. Who’s available at corner to replace Mikey? Me in Madden, he’s gone. — ComplainingIsAPayne Mark Tyler wrote about Mike Sainristil in Tyler’s Take and advocated for a quick hook. Here’s what he wrote: “Mikey has to be benched. There is no other nice way to put this. Amik Robertson played a heck of a game against Philly on Sunday, but the worry is who plays outside opposite him until Trey Amos can return off injured reserve . What I would do is elevate Terell Smith , the 6-foot, 207-pound athletic corner from the practice squad and get him up to speed quickly. For now, Rasul Douglas showed enough against Philly to hold down that outside spot, but Smith may be the better long-term option if he’s finally back to health following a torn patellar during the 2025 preseason .” Adding more to Douglas’s plate sounds like the immediate option, with coaches keeping a close eye to see how Sainristil responds to a relative demotion. There are enough slot options to account for this move, especially with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens looming on Sunday. I have covered Smith before and he’s a really good player. The Commanders will know how his knee is doing, and whether he was the same player he was before the injury. It was an excellent practice squad pickup that will pay off at some point this season. Dan Quinn is normally reserved regarding public player criticism, but he said Sainristil’s two big plays allowed were unacceptable . The Commanders simply can’t have that when there are other options in wait while Amos gets healthy.

The addition’s corresponding move will be known later on Wednesday. The Commanders have struggled to find interior depth, especially at the center spot. Nick Allgretti missed significant time this summer with a calf strain, and Julian Good-Jones (now on the practice squad) and rookie Matt Gulbin clearly weren’t ready to assume starter’s duties. Patrick is an established pro, but we’ll have to see how he fits and what he’s able to contribute once he works into the Commanders culture and position group. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Sun The Commanders’ Dilemma: Protect Jayden Daniels or Let Him Loose? In Week 1, Washington’s young quarterback stuck to a new script until his team needed a hero In a perfect world, the Commanders wouldn’t have to choose between keeping their franchise quarterback healthy and winning games. In a perfect world — such as the one they inhabited in 2024, when Daniels was a spectacular rookie and the Commanders were a 12-5 juggernaut — they can accomplish both objectives. But here, at the start of the 2026 season, it’s already feeling like something close to a binary choice. And for most of Sunday night’s entertaining game, it felt like the Commanders were unsure which side of that line they wanted to occupy. For the first three quarters Sunday night, the Commanders mostly stuck to that script. And what did that get them? A 17-9 deficit. Nine completions in 24 attempts for Daniels, for a total of 65 passing yards. No sacks, but no touchdown passes. Their longest play from scrimmage at that point was for 15 yards. They were 2 for 11 on third-down conversions. Terry McLaurin, their two-time Pro Bowl wideout, had two targets and no catches. They absolutely, positively, 100% don’t want Daniels to feel like he has to go out there and win games for them with his unique blend of athleticism, artistry and aerial acumen. Until they absolutely, positively, 100% need him to do exactly that. And then, it seems, they are willing to hold their breath and turn him loose. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Jayden Daniels showing off the moves 😮‍💨 WASvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OEZovvBO38 — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Riggo’s Rag Joshua Josephs keeps turning limited Commanders chances into lasting impressions Josephs didn’t generate many headlines, certainly not compared to Styles, Williams, and even special-teams ace Tyler Owens . He played only 13 snaps on defense, but the Tennessee product stood out a couple of times. Just how much time Josephs will see on the field now that edge rusher Dorance Armstrong Jr. is back from his one-game suspension remains to be seen. But if the No. 147 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft keeps making this kind of impact against elite-level tackles like Johnson, it’ll stay on the radar. At the very least. These Week 1 flashes weren’t without substance, either. Josephs was among the standout performers at training camp , displaying the speed, length, and dynamism that convinced the Commanders to take a chance. He backed this up in the preseason, even scoring a touchdown by bursting onto a loose football against the Detroit Lions. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) His stunning special teams effort went viral. To Tyler Owens, it was ‘just a normal football play’ It wasn’t the first time Tyler Owens ripped down the field to slam a returner to the ground. It wasn’t even the first time in that game. But in the second quarter of the Washington Commanders’ loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Owens’ play as a special-teams gunner made him a household name literally overnight. Facing a vise, or double-team, in punt coverage, Owens split Eagles jammers Jonathan Jones (a former Commander) and Darius Cooper by essentially tossing them to the side and leaving them in his wake as he pursued returner Britain Covey — whom he then lifted off the ground and body-slammed at Philadelphia’s 38-yard line. “I feel like it was just a normal football play out there,” Owens told The Athletic on Tuesday. He is the definition of an athletic freak and while he adjusts to the mental side of the game at the NFL level, his athleticism can carry him through to be productive. Against the Eagles on Sunday, we saw that athleticism stand out in a number of different situations. As soon as the ball is snapped, Styles triggers and gets a full head of steam as he works up to Barkley. Barkley has to abandon the play-action fake because Styles covers the ground so quickly. He attempts to get low and get under Styles in order to redirect his momentum upwards and stall out the rush, but Styles runs over him. Barkley is one of the premier running backs in this league. He’s listed at 6-foot, 233 pounds, which is big for a running back. He’s been one of the hardest backs to tackle and bring down in the NFL since he was drafted. This is not someone who just gets run over by a better athlete. Typically Barkley is the one running over people as the better athlete. But Styles gets low, gets his hands on Barkley’s chest and uses his momentum to knock Barkley off his feet and run through the block. Styles then quickly turns his attention to Jalen Hurts, who is another player that is very hard to bring down. But even when he wasn’t making freaky plays against Barkley, the athleticism still stood out. Sonny Styles had two flash plays against the Eagles on Sunday, but how did the rest of his NFL debut go? title: Washington Commanders at the Cowboys in Week 2: Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates […]
full_text: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: The Washington Commanders are coming off a tough 22-24 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday that was a golden opportunity to start a tough early schedule well. Unfortunately, head coach Dan Quinn and his team came up just short. The Commanders now head to Arlington, Texas, trying to avoid going 0-2 in the NFC East (and overall) to start the season. The Cowboys will look to do the same after a loss to John Harbaugh’s Giants, who got out to an early lead and never gave it back on the way to a 28-20 victory over Dallas Sunday night. The matchup between the NFC East rivals features two rookie coordinators on opposite sides of the ball in David Blough and Christian Parker, both of whom are looking to get things on track after a rough outing in Week 1. The Commanders’ offense looked out-of-sync and ineffective for the first three quarters versus a tough Eagles defense that was able to generate pressure with only a four-man rush while bracketing Washington’s wide receivers downfield. Blough finally switched to an up-tempo, shotgun-style approach late in the game, and Jayden Daniels will look to build off his 9-of-11, 100-yard, two-touchdown fourth-quarter performance in Sunday afternoon’s game. Dallas would appear to offer the perfect opportunity to do so. The Cowboys’ defensive overhaul was a complete disaster in Parker’s debut, which ranked 571 among 574 total defensive performances since Week 1 of 2025 based on EPA/drive and, at one point, the Giants successfully ran the same play four times in a row. The Giants ran the SAME PLAY 4x in a row and the Cowboys STILL can't stop them 😭 pic.twitter.com/cGidMoavhU — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) September 14, 2026 Parker’s defense showed more finesse than physicality, and New York’s offense dominated the Cowboys D to the tune of 394 yards of total offense, converting 9-of-11 third downs, which let the Giants maintain a chokehold on time of possession. Dallas failed to get much pressure on Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and, unlike the Philadelphia Eagles, only generated two pressures on four-man rushes during the evening. Blough should have plenty of opportunities to get his offense on the right track, as the Cowboys’ defense also lost safety Malik Hooker and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown to injuries this week. Conversely, Washington’s defense looked vastly improved under Daronte Jones’ direction, but failed to limit the Philadelphia’s explosive playmaking ability, giving up 171 of the Eagles’ 318 total yards on just four plays. The secondary in particular struggled. Dallas’ two big wide receivers George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb will be going against last week’s starters, Amik Robertson and Mike Sainristil, making this a matchup to watch. As Bill noted in June , Brian Schottenheimer’s 2025 offense was one of the most prolific in the NFL, finishing second in the league in both total yards (6,663) and passing yards, but Dallas’ offense got off to a slow start in Week 1. Entering his 11th season, Dak Prescott completed 22 of 34 attempts for just 175 yards . The Cowboys, who had the fewest three-and-outs in 2025, opened Sunday with a three-and-out and Dallas failed to generate a play of more than 17 yards all game, with both George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb having opportunities go through their hands. Running back Javonte Williams also had a poor game, rushing for 41 yards on 12 attempts and drawing a momentum-stealing taunting penalty on his rushing touchdown. If Jones can dial up the pressure early, the Commanders’ defense should be able to set the tone versus the Cowboys. One of the bright spots for Dallas last week was first-round selection Caleb Downs. The safety was popularly mocked to the Commanders before the draft and played 61 total defensive snaps , with eight total tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and just two receptions allowed for seven yards. Washington’s offense will need to the keep their heads on swivels to avoid a play like this one happening to Jayden Daniels. The All-Time Series Numbers Dallas holds a clear lead in the historic series between the two franchises. Entering this game, the Cowboys have an 81-49-2 all-time record against Washington. The Commanders are 17-43-2 all-time on the road against the Cowboys, though four of those Washington wins have come since 2014. Dallas Coaching Changes The Cowboys overhauled their defensive coaching staff during the offseason. After finishing with the worst defense in 2025 as measured by points surrendered, team owner Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer replaced the previous defensive coordinator, Matt Eberflus, with a new hire from another division rival. Christian Parker is the new defensive play-caller. He previously worked as the passing game coordinator/defensive backs coach for the Philadelphia Eagles. A former defensive backs coach under Fangio in Denver (2021) and passing game coordinator in Philadelphia (2024–2025), Parker will likely use foundational Fangio concepts to build his modern defensive schemes that rely on pre-snap 2-high safety alignments to obscure coverage intentions and limit big plays. Similar to Fangio, Parker’s defense is expected to focus on manipulating offenses by shifting coverages after the snap to confuse quarterbacks. He will probably utilize lighter boxes against the run in favor of coverage strength in the secondary, deploying both 3-4 and 4-2-5 alignments with versatile players, and favor rush efficiency (getting to the quarterback with a standard 4-man rush) rather than relying on heavy, exotic blitz packages.
