title: NFL Week 2 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips
summary: What's the latest for three teams dealing with QB injuries? What are we hearing on the Rams and Chargers after bad losses? And which Week 1 debuts stood out?
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is officially rolling. As we head into Week 2, insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 Week 1 saw the Seahawks, Vikings and Falcons all forced to turn to backup quarterbacks -- and in Atlanta's case, it was a third-stringer. Where do those franchises sit at QB entering Week 2? Jeremy and Dan also asked around about a tough opening week for the two Los Angeles teams. Is there concern yet for the Rams and Chargers? Plus, they debated debuts for coaches and rookies then offered up their best fantasy tips based on what they're hearing.

 It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 2.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 QB situations | Rams, Chargers concerns 
 Coaching debuts | Rookie debuts 
 Fantasy football takes  | Notes and more buzz 

 
 

 What's the latest on the quarterback situation for the Vikings, Seahawks and Falcons? 
 Graziano: Things seem straightforward for Minnesota. Based on what I've been able to gather, my sense is that Kyler Murray will start if he clears concussion protocol in time, and Carson Wentz is likely to start if Murray isn't clear in time. That sounds like a negative toward J.J. McCarthy , since it was him and not Wentz who competed with Murray for the starting job in camp. But this is more about the Vikings believing Wentz's veteran experience puts them in better position with limited preparation time when a QB gets hurt in-game (as happened Sunday) and/or there's uncertainty about who's going to start throughout the week.

 

 McCarthy was the emergency third QB on Sunday, so the team knew there was a chance they might have to play him. I could see a scenario in which Wentz starts this week with McCarthy as the backup, assuming Murray can't go.

 Fowler: That's certainly plausible. Murray took a nasty hit, and teams tend to be overly cautious when a player has assumed the fencing position, for good reason. But how players work through the five stages of the protocol often varies, so it's tough to know Murray's timeline at this point. Wentz is set up for success in Week 2 . He got hot last week  versus Green Bay , and Chicago just allowed 361 passing yards to Bryce Young .

 In Seattle, it's clear Sam Darnold will miss this week and possibly Week 3. But the Seahawks have refrained from putting him on short-term injured reserve, which is a good sign. The team seems confident that  Drew Lock is plug and play until Darnold returns.

 Graziano: Yeah, Seattle believes Lock can handle it, so he's the guy there for the foreseeable future. I'm personally interested to see whether they put in anything specific for Jalen Milroe in terms of plays or packages that take advantage of his running ability and maybe give their offense a little bit extra juice. Why not, if Milroe is going to be active anyway as the second quarterback?

 What about Atlanta? Kevin Stefanski probably thought he left the QB mess behind in Cleveland, but he has a situation on his hands, no?

 Fowler: Stefanski has seen it all at quarterback, but at least his signal-callers in Cleveland mostly stayed out of the training room. Tua Tagovailoa 's body seems to be betraying him at an inopportune time. The Falcons' best option remains third-year man Michael Penix Jr. , but he's not yet ready for live game action. Penix wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field following left ACL surgery in November. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.

 Tagovailoa's injury, an oblique strain , can linger, which puts his Week 2 status up in the air. So,  Cooper Rush starting another week wouldn't be shocking. What helps Tagovailoa's case is his accuracy, which Stefanski highly values. If Tagovailoa's body doesn't totally break down in the short term and he can return before Penix is ready, perhaps Tagovailoa can provide a spark.

 Graziano: Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction , which is a lot of ACL reconstructions. I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it's OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I'm sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season. The Falcons are going to want to know whether he is a real long-term option moving forward.

 

 My sense is Tagovailoa was the favorite to start at the beginning of camp even when Penix was healthy but that Tagovailoa didn't perform the way the team had hoped he would. That has turned things into a confusing mess.

 Fowler: That two-week stretch, from the second preseason game rolling into the joint practice with the Colts, was rough for Tagovailoa. The schedule provides another wrinkle. Atlanta will play on Thursday night in Week 3, so even if Penix is close, that might not be the best week to reacclimate him.

 

 
 How high is the panic level in the Rams' building? What about for the Chargers? 
 Fowler: Well, the Rams' top-ranked offense scored seven points , and the league's best pass rusher is out at least a month . But other than that, everything's fine! I don't, however, sense heavy panic from the Rams, who seemed to approach the Australia trip with the excitement of a teenager asked to take out the trash. 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris knows the Rams' offense well, so San Francisco's ability to stymie Matthew Stafford shouldn't be a total shock.

 The Myles Garrett situation is more alarming. The Rams thought they could manage his knee injury with rest all camp and preseason, and it got exposed in Week 1. It leaves some uneasiness that they perhaps should have had this injury surgically repaired a tad sooner. But the Rams have plenty of defensive talent to offset the Garrett loss.

 Graziano: Garrett missed basically an entire month's worth of training camp with the knee problem, so those of us on the outside should have considered that a possible warning sign, at the very least. Aaron Donald being able to play Monday night would help, but the issues that came up in Australia went beyond Garrett's health. The Rams' expensive new cornerback tandem looked miscast in the defensive game plan, and they couldn't get the passing game clicking.

 The Rams are certainly not going to panic because of one game, even if it was an embarrassing loss to a division rival. But they are (and should be) taking the problems that were on display against the 49ers seriously. The operation needs to be sharper on both sides of the ball. One possible benefit of the Rams' controversial Australian travel plan is that they likely didn't need to get reacclimated upon their return home, since their body clocks theoretically never reset in the first place. We'll see if they come out looking sharper in Week 2 against the Giants.

 

 Fowler: The Chargers' panic meter will rise if they lose to the Raiders this week . Arizona was deemed terrible in the preseason, but the Cardinals are more respectable than that, particularly on offense. So, the Chargers' defense gets a mulligan after seeing the Cards in the opener. It's a veteran group that should improve.

 The bigger concern is how the Bolts' offense looked after wide receiver Ladd McConkey left the game with a rib injury. McConkey and Justin Herbert showed easy chemistry in that first half. They need McConkey, who is listed as day-to-day , to work his way back or concerns about the offensive attack will mushroom. I'm expecting a better running game from Los Angeles in Week 2 as it tries to find some continuity with the offensive line.

 Graziano: McConkey is a great player, but the game plan falling apart completely once he exited makes it seem as if it was flimsy to begin with. Where are the smart, creative run plays Mike McDaniel was calling last season in Miami? Wasn't running back Omarion Hampton supposed to explode in this scheme? Wasn't the…

title: Why NFL offenses are going under center more often in 2026
summary: Teams such as the Commanders, Eagles, Ravens, Chiefs, Giants and Raiders are going under center more -- and out of the shotgun less and less. Will this trend stick?
full_text:
A trend that had been a popular topic of conversation over the summer in buildings around the NFL was even more prevalent in Week 1 than I would have expected.

 During the offseason, organizations that have a track record of operating out of the shotgun or pistol with mobile quarterbacks made plans to move that QB under center. The Commanders, Eagles and Ravens hired new offensive coordinators in David Blough, Sean Mannion and Declan Doyle, respectively, who come from offensive trees built around under-center play. And the Vikings signed Kyler Murray , who had spent the vast majority of his college and pro careers working in the shotgun, and spent training camp working on his ability to read the field, take drops and throw from under center.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 Some of these organizations committed more aggressively than others in Week 1, and in the Vikings' case, the plans were thrown off by a first-quarter concussion to Murray. On a leaguewide basis, though, teams took snaps from under center at the highest rate since 2012.

 Why are NFL teams shifting back toward getting under center? Who benefited the most in Week 1? And will this trend stick? Coaches will talk about their philosophies during the offseason, but now that offenses had to show their cards in Week 1, the move under center is one of the more dramatic changes we've seen from NFL offenses in years. Let's cover how we got here and what might be next.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 How did we get here? 
 Why the return to under center? 
 What's missing from the approach? 
 Which teams have leaned in? 
 What's next for this trend? 

 
 

 The path to shotgun (and back) 
 Let's go back to 2007 and the 16-0 Patriots, who produced one of the best offenses in league history with a spread attack that looked little like the league's other 31 attacks. Though the NFL had seen the "run and shoot" and K-Gun in the 1990s, those were perceived to be short-lived fads from a relatively small number of coaches.

 But in '07, more than 74% of Tom Brady's dropbacks came from the shotgun, a figure that was nearly double the league average. The Patriots ran more than 49% of their snaps out of shotgun, a figure that would have been even higher if they hadn't been blowing teams out in the second half and running out the clock for most of the season. Consider that in 2001, Brady's first year as a starting quarterback, the Patriots had been in the shotgun just under 14% of the time.

 The league as a whole was still primarily operating from under center in 2007. Even as the Patriots tore up the NFL, the other 31 offenses were in shotgun only about 26% of the time. Getting out from under center was more of a move for obvious passing situations like third-and-long or as part of a two-minute drill. On first-and-10 in 2007, NFL offenses were in shotgun only 15% of the time. The Patriots were there on 40% of their snaps.

 

 Within five years, the league had shifted. During the 2012 season, NFL teams were under center just 54% of the time, down from 74% in 2007. And in 2013, the pendulum really swung. NFL teams took more snaps out of the shotgun or pistol (which had gained a foothold in the league after traveling with Colin Kaepernick from Nevada to San Francisco and being installed by Mike Shanahan and his staff of future head coaches in Washington for Robert Griffin ) than they did from under center. That disparity continued to rise in the years to come, with both scoring and offensive efficiency gradually rising alongside.

 By 2023, the shotgun craze peaked. Teams ran 71% of their offensive snaps from the shotgun or pistol and just 29% from under center, nearly one-third of where it had been in 2007. At the same time, though, offensive efficiency had cratered. Teams were scoring just under 22 points per game, down three points from the high-water mark of 2020. Vic Fangio-style defenses were spreading around the league, squeezing big plays away from offenses and daring them to run the ball. Teams grew more experienced dealing with some of the problems those three- and four-wideout sets presented.

 And as a result, in the past few years, we've seen a shift back toward the football of years past. We've watched offenses lean into bigger personnel groupings with multiple tight ends and/or a fullback on the field, something I wrote about during the offseason in my piece on the Rams and their surprising shift to 13 personnel in the middle of the 2025 season. In part, that's to push defenses out of nickel alignments and back to their base defense with four defensive backs, which would allow offenses to get back to tormenting linebackers with the passing game. The Seahawks exploited those base defense looks  during last season's run to the Super Bowl, and perhaps as a result, defenses were  more aggressive  about staying in their nickel defense against 12 and 13 personnel looks in Week 1 of the 2026 season.

 We've also seen the league get under center more often. After a decade of heading toward the shotgun, the under-center rate took a small step forward from 29% in 2023 to 30.5% in 2024. In 2025, that rate rose more dramatically to 35%. And in Week 1 of 2026, NFL offenses were under center 42.5% of the time .

 We're suddenly back where we were in 2013 (42.2%) in terms of under-center rate. And as you might have noticed, that decision came with plenty of scoring. Teams averaged 24.7 points per game in Week 1, tying with 2012 for the highest-scoring opening week since the 1970 merger. Correlation isn't necessarily causation, but offenses went under center at the highest rate in more than a decade and didn't exactly suffer for their choice.

 OK, so now you know how we got to what we saw in Week 1. But what benefits are teams hoping to realize from moving under center? How does it fit what defenses are showing? And what are the trade-offs?

 

 

 

 The 'why' of going under center 
 If you ask NFL coaches why offenses are going under center, one answer invariably comes up: They want a more diverse and unpredictable run game. There are advantages to operating out of the shotgun, and we'll get to them in a minute, but one of the disadvantages comes with what teams are able (or unable) to do on the ground. In the shotgun, running backs line up to the side of the quarterback, which both limits the types of run concepts offenses can run and makes the side to which they'll ultimately run more predictable. Offensive architects have gotten more creative with motion to try to disguise some of those concepts, with blockers motioning in one direction pre-snap before immediately turning around and attempting to kick out a defender post-snap, but there are concepts where the timing just doesn't really work from shotgun.

 Take last season's Seahawks, for example. Under center, Seattle ran all kinds of concepts, including inside zone and outside zone, power, counter, duo and a handful of other run schemes. When the Seahawks were in the pistol or shotgun, though, their run game (and the play-action attack that resulted) was almost always built around counter. If you can nail down what a team's going to run by where the running back lines up, you can limit some of its offensive creativity.

 Under center, the RB lines up directly behind the quarterback, which allows offenses to retain the ability to run to either side without needing to realign or shift personnel. It also helps create the timing needed to run outside zone concepts consistently and effectively. When Washington drafted Griffin in 2012 and attempted to mesh a Shanahan-style zone-rushing attack around the zone-read concepts the rookie had run at Baylor, the coaches installed the pistol to keep the back -- usually Alfred Morris  -- directly behind Griffin as opposed to lining him up alongside him. Morris and Griffin combined for 2,428 rushing yards during their shared rookie campaign, but once Shanahan started working with more traditional QBs, he moved…

title: How to bet Lions-Bills on 'TNF': Analysis, tips and favorite plays
summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Lions-Bills on "Thursday Night Football."
full_text:
The "Thursday Night Football" slate gets going with the Buffalo Bills hosting the Detroit Lions in the first regular-season game at the new Highmark Stadium.

 

 The Lions and Bills both won in Week 1, but neither defense looked particularly good doing it. Buffalo gave up 31 points to the Houston Texans  and Detroit blew a 21-point lead before escaping with a 31-30 overtime win over the New Orleans Saints .

 I'd be concerned about Detroit's secondary heading into this matchup. Tyler Shough just threw for 410 yards against the Lions, who are dealing with injuries to safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch . Now they have to face Josh Allen , who can beat you through the air or take off running when the coverage holds up. The Bills' addition of wide receiver DJ Moore gives Allen another playmaker to work with.

 The Lions have plenty of firepower, too. Jahmyr Gibbs should be heavily involved against a Bills defense that had trouble slowing down the Texans. Jared Goff also has top wideout  Amon-Ra St. Brown to lean on.

 The matchup I'm watching is defensive end Aidan Hutchinson against the Bills' offensive line. Detroit needs to make Allen uncomfortable. If he has time to throw, that Lions secondary could be in trouble again.

 

 

 

 Betting outlook 

 I'm more interested in the total than the spread here. The Bills opened as a 3-point favorite, but that number has moved to 4.5. The total has also climbed, from 52.5 to 54.5. I would have been much more comfortable backing Buffalo at the opening number, but I'm not interested in laying nearly a touchdown now.

 

 The total is a tougher decision. Both teams have the offensive talent to put up points, but oddsmakers have already adjusted for that. At 54.5, you're asking these teams to combine for at least 55 points on a short week. That's a high bar, especially with the Lions coming off an overtime game.

 I'm also interested in how Detroit approaches this matchup. Head coach Dan Campbell could lean on the running game to keep Allen on the sideline, which would eat up clock and make the over harder to cash.

 I liked the over earlier in the week, but at 54.5, I'm staying away. I'm not going to force a bet just because this game has shootout potential.

 

 Notable player props, bets 
 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 

 DJ Moore to score a touchdown (+150) 

 Moore led the Bills in targets in Week 1 and ran a route on more than 80% of Buffalo's pass plays. He has already established himself as a key cog in Allen's passing game. Now he faces a banged-up Lions secondary that allowed Shough to throw for 410 yards and three touchdowns last week. I like Moore's chances of finding the end zone.

 Dalton Kincaid receiving yards OVER 51.5 (-110) 

 Kincaid led Buffalo's tight ends in snaps, routes, targets and receiving yards against Houston in Week 1. He finished with a team-high 130 receiving yards and tied for second in targets with Khalil Shakir . Detroit allowed Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant to combine for 87 receiving yards last week, and with this game carrying one of the highest totals of Week 2, I like Kincaid's chances of clearing this number.

title: Bryce Young's 4-1 record vs. Falcons a harbinger for Week 2?
summary: The Panthers QB's previous trips to Mercedes-Benz Stadium should keep Falcons fans and coaches up at night.
full_text:
During the third quarter of a back-and-forth divisional donnybrook to end the 2024 season, the Carolina Panthers trailed the Atlanta Falcons by one point, roughly four minutes into the second half.

 It was fourth-and-1 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

 Bryce Young lined up under center and took a snap before faking a handoff to running back Miles Sanders . With tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders darting to the right behind the line of scrimmage to pick up a defender for a lead block, Young sprinted behind him on a bootleg. The quarterback then set his feet midway through his jaunt and fired a dart over the middle to tight end Tommy Tremble in the end zone.

 Before the ball even reached the wide open Tremble's hands, Young turned around and threw up a touchdown signal as a way of celebrating the 12-yard heave for a go-ahead score. The oft soft-spoken signal-caller showed off his understated bravado with the early commemoration of the touchdown connection.

 

 "It was the coolest thing ever," Tremble said about Young's signature throw of 2024. "That play is one of my favorites. Like, it's fun to see, and that's when I feel like Bryce Young really, like, activated and everyone else could see the kind of player he was."

 

 The Panthers won the 2024 season finale against the Falcons on the road, 44-38, in overtime, as Young produced a career-high five total touchdowns -- three with his arm and two with his legs -- nearly four months after he was benched in Week 3 of his second campaign. The shot of Young's pre-completion celebration spread throughout the 2025 offseason and served as a beacon of hope for fans of the much-maligned passer.

 "He was the best dude on the field," Panthers right guard Rob Hunt said. "That was cool. ... It was a good moment for him, for sure -- confidence builder. ...That was good going into the next season."

 And while Young did improve throughout his 2025 season, it was again his bout against the Falcons on the road last season that turned heads. In his Atlanta-based follow-up to the 2024 clash, Young threw for a franchise-record 448 yards -- surpassing Cam Newton's previous mark of 432 yards in 2011 -- and three touchdowns in a 30-27 overtime win against the Falcons.

 While the Panthers head back to Atlanta on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) with an identical 0-1 record to the Falcons, Young's previous two trips to Mercedes-Benz Stadium should keep Falcons fans and coaches up at night. And considering the Panthers' defense gave up 59 points and 552 yards to the Chicago Bears last week, Young -- who led six scoring drives in Week 1 -- might need to be the difference-maker again on Sunday.

 "Coach [ Dave Canales ] talks about it all the time: Our first goal is to win the [NFC] South," Young said Wednesday. "And obviously, those division wins mean so much, when you're trying to accomplish that goal. You have the same process and you understand that. You don't want to get too high or too low, but again, this is a business, we're all pros and we understand what's at stake every time that it's a division opponent."

 Let's look closer at how Young has gone above and beyond inside the dome that sits in the heart of Atlanta and get a feel for what the 25-year-old could do for an encore.

 

 Young's performances in Atlanta 
 Despite losing his NFL debut in Atlanta in the season opener against the Falcons in 2023, Young's numbers against his familiar foes run counter to his overall career stat line.

 Young had a 16.4 total quarterback rating in his debut loss against the Falcons, but he has since won four consecutive starts against Atlanta, raising his QBR against the rival NFC South franchise to 67.4, which is more than 20 points higher than his career number of 43.9.

 

 Young is 4-1 in his starts against the Falcons and 10-30 as a starter against everyone else. His 66.7% completion percentage against Atlanta is five percentage points higher than his career average (61.4%). In five games, Young has thrown for 1,133 passing yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. He is throwing 3.5 touchdowns for every interception against Atlanta; he averages 1.7 touchdowns per interception against the entire league.

 The QB has also scored a third of his career rushing touchdowns against the Falcons, as three of his nine QB-keeper TDs have come against Atlanta.

 "I feel like every single time he goes to Atlanta, he just makes the plays," Tremble said. "And him breaking Cam Newton's passing record that game [in 2025] -- it was sick to see. It was fun to be a part of that. So, I'm excited to see him, hopefully, even top that game from last time."

 And while his numbers are comparatively modest at home in Charlotte (288 total passing yards, 17 rushing total yards and a rushing touchdown in two games) against the Falcons, his last two road trips to Atlanta featured 699 total passing yards, 23 total rushing yards and eight total touchdowns to go with a pair of overtime victories in thrilling shootouts.

 It's also worth noting, Young's success at Mercedes-Benz Stadium predates his NFL career. He threw for 765 total yards and seven total touchdowns in two blowout wins in Atlanta during his tenure as the Alabama Crimson Tide's starting QB. During one of those outings, he also ran for 40 yards and a touchdown on three carries -- to go along with 421 passing yards and three passing touchdowns -- against Georgia in the 2021 SEC Championship Game.

 
 Young's outlook against Falcons in Week 2 
 Young's fourth Week 1 appearance went much better than his previous three opening-week outings for Carolina. He finished the 59-37 loss to the Bears with 361 passing yards, four total touchdowns (including a rushing score) and an interception. He had a 66.4 QBR, nearly identical to his overall success against Atlanta.

 "He's off to a hot start right now, we've just got to keep it rolling," Tremble said.

 According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Young threw for a career-high 221 yards on deep throws against Chicago, completing 64.3% of his downfield heaves. He was particularly effective against zone coverage, throwing for 289 yards compared to 72 yards against man coverage.

 Against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1, the Falcons ran zone coverage on nearly 40% of their defensive snaps. Atlanta favored man coverage at nearly 60% against Pittsburgh.

 

 Young will need to be much more efficient against man coverage than he was against the Bears, who primarily used zone coverage against Carolina in Week 1.

 Still, Young faced coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's scheme twice last season, and while the quarterback had a modest stat line in their initial meeting in Charlotte (121 passing yards, eight rushing yards and a rushing touchdown with 66.7% completion percentage), he exploded to boast career-high passing numbers in the second go-around in Atlanta in 2025.

 Nothing should be particularly foreign to Young about Ulbrich's attack, even with coach Kevin Stefanski now overseeing the team.

 "Very matchy group, guys that -- especially on the perimeter -- they play really well," Young said about the man coverage-heavy scheme. "Understand concepts, do a great job of pattern matching, all that stuff, so we know it's going to take everything. We have to be executing at a high level to have success."

 

 Biggest X factor for Young in Atlanta? 
 The Panthers' offensive line needs to keep Young upright Sunday. Against Chicago, Young was pressured on 11 of his 41 dropbacks, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He also took two sacks.

 Carolina will go up against new faces on the Falcons front, too. With defensive ends James Pearce Jr . (suspension) and Jalon Walker (injured reserve) unavailable, Atlanta will count on veterans Za'Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam to bring the pressure, along with newly acquired defensive tackles Maason Smith and Gervon Dexter Sr . Against Pittsburgh, Za'Darius Smith picked up both of the Falcons' sacks and the front seven pressured Rodgers on 13 of his 40…

summary: When even the "little guys" are getting a hat on a hat, it's that much easier to post 59 points and over 500 yards.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. --  Chicago Bears  receiver  Jahdae Walker threw his right shoulder into Will Lee III , sending the Panthers cornerback to the turf and creating the opening for receiver Kalif Raymond to work his way shy of the first-down marker.

 It was late in Chicago's 59-37 win over Carolina, and the force of his block left Walker winded. Even in the thick of the Bears' offensive explosion, all the dirty work that Walker put in on 33 of his 34 offensive snaps was not lost on coach Ben Johnson.

 Five plays later, Johnson sent in a playcall that rewarded the second-year wide receiver. Walker caught a 1-yard touchdown and became the fifth different Bears player to score in the season opener.

 Walker, the former undrafted free agent, knew long before he made the team in 2025 that any role he'd earn on offense is dependent on him embracing the selfless, physical aspects of playing receiver that don't show up in a box score. But what's required of Walker isn't limited to players further down the depth chart. There's a rallying cry inside the offensive meeting rooms that everyone from star tight end Colston Loveland , who did not record a catch in Week 1 but has always been a willing blocker (27 run blocking snaps at Carolina), to rookie receiver Zavion Thomas must buy into.

 "Oh shoot, [Johnson] just says, 'no block, no rock' and that just gets us going because we all want the ball," Walker said. "So that's pretty much all we be thinking about. It's just you got to buy into it or you're going to get left."

 "No block, no rock" is a philosophy Johnson picked up during his days as a position coach with the Miami Dolphins . It's a common football expression that has been hammered into offensive players since Johnson became the Bears' head coach last year, making clear that if skill players want their touches, they have to be willing physical contributors.

 That requirement is most necessary in the run game. Chicago's 291 rushing yards led to six touchdowns, the most rushing touchdowns in a season opener since the 1922 Canton Bulldogs. The Bears had not compiled that many rushing yards in a game since they ran for 302 against the Denver Broncos in a 27-0 win in 1984.

 

 D'Andre Swift  (124 yards, 3 TDs) and Kyle Monangai (100 yards, TD) made franchise history by becoming the first Bears duo to each rush for 100 yards in a season opener. Quarterback Caleb Williams contributed to the run game with 65 yards, which resulted in his first career game with multiple rushing touchdowns (2).

 Of all 70 plays the Bears ran in Carolina, Johnson said Monangai's 61-yard touchdown run was his favorite. It wasn't just the offense's ability to score quickly one play after the Panthers turned the ball over on downs, nor was it Monangai keeping his balance in a track race to get away from defenders.

 Blocks by Raymond and tight end Cole Kmet allowed Monangai to get to the second level. As Walker ran in stride with his running back teammate, the block he had on Panthers outside linebacker Princely Umanmielen sprung Monangai loose. As stoic as he appeared on the sideline, Johnson says he was rife with excitement at all the things that took place for that to be the result.

 "We had a lot of our little guys going down and making big plays for us on the running game that ended up being some big runs for us," Johnson said. The Bears have amassed over 500 yards in a game twice under Johnson, including Week 1 at Carolina and a 47-42 win over the Cincinnati Bengals in November 2025. In the previous 25 seasons, a span that includes 413 games, there were two instances where the offense put up 500-plus yards.

 Just like in Carolina, the run game was a huge factor in that Cincinnati win with 283 rushing yards. Swift's breakout performance in the season opener coming off signing a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension is why Johnson said he's "vital" to everything the Bears do on offense.

 It also highlights the need from at least nine others on offense to make those plays happen routinely.

 As the 2026 Bears build their identity over the first quarter of the season, one thing is already established. To reach or top the 127 explosive plays (10-yard rush or 20-yard completion) they had last regular season will require the efforts of everyone, not just the players who wind up with the ball in their hands.

 "No block, no rock" is a mindset that will get its next test on Sunday against the  Minnesota Vikings  (1 p.m. ET, Fox) at Soldier Field.

title: Cowboys' TD record: I caught a TD pass from Dak Prescott
summary: Prescott needs four TDs to pass Tony Romo in the record book, so we sought the best moments from those who are helping him make history.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Sometime soon, perhaps as soon as Sunday against the Washington Commanders , Dak Prescott will set another Dallas Cowboys record: most touchdown passes in team history.

 He has 245, leaving him three shy of the 248 Tony Romo threw from 2006 to 2016.

 "I might remember every single one of them," Prescott said.

 His first?

 "Slant to Dez in the fourth quarter against Chicago," Prescott said.

 True. Prescott's first touchdown pass was a 17-yarder to receiver  Dez Bryant in the third game of his rookie season after being selected in Round 4 of the 2016 draft. The Cowboys beat the Chicago Bears , giving Prescott his first career victory at AT&T Stadium.

 His favorite?

 "I don't think I have a true favorite, one that stands out," Prescott said. "Any of them that have been a game winner or some big-time, fourth-quarter touchdowns, those are the ones that stick out in my mind."

 Needing four touchdown passes against the Commanders in the Cowboys' home opener at AT&T Stadium on Sunday ( 4:25 p.m. ET, Fox ) might seem daunting, but Prescott has already reached that mark four times against Washington, the last coming in a 38-10 win in Week 18 of the 2023 season.

 Prescott has thrown touchdowns to 39 different players, including 10 current teammates. CeeDee Lamb has the most with 35. Eleven have caught one.

 Instead of Prescott's favorite touchdown passes, ESPN asked nine current and former teammates to describe their favorite scoring receptions from the quarterback, including Lamb and right tackle Terence Steele , whose only career catch is a TD from Prescott.

 

 

 CeeDee Lamb, WR 

 Situation: Week 17, 2023, vs.  Detroit Lions , first quarter, third-and-13 from Cowboys' 8 

 Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes  should have sacked Prescott, but somehow he escaped at the goal line, drifted to his right and let go of a deep ball toward Lamb. Before he caught the pass, cornerback Kindle Vildor fell. Lamb caught the ball at midfield and was able to jog into the end zone for a 92-yard score.

 "Dak did a great job of beating the blitz. I did a good job of expanding on the scramble drill," Lamb said. "We preach extending drives and extending plays and that was a big part of that. That was one of the longest plays of my career. For sure, my most favorite."

 

 It was the longest completion of Prescott's career, the longest catch of Lamb's and the second-longest completion in team history. It was also Lamb's 111th catch of the season, which tied him for Michael Irvin 's team record for most in a season, which he later broke.

 Has he ever run that far without being chased?

 "Nah, I don't think I'll ever get that close to it again. Great time," Lamb said. "I enjoyed it. As you could tell, I trotted in the end zone. It was fire."

 

 

 Jason Witten , TE 
 Situation: Week 8, 2016 vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , overtime, second-and-goal from Eagles' 5 

 The Cowboys trailed 23-13 early in the fourth quarter, but Prescott forced overtime with a touchdown pass to Dez Bryant with 3:04 to play. In overtime, the Cowboys never gave the Eagles a chance to win it.

 Pressured on the play, Prescott went into scramble mode, first cheating up toward the line of scrimmage as some Eagles defenders converged and then sliding to his left. As chaos ensued, Witten just stopped in the end zone, leading to a wide open throw and a 29-23 win.

 

 "I was running away from the guy and I just kind of stepped back and so it kind of went against the grain if you will and stepped back instead of keeping on scrambling and mirroring him," Witten said. "He immediately saw it and immediately threw it. It was almost like he saw it at the same time I saw it -- and didn't even flinch ... it was at a critical time but that's my favorite one just because it was the Eagles and it was fairly early on in our time together.

 "For him to have seen that and anticipate what I was doing at the same time, because if he's a half second late, I don't know if we complete it. Mike Jenkins was the guy covering me. He was a crafty veteran guy and I just kind of did that move and Dak saw it at the same time."

 It was Prescott's first touchdown pass to Witten on a night when Witten set the Cowboys' record for most career starts and tied linebacker  Lee Roy Jordan 's team mark for most consecutive starts.

 

 Terence Steele, OT 
 Situation: Week 16, 2021 vs. Washington Commanders, third-and-goal from Commanders' 1 

 Steele was in his second year but wise enough to know if he dropped a pass in practice, offensive coordinator Kellen Moore would be unlikely to call the play in a game.

 "It'll sway the coach to not run it, but every time we ran it in practice, I caught it," Steele said, "so I think that gave him a lot of confidence to call it."

 It helped the Cowboys were already leading 28-7 in the second quarter against the Commanders, but when Steele heard Prescott say, "Red Raider report," a nod to Steele's Texas Tech days, the play was on.

 

 Steele started at left tackle that day but moved to jumbo tight end next to right tackle La'el Collins and dutifully told the referee he was reporting as an eligible receiver.

 "I'm supposed to slowly lose [his block] and let him beat me up the field and then I get in the end zone," Steele said. "And Dak throws me a perfect ball. Right between the hands."

 Steele spiked the ball so ferociously that it ended up in one of the field suites. Ezekiel Elliott was able to track the ball and make sure Steele had it.

 "I got it framed," Steele said. "They got it all painted up for me. It sits in my office right now."

 Steele became the first Cowboys offensive lineman since the 1970 merger to catch a touchdown. Prescott finished with four touchdown passes in a 56-14 win.

 

 

 George Pickens, WR 

 Situation: Week 16, 2025 vs.  Los Angeles Chargers , second-and-2 from Chargers' 38 

 Pickens  caught nine touchdown passes from Prescott in his first season with the Cowboys.

 His first choice for the favorite was a 34-yard catch-and-run on a slant at the Carolina Panthers  in Week 6.

 "Just running away from all the guys," he said.

 But then he remembered the go ball from Prescott against the Chargers.

 

 Using an outside release against Chargers cornerback Cam Hart , Pickens gained separation with a little stop-and-go. But then he noticed Prescott's pass was a little deeper than he thought.

 "Just definitely looking at the ball and changing my speed on how I should catch that ball," Pickens said. "It was a led ball, so I kind of knew, pick up the speed, but if it was a high ball or a ball that's kind of going to sit over his head, I would've made it fine."

 It wasn't the first time he and Prescott connected on that type of pass.

 "Definitely, practice," he said. "Tons of practice reps."

 

 Jake Ferguson, TE 

 Situation: Week 4, 2025 vs.  Green Bay Packers . Second-and-6 from Packers' 8 

 Ferguson might not have forgotten what it felt like to score a touchdown, but for him it felt like an eternity. He had gone 22 games since scoring against the Seattle Seahawks on Nov. 30, 2023. Part of his drought had to do with Prescott missing nine games in 2024 with avulsion of a hamstring.

 But it stretched through the first three weeks of the 2025 season.

 "It was a while," Ferguson said. "I remember, and the media didn't let me live it down."

 

 Lined up initially as a wing, Ferguson shifted a few yards to his left before the snap, putting cornerback Nate Hobbs in coverage. Ferguson was able to get inside of Hobbs at the goal line, using his body to shield the smaller corner and give Prescott an easy throw that gave the Cowboys a third-quarter lead.

 "When I caught it, it was like a huge weight off my shoulders," Ferguson said. "And I remember the guys coming up to me and [Prescott] came up to me very calm and was like, 'Welcome back,'" Ferguson said. "I was like, 'Thank you.' All I could say was, 'Thank you, thank you, thank you.'"

 Ferguson…

title: Broncos face tough opening stretch, try to avoid slow start
summary: The Broncos are 4-8 in September under Sean Payton after Monday's loss to the Chiefs. And they now face five 2025 playoff teams in a row.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Stumbling out of the gate has been a theme for the Denver Broncos since Sean Payton was hired as coach prior to the 2023 season. And those slow starts are coming to the forefront again after Monday night's season-opening loss to the Kansas City Chiefs .

 The 31-10 meltdown at Arrowhead Stadium was the first game of a brutal opening stretch that could potentially put the Broncos in a big hole by mid-October if recent history repeats itself. Denver's next five games are against 2025 playoff teams that won at least 11 games last season. And two opponents in that stretch -- including the Jacksonville Jaguars , who the Broncos (0-1) will play in their home opener on Sunday ( 4:05 p.m. ET, Empower Field at Mile High, CBS ) -- scored 27 or more points in Week 1 victories.

 "We're kind of tired of these slow starts," said edge rusher Nik Bonitto in a sullen locker room as Monday night turned into Tuesday morning. "Coming out every year and not starting the way we want. I don't think it was a wake-up call; we've just got to execute better from everybody."

 

 Monday's loss dropped the Broncos to 4-8 in September under Payton. They've won only one of their past four openers and are trying to avoid their third 0-2 start in four seasons. Even last season, when Denver went 14-3 and advanced to the AFC Championship Game, started with two losses in the first three weeks. So, starting faster was a talking point throughout August, both publicly and behind the scenes.

 "I don't think we've really started fast here in my three years -- I'm pretty sure we haven't," Payton said just before the season began. "... I think that's going to be important."

 It could be vitally important to the Broncos' playoff pursuits given how frontloaded their schedule is this season. Next up are the Jaguars (1-0), who got four touchdown passes from Trevor Lawrence in their season-opening win over the Cleveland Browns . Jacksonville won the AFC South with a 13-4 record last season, which included a 34-20 victory in Denver last December that snapped an 11-game Broncos winning streak.

 That will be followed by a Sunday night home game against the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams (0-1). Then the Broncos will hit the road to play the  San Francisco 49ers  (1-0) and Los Angeles Chargers (0-1). The tough stretch finishes with a short-week, Thursday night game at home against the  Seattle Seahawks (1-0).

 The schedule softens considerably after that point, as the Broncos face only one opponent that finished last season with a winning record in Weeks 7-15. But they know they can't afford to dig a massive hole before that.

 "I think everybody knows [Payton] has talked about a fast start," Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton said. "You go into every game thinking you want to get going early and you don't really think about anything more than the week in front of you. So, it's just like, if we start fast each week that's a fast start of a season."

 Monday's loss was particularly troubling, especially the run defense and quarterback Bo Nix 's unsettled play in Davis Webb's first regular-season game as the playcaller.

 Nix was sacked four times for only the second time in his three-year career. He fumbled three times (losing one) and threw an interception, finishing 17-of-28 with 131 passing yards with a touchdown and the interception. The Broncos gained only 176 total yards on a mere 47 plays (32 pass plays, 15 runs), with Payton saying the Broncos' game plan had "a lot of throws, not enough runs."

 

 The leaky run defense is a growing issue, as Monday was the third consecutive game (including playoffs) the Broncos had given up at least 141 rushing yards dating to last season. The Chiefs pounded out 220 rushing yards, 173 coming from running back Kenneth Walker III . Kansas City pointed its rushing plays toward the middle of the formation, often pinning linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad away from ball carriers. The Chiefs broke 19 tackles Monday, according to ESPN Research, with Walker breaking 11. The Broncos broke six as a team .

 "Coach had us in the right spot and we missed tackles and plays we were in the wrong spot," Singleton said. "... We're going to point the fingers at ourselves."

 Monday wasn't the fast start the Broncos hoped for, but they can take solace in being able to dig out of slow starts the past two seasons to make the playoffs. Denver started 0-2 in 2024 and was 5-5 in November before finishing on a 5-2 kick to reach the postseason. Last season's 1-2 start was erased by 13 wins in the Broncos' final 14 regular-season games. Even in 2023, when the Broncos' 0-3 start included an infamous 70-20 loss to the Miami Dolphins , Denver recovered and had a 6-5 record entering December before finishing 8-9.

 But that all seemed like ancient history as the Broncos quietly packed their gear to leave Arrowhead. Now they must find solutions on the practice field the rest of the week before they face the Jaguars in Game No. 2 of a rough six-week opening stretch.

 "We know this is not going to be the whole season for us," Nix said. "That's the first time since Baltimore [a 41-10 loss in Week 9 in 2024] that we've been beat pretty handily like that. ... I do think [Monday] was not a good representation of us as a team."

title: How family and fatherhood are fueling Lions QB Jared Goff
summary: The arrival of Goff's daughter, Romy Isabelle, has helped sharpened the quarterback's focus heading into 2026.
full_text:
DETROIT -- To the child waiting in the friends and family tents, it didn't matter the Detroit Lions had just wrapped up an intense two-hour practice on the sunny afternoon of Aug. 10. The moment 1-year-old Romy Isabelle Goff spotted her father, Jared Goff , on the practice field afterward, she immediately threw herself into his arms.

 Goff then introduced his daughter to teammates and coaches in between chasing her around.

 

 Romy, who was born in early July 2025, was too young to regularly attend training camp with her dad last summer. But this season, she and Goff's wife, Christen, were a consistent presence on the practice fields as the Goff family would often spend quality time together once training concluded.

 As Goff plays his 11th season, and the Lions' Thursday night game against the  Buffalo Bills  (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video), he and others around him have seen a different mindset from the 31-year-old quarterback. Romy's presence in his life has sharpened his focus and supercharged a sense of urgency that was instilled in him by his father, Jerry, a former MLB catcher.

 From the start of the Lions' offseason workout dates, teammate Penei Sewell said he could sense a different vibe from Goff, and head coach Dan Campbell said he noticed a heightened sense of urgency.

 "I think it absolutely transitions to the field," Christen said. "I think having perspective and having [an] understanding that there's more [to] life than football really helps you even focus in more on football and what you're doing there because it takes that pressure off that this is your whole life. Like, there's so much more to life.

 "So he can really, when he's at work, he can focus -- he can put in his time, he can put in his energy and to know when he's at home that nothing's going to change. He has a wife and a baby that loves him, and it gives him the freedom to play more freely, I think, without the pressure of his full identity being wrapped up as the quarterback of the Detroit Lions."

 

 In Week 1, Goff helped the Lions get off to a 1-0 start with a 31-30 victory over the New Orleans Saints . He threw two touchdowns, including the game winner in overtime to Amon-Ra St. Brown, which extended his TD streak to 24 games -- a franchise record and the longest active streak in the league.

 After the victory, Christen posted Instagram photos of Romy roaming the sidelines of Ford Field before the game. She also posted a candid photo of Romy in the arms of her beaming father with the caption: "Sundays are back!"

 "Your goal is to win the whole thing, and you want your career to go a certain way, and you have aspirations and all these things, but I think she reminds me that there's more to it," Goff said of Romy. "And every time I finish up, getting able to see her and just [knowing] I get to go home to someone who doesn't care.

 "It makes things a lot lighter for sure."

 And Goff said the new perspective fatherhood has brought will translate to the field when it matters most.

 "[Fatherhood] gives you a little freedom. It does," Goff told ESPN. "And I felt like I was in a really good place prior to having her, but I think it just unlocks a new world that you can't really feel until that happens."

 

 

 JERRY GOFF UNDERSTOOD exactly what it took to excel in sports. He spent six years in the major leagues as a catcher between 1990 and 1996, playing for the Montreal Expos, Pittsburgh Pirates and Houston Astros.

 In the Goff home in Novato, California, Jerry instilled a sense of urgency in his son at a young age.

 "He'd be playing video games like every other kid. I said, 'Let's go out and hit,' for example. ... He would say, 'I'm playing video games,'" Jerry recalled. "And I would just tell him, 'You go play your video game and I'm going to support you there, but somebody else is getting better while you're doing that.'

 "And that was always my thought when I was training. If I'm not working, somebody else was working and then next thing you'd know, I'd get a tap on the shoulder, 'Hey dad, let's go hit.' He understood."

 

 Those lessons ultimately helped Jared finish his prep career with a 39-4 record over three varsity football seasons at Marin Catholic High School in Kentfield, California. He was the first quarterback in Cal history to start as a true freshman, then the No. 1 pick in the 2016 NFL draft by the Los Angeles Rams .

 "What I have been able to give him, which most dads can't, is the perspective -- when he was younger in particular -- of playing at the highest level," Jerry told ESPN. "And giving him the tools, and he took it and ran with it to know how to prepare for the highest level, and I mean like in work ethic.

 "I've always said, 'You can't be like the rest of the kids if you want to be the best player, you can't. You can't go to the beach on the weekends every time, you have to be different.' You have to be different if you want to pursue greatness."

 That pursuit of excellence has become a feature of Jared Goff's professional career. He was traded by the Rams to Detroit in winter 2021 for former Lions star Matthew Stafford just two seasons after leading L.A. to a Super Bowl berth. But Goff resurrected his career in Detroit, leading the Lions to four consecutive winning seasons while becoming one of the NFL's most accurate and efficient quarterbacks.

 The trade worked out for both teams as Stafford led the Rams to a victory in Super Bowl 56. Now entering Year 6 in Detroit, Goff's focus and standard to win has heightened.

 "With Jared, things change when the season starts," Jerry said. "It's a little bit of a switch that gets flipped in terms of his focus and attention to detail and just his demeanor. Similar to me when I played [professional baseball]. In the offseason, it's loose and all that, but once the season goes, he's a different cat. He's so locked in.

 "Yes, the baby is the focal point, love of his life with him and Christen, and I can see there being a sense of urgency a little bit. But there's always a sense of urgency for Jared. He's got one thing in mind, and we all know what that is and that's the ultimate goal."

 

 
 THE LIONS WILL need the best version of Goff if they hope to return to the postseason and potentially bring home a Super Bowl.

 According to ESPN Analytics, the Lions entered the year with a 40% chance to win the NFC North -- the best odds of any team in the division.

 

 And after the Week 1 win over the Saints, Goff reached 39,828 career passing yards, passing Eli Manning (39,755) for the eighth-most passing yards through 11 seasons in NFL history.

 But 2025 represented a slight step back for Goff. After Ben Johnson left as offensive coordinator to become head coach of the Chicago Bears , Goff posted his worst Total QBR (57.3) since his first season in Detroit (45.5 in 2021), when the Lions finished 3-10-1.

 Last season, Goff particularly struggled when pressured. He faced a pressure rate of 28.9%, his highest since his first two seasons with the Rams. He also was sacked a career-high 38 times. Doubts outside the Lions building have arisen about his ability to lead Detroit to a title.

 ESPN analyst and former Lions QB Dan Orlovsky said such questions being asked about Goff are a sign of how far he has come as a quarterback.

 "I think he's really started to get the national and public appreciation as a player," Orlovsky said. "Like, you hear guys talk about Jared Goff now and it's not just Lions, it's not just [St. Brown] and [ Jameson Williams ]. I think that gives you, whether we like to admit it or not, that just gives you that credibility and that belief.

 "And when your peers are talking about you, the way I feel like they've started to talk about Jared in the last year or two, I really think it has an impact."

 And Goff remains hungry for more. The heightened sense of urgency he has felt because of Romy's presence in his life has him drilling down even harder on every aspect of his…

title: Packers' No. 1 task after loss: Protect Jordan Love
summary: Green Bay's offensive line has to improve after Love was pressured relentlessly by Minnesota's defense Sunday.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- It wasn't just how many times Jordan Love got hit in the Green Bay Packers ' 39-22 loss to the Minnesota Vikings  on Sunday -- although even that number was more than originally believed -- it was how quickly the quarterback had defenders in his face.

 Ten times on Sunday, Love faced unblocked pressures -- the most of any quarterback in Week 1 and tied for the most in a game by any quarterback in the past five seasons, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

 Among the 28 quarterbacks to be sacked in Week 1, Love's average time before being sacked was the fourth fastest (3.59 seconds).

 "What's disappointing is we had a few protection busts that absolutely should not and cannot happen," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said.

 According to the official game statistics, the Vikings registered 15 hits on Love.

 When asked what he told the offense after Love was hit 15 times, offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich replied: "18 times actually."

 LaFleur and his staff have a long list of things to fix before their Week 2 game at the New York Jets  ( 1:00 p.m. ET, Fox ). The offensive line -- and the entire blocking operation -- is at the top of that list.

 

 Perhaps the most telling breakdown of the game came with a little more than 5 minutes left. The Packers had just fallen behind 25-22 after leading 22-10, but they still had a chance if they could put a drive together. Instead, Love was sacked on consecutive plays, losing the second one and giving the Vikings the ball at the Packers' 1-yard line, where they put the game away.

 On the first sack, Minnesota's Dallas Turner was unblocked off the left edge despite having two players -- right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele and tight end Mark Redman -- lined up across from him. Neither blocked him, with Redman essentially knocking Bako-Bewele out of the way.

 "Yeah, that was a bust," LaFleur said.

 "I mean I think that's the type of team they are, so in order to combat that you gotta communicate, be on the same page, focus in," Bako-Bewele said. "I think in the second half, there were some miscommunications here and there that got us beat."

 

 In some ways, it should not have been a major surprise that there were issues with the offensive line. It was a game of musical chairs throughout training camp. One day, guard Aaron Banks would practice a little. The next day, he wouldn't practice at all. He rarely took any 11-on-11 snaps because of a lingering knee issue from last season. It was much the same for Bako-Bewele, who had offseason knee surgery.

 Still, the Packers thought Banks would be ready for the season opener but when he was a late scratch at the end of the week, they had a decision to make. Based on the way they practiced for six weeks in camp, it seemingly would have been a choice between playing rookie Jager Burton in Banks' place or putting Anthony Belton at right guard and moving Jacob Monk to left tackle. The problem was that Belton, who started six games at right guard last season, took most of his reps at right tackle in camp because Bako-Bewele was limited.

 They did neither.

 Instead, Donovan Jennings got the call because he had been better of late in practice, Stenavich said.

 With or without Banks, who is looking more and more like a bad signing after Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst gave him a four-year, $77 million contract as a free agent in 2025, the Packers appear to be open to some personnel changes up front.

 "We're gonna keep working that this week [now that] Zach [is] kind of more situated at tackle," Stenavich said Tuesday. "So we're gonna kind of rotate a few guys and just see what our best combination is for sure."

 The Packers can sit back and say that no other team is likely to blitz as much as the Vikings did. It's defensive coordinator Brian Flores' M.O., and he lived up to it. According to NFL Next Gen stats, the Vikings blitzed Love on 78.3% of his dropbacks -- the fourth-highest rate in any game since at least 2018.

 

 The Packers handled it in the first half -- 189 passing yards and two touchdowns against the blitz -- but melted down in the second, when the Vikings sacked Love four times and picked him off once while blitzing.

 That doesn't mean the Jets, or anyone else on the Packers' schedule, will scrap their usual style in favor of the Flores formula, but it might make them throw in a few extra pressures.

 The Packers were last in pass block win rate for Week 1 at 9%, according to ESPN Analytics. The next-worst team, the Cardinals, were 22%. Jordan Morgan , making his first start at left tackle, ranked dead last among all Week 1 tackles in pass block win rate. Bako-Bewele was 47th. Among guards, Monk ranked 55th and Jennings 56th. Sean Ryan ranked last (32nd) among centers.

 "I think there's some things that we definitely have to get cleaned up that we'll certainly see, I'm sure, this week," LaFleur said. "But that would be a wholesale commitment to go to that style of defense, you don't see a whole bunch of that in the league."

title: Could David Montgomery be key to unlock Texans' offense?
summary: Houston scored its most points in a season opener since coach DeMeco Ryans took over.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Throughout training camp for the  Houston Texans , newly acquired running back  David Montgomery  was adamant about his all-around ability .

 In his debut Sunday, he backed his talk -- finishing with the most touchdowns (two rushing and one receiving) in a Texan debut in franchise history. 

 Houston fell short 36-31 to the  Buffalo Bills  to foil Montgomery's day, but he had 79 total yards (60 rushing and 19 receiving) as Houston scored the most points in a season opener under coach DeMeco Ryans in his four years.

 Houston had a need at running back, so they traded for Montgomery with the Detroit Lions in March. The offense finished with 124 rushing yards on 32 carries, which helped take pressure off quarterback  C.J. Stroud  and helped open up passing lanes en route to a 287-yard passing day. 

 

 "That's going to be our identity," Montgomery said. "[Offensive coordinator] Nick Caley believes in that. Coach Ryans believes in that also. Me, [ Woody Marks ] whenever we get the balls in our hands, we want to make it a point to take it personal to ensure that they can lean on us when they need us."

 Ryans felt good about the execution from Houston's offensive line combination of left tackle Aireontae Ersery , rookie left guard Keylan Rutledge , center Evan Brown , right guard Ed Ingram and right tackle Trent Brown .

 If the offensive line can consistently pave running lanes for Montgomery, that'll create the foundation Ryans wants: Physicality.

 "David doesn't do a great job without talking about the offensive line," Ryans said. "I thought those guys controlled the line of scrimmage really well, especially in those short-yardage, critical situations."

 From an advanced metrics standpoint, Montgomery's day where he averaged 3.0 yards per carry could have been more efficient all-around. He had a 35% success rate, which ranked 27th among running backs with at least 10 carries in Week 1 according to Next Gen Stats, and Houston's run block win rate was 74% (16th). So there's room to grow.

 

 Montgomery called their offensive output "OK" -- which speaks to them not being satisfied. But his individual performance added him to an active two-player list of having a multi-rushing touchdown game with three different franchises ( Detroit Lions , Chicago Bears and Houston) joining his former teammate in quarterback Justin Fields (Bears, Pittsburgh Steelers , New York Jets ).

 Houston brought in Montgomery with hopes that he could be a true bell cow for an offense that ranked 22nd in rushing yards per game (108.9) and 29th in yards per carry (3.9).

 "I would've loved to give David a game ball," Ryans said. "Very impressive game by him. Really encouraged with what he brings. Guy who can be an explosive runner, physical runner, he was able to get positive yards -- even when the run may have been blocked for zero [yards], he was able to get four and five yards on runs."

title: Colts' D looked lost vs. Ravens, and Patrick Mahomes is next
summary: Communication problems hurt the Colts vs. Lamar Jackson, and that likely piqued Patrick Mahomes' curiosity.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Quarterback Lamar Jackson casually broke the huddle and his Baltimore Ravens offense took its place in a tight, two-tight-end formation.

 Meanwhile, the  Indianapolis Colts ' defense across the line of scrimmage was in a state of chaos. Players were scrambling to get lined up, pointing, yelling. Confusion ruled.

 Jackson, likely taking notice, quickly called for the snap. He executed a hard play-action fake to running back Derrick Henry , then bootlegged to his left. Jackson found receiver Zay Flowers a couple of steps ahead of defender Justin Walley , hitting Flowers for a 49-yard gain that took the ball to the 2-yard line.

 Somewhere, Patrick Mahomes likely smiled.

 Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs host the Colts on Sunday night (8:20 ET, NBC), and it is not difficult to imagine Mahomes taking pleasure in seeing the Colts' many defensive miscues in Sunday's blowout loss to the Ravens. Indianapolis' defense looked lost, giving up its most total yards in nearly three seasons (506).

 Because, according to players, it was lost.

 "We're not getting the line right, being late to our alignments and just [not] executing the little details of the defense," defensive tackle DeForest Buckner said. "That was our biggest challenge."

 Embarrassing miscommunications that led to costly plays by Baltimore defined the Colts' 2026 debut, and it has left defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo to rectify things ahead of the team's Week 2 meeting with the crafty Mahomes.

 

 Among the things he'll be examining: Whether veteran safety Cam Bynum should continue to handle defensive communication, including wearing the helmet transmitter that allows Anarumo to share info with him from the sideline.

 The Colts are the rare team that has attempted to use a player other than a linebacker to handle sideline communication. Whether it was a good decision remains to be seen.

 "We make sure that it's certainly not just on Cam, but we've got to evaluate everything we do," Anarumo said, adding, "Cam did a phenomenal job for the first game, but I want to look at everything."

 The identity of the player wearing the helmet transmitter is not something fans typically obsess over, but the role is critical. Teams may designate one player to wear a helmet transmitter, denoted by the "green dot" on the helmet, to receive one-way communication from a coach. That is how Anarumo relays defensive calls and coverages to his unit, just as offensive coaches do with quarterbacks.

 In nearly all cases leaguewide, linebackers handle this responsibility because they are positioned in the middle of the defense. Rookie CJ Allen , the Colts' second-round pick, was projected to be the starting middle linebacker and was expected to wear the transmitter this season. But those plans fell through when Allen missed time with injuries in training camp and the preseason, leading coaches to determine he is not ready to be a starter. The Colts instead plan to use a rotation of linebackers, so it was not ideal to have one specific linebacker tasked with the job of sideline communication.

 So Anarumo turned to one of his trusted veterans instead. Bynum was caught off guard, to say the least.

 

 "I didn't even know defensive backs did that," Bynum said.

 But Bynum was up for the challenge. He now admits, however, that running the defensive huddle at the speed of a regular-season game proved challenging. Bynum is sometimes the deep safety in the Colts' system, meaning he has to travel a significant distance back to the huddle. Then, he oftentimes must return to the back end of the defense before the ball is snapped.

 "At the end of the day, communication has to be on point," Bynum said. "It's obviously my first time doing it, and I just want to make sure that everybody's always on the same page, and I have to take pride in being able to communicate and relay little messages."

 The Ravens made things even more challenging by using offensive tempo and snapping quickly on multiple occasions. It proved disastrous for the Colts. Anarumo said a majority of Baltimore's explosive plays were related to the Colts being misaligned or to communication issues.

 "You can never lose the explosive battle like we did," he said.

 But the problems could repeat themselves if the Colts aren't better prepared to deal with this issue in Week 2.

 "We were a little lackadaisical, man," cornerback Charvarius Ward said. "So, we can't allow that to happen again. It's, for sure, not the standard."

title: Njoku, Nwosu, Emmanwori, and more - 10 NFL players of Nigerian origin to watch this season
summary: The NFL has long had a significant African presence, but no country is represented quite like Nigeria.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is underway, and Nigerians will once again have plenty of reasons to pay attention, with players of Nigerian origin spread across the league, from defending Super Bowl champions to established starters, and former high draft picks looking for breakout seasons.

 The NFL has long had a significant African presence, but no country is represented quite like Nigeria. There are 137 players of African origin across NFL rosters and practice squads at the start of the 2026 season, representing 24 African countries, with Nigeria accounting for 93 of them, more than two-thirds of the total.

 Liberia is a distant second with nine players, followed by Côte d'Ivoire with seven, Cameroon with six and Ghana with five.

 Every NFL team has at least one player of African origin, while Nigerian representation stretches across 29 of the league's 32 teams. Only the Minnesota Vikings , New Orleans Saints and Arizona Cardinals do not have a player of Nigerian origin on their roster or practice squad.

 

 No team has more than the New York Jets . The Jets have eight players of Nigerian origin, including one on the practice squad, with Olu Fashanu , Joseph Ossai and Lagos-born veteran David Onyemata among the most recognizable.

 Those numbers help illustrate how dramatically Nigeria's footprint in American football has grown. The country's NFL connection is no longer represented by a handful of isolated success stories.

 Nigerian-born players and the children of Nigerian immigrants now occupy positions across the league, from quarterbacks and offensive linemen to linebackers, defensive backs and pass rushers.

 Some are already champions. Uchenna Nwosu and Nick Emmanwori helped the Seattle Seahawks win Super Bowl LX last season, while Moro Ojomo and Osa Odighizuwa enter this year on NFC teams with legitimate championship ambitions.

 Foye Oluokun remains one of the league's most productive linebackers, while former high draft picks Olu Fashanu and David Ojabo enter potentially important seasons in their development as potential breakout candidates.

 Jalen Milroe , whose playing time may be considerably more limited but whose position, Nigerian heritage and presence on the defending champions make his development particularly intriguing.

 Several others could have a significant say in who is still playing when Super Bowl LXI arrives in Los Angeles on Feb. 14.

 From the contenders to the challengers and potential breakout players, here are 10 NFL players of Nigerian origin to watch in 2026.

 

 SUPER BOWL CONTENDERS 
 Uchenna Nwosu, Edge, Seattle Seahawks 
 There is probably no better place to start than Nwosu. He is an established NFL veteran, a Super Bowl champion and a significant contributor on a Seattle team trying to win consecutive titles.

 Nwosu played 16 games last season and recorded seven sacks, his best total since registering 9.5 in 2022.

 He played 33 defensive snaps in Seattle's season-opening 13-10 victory over New England, finishing with five tackles and a pass defended as the Seahawks began their title defense by beating the team they defeated in Super Bowl LX.

 At 29, Nwosu is entering a stage where another strong season and another championship run would add considerably to an already successful NFL career.

 Why watch: An established Nigerian-American pass rusher playing significant snaps for the defending champions.

 Super Bowl chances : Excellent.

 Nick Emmanwori, Safety, Seattle Seahawks 
 Nwosu may be the established veteran, but Emmanwori could eventually become the bigger star. The young safety made an immediate impact as a rookie, finishing runner-up for AP Defensive Rookie of the Year and helping Seattle win the Super Bowl.

 At 6-foot-3, Emmanwori possesses unusual size and athleticism for a safety, allowing Seattle to deploy him in multiple roles rather than simply leaving him deep in the secondary.

 The challenge now is the second season. Opposing offenses have a full year of film on him, while expectations are considerably higher than when he arrived in the league. An offseason ankle problem also makes his health worth monitoring early in the season.

 If healthy, Emmanwori has an opportunity to establish himself among the league's emerging defensive stars.

 Why watch: He could make the jump from outstanding rookie to one of the NFL's better young defensive backs.

 Super Bowl chances: Excellent.

 

 Moro Ojomo, DT, Philadelphia Eagles 
 Ojomo has taken a very different route than usual to the NFL. Born in Lagos, he moved to California with his family when he was 8, eventually starred at Texas and was selected by the Philadelphia Eagles in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL draft.

 For players selected that late, simply sticking around is an achievement. Ojomo has done considerably more. He has developed into an increasingly important part of an Eagles defensive front featuring Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis , giving Philadelphia another source of interior pressure.

 That development makes 2026 particularly interesting. Ojomo has already gone from seventh-round project to legitimate NFL contributor. Another step Up the ladder could make him a much more recognizable name beyond Philadelphia.

 Why watch: One of the best development stories among Nigerian-born players in the NFL and now an important piece on a championship contender.

 Super Bowl chances: Very good.

 Osa Odighizuwa, DT, San Francisco 49ers 
 There are flashier names on this list, but few have been more dependable. Odighizuwa played all 17 games in each of his final four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys before moving to San Francisco, establishing himself as one of the league's more durable interior defensive linemen.

 Odighizuwa also comes from a football family. His older brother Owamagbe played in the NFL and now Osa arrives in San Francisco with an obvious assignment.

 The 49ers recorded an NFL-low 20 sacks last season and needed additional help for a defensive front that had lost some of its previous dominance. Odighizuwa provides an established interior presence alongside Nick Bosa .

 His first game suggested that the opportunity will be substantial this season. He started at defensive tackle and recorded two tackles as San Francisco's defense overwhelmed the Rams in a 27-7 season-opening victory in Melbourne. They limited the Rams to just seven points and 290 total yards, forced two turnovers, and limited Matthew Stafford to 155 passing yards

 With fellow starting tackle Alfred Collins lost for the season with a torn patellar tendon, Odighizuwa is now an even more important part of a 49ers defensive front attempting to return to its old standards.

 Why watch: Proven durability, substantial playing time and a new role on a team expecting to contend.

 Super Bowl chances: Very good.

 

 CHALLENGERS 
 Michael Onwenu, OL, New England Patriots 
 Onwenu already knows how close the Patriots came. New England's 2025 season carried them all the way to Super Bowl LX before Seattle ended the run with a 29-13 victory.

 Onwenu remains one of New England's most important offensive linemen and has provided valuable versatility throughout his career, playing both guard and tackle. His role becomes even more important with quarterback Drake Maye established as the centerpiece of the Patriots offense.

 Onwenu began 2026 where he left off, starting at right guard as New England's rebuilt offensive line allowed just two sacks against Seattle in its 13-10 opening-night loss.

 The Patriots still had problems dealing with Seattle's pressure, particularly late, but Onwenu remains the established presence on an offensive line charged with protecting Maye as New England attempts to return to the Super Bowl.

 Why watch: An established Nigerian-American starter protecting one of the AFC's leading young quarterbacks.

 Super Bowl chances: Very good.
